verdict.what_is_spun: UPL's India and international crop protection businesses, combined into a single listed pure-play crop protection platform
demerged_business_names: UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions Limited
verdict.reason: "Unlocking value for its shareholders by creation of an independent and focused crop protection platform"; two listed entities enable clearer value discovery, group simplification, independent capital raising and deleveraging
verdict.insiders: Promoters go 100% to 71.56% of UPL 2; UPL 2 Promoters (Shroff family, UPL Corp Mauritius, etc.) voluntarily locked for eighteen months from Listing Date; Mike Frank CEO of UPL Global
verdict.hidden_value: The spin holds the bulk of earnings: UPL Cayman turnover USD 4,187 Mn vs UPL 1's INR 53,313 Mn, demerged India undertaking 31.15% of turnover; "world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform", 140+ countries. Parent keeps diversified residual; scheme drives deleveraging
verdict.selling_pressure_why: 1 for every 1 entitlement puts UPL 2 shares with every UPL holder at a fresh listing; promoter lock-in leaves only 28.44% public float
verdict.listing_timeline: Press release dated February 20, 2026: "The transaction is expected to be completed within 12–15 months, subject to the timely receipt of regulatory and other required approvals"; BSE "no adverse observations" and NSE "No Objection" letters dated July 29, 2026; "Subsequently, UPL 2 will be listed on Indian stock exchanges pursuant to the Scheme"
verdict.read_next: Scheme/abridged prospectus for UPL 2: assets and liabilities transferred, debt allocation, and 3-year revenue, EBITDA, PAT
verdict.quote: Bringing our crop protection businesses under one platform creates the world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform.

verdict.what_is_spun: The Graphite Undertaking — graphite electrodes business plus overseas investment and TAWA power plant assets/liabilities
demerged_business_names: HEG Limited (formerly known as HEG Graphite Limited)
verdict.reason: not stated
verdict.insiders: Ravi Jhunjhunwala is Chairman, MD & CEO of HEG Limited (Resulting Company); son Riju Jhunjhunwala chairs HEGAM. Promoter stake in new entity not stated.
verdict.hidden_value: Graphite carried Rs 4,601.53 cr assets vs Rs 1,357.07 cr liabilities (June 30, 2026) and earned Rs 319.71 cr H1 FY27 PAT; parent keeps debt-free hydro with over Rs 300 cr annual cash flows and Rs 1,322.84 cr cash.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: 1 share issued to every HEGAM holder; shares still unlisted pending trading approval; graphite is a different industry from parent's advanced materials/power.
verdict.option_pricing_date: not stated (ESOP 2026 approved by Board November 3, 2026; pricing formula 'As per Scheme (as determined by Nomination and Remuneration Committee)')
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated as a date; in the October 30, 2026 letter: 'the equity shares of HEG Limited, the Resulting Company, ate presently unlisted, and the process of obtaining listing and trading approvals from the stock exchanges is underway'
verdict.read_next: HEG Limited's listing/trading approval intimation, and its standalone balance sheet borrowings of Rs 708.97 cr.
verdict.quote: Under the Scheme, the graphite electrodes business was transferred to HEG Limited (earlier known as HEG Graphite Limited), and Bhilwara Energy Limited was amalgamated into the Company.

verdict.what_is_spun: The Bio Pharma (Biopharma) Undertaking — bio-pharma and bio-polymers businesses, plant-based APIs, nutraceuticals and nicotine derivatives
demerged_business_names: Ennature Biopharma division of India Glycols Limited
Ennature Bio Pharma Private Limited (former name)
verdict.reason: "The demerger will result in the creation of three separate companies, each with a clear business focus," giving each dedicated management oversight and capital, investments and resources managed to its own business requirements.
verdict.insiders: Promoter family controls it: Pragya Bhartia Barwale Managing Director 5 years (ran the division to Rs 200 crore revenue); father U.S. Bhartia and sister Pooja Jhaver non-executive directors; promoters held 3,99,67,854 of 6,70,26,765 IGL shares, voted 100% in favour.
verdict.hidden_value: Tax cost apportionment assigns Ennature 20.61% of value on only ~2% of group revenue (FY26 segment revenue Rs 207.77 crore, EBIT Rs 7.23 crore, 3.5%, down from 20.76 crore EBIT in FY25), with segment assets Rs 426.42 crore versus liabilities Rs 92.49 crore — a depressed-margin, asset-heavy business management says is being rebuilt into branded nutraceuticals.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Smallest of three entities, only 2,23,42,255 shares on a 1-for-3 ratio creating odd lots; pharma/nutraceuticals unrelated to chemicals or spirits holders bought.
verdict.listing_timeline: Per EBPL's letter dated 2 November 2026: listing and trading approvals received from BSE and NSE on November 02, 2026 for 2,23,42,255 equity shares of Rs 5/- each, with "Date of Commencement of Trading: November 04, 2026"; earlier, the 1 September 2026 news release said only that "The management of Ennature Bio Pharma Limited will apply to BSE and NSE for listing of its shares on the respective bourses."
verdict.read_next: Ennature Bio Pharma's Information Memorandum (board-approved 8 September 2026) — standalone balance sheet, debt allocation and segment margin trend.
verdict.quote: Ennature Bio Pharma Limited will house the bio-pharma and bio-polymers businesses.

verdict.what_is_spun: Clinical Services undertaking of NH Integrated Care Pvt Ltd — 9 Bengaluru clinics and 1 Hosur clinic
verdict.reason: Merging the clinic business into NHL to share corporate resources and manage synergies and costs between two entities; clinics best reflect their contribution to the hospitals
verdict.insiders: No shares issued as consideration; no change in share capital or shareholding pattern. Largest individual shareholder (Mrs Shakunthala Shetty) holds 35.38%/34.80%. No ESOP scheme in operation.
verdict.hidden_value: Reveals a loss-making vertical absorbed upward, not released: integrated care cash burn ~INR 66 crore in FY26, with similar run-rate guided. HSBC charge on the Demerged Undertaking moves to NHL. Narayana Aarogyam Vertical stays inside NHIC.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: No shares issued, no new listing, no change in share capital or shareholding pattern of the listed company.
verdict.listing_timeline: No listing: the undertaking vests in already-listed NHL and "no shares shall be issued by the Company as consideration"; per the 4 November 2026 letter the Scheme "shall become effective on the last of the dates on which the certified copy of the Order is filed by the Demerged Company and the Company with the Registrar of Companies", with certified copy to be delivered within 30 days of the order dated 30.10.2026.
verdict.read_next: Annexure 1 to the 29.09.2026 reply: pre- and post-demerger assets and liabilities of the Demerged Undertaking.
verdict.quote: The Scheme provides for the demerger of the Clinical Services (as defined in the Scheme) undertaking of the Demerged Company, comprising 9 clinics located in Bengaluru and 1 clinic in Hosur, into the Company on a going-concern basis.

verdict.what_is_spun: Merchant Power Undertaking — Vedanta's merchant thermal power generation business (Athena, Meenakshi), demerged into Talwandi Sabo Power Limited
verdict.reason: Creation of five independent sector-specific pure-play companies, allowing each to chart its own growth trajectory and attract thematic investors; unlocking hidden value by enabling each business to be valued independently, with improved transparency
verdict.insiders: Each Resulting Company issued 1 share for every 1 Vedanta share, so promoter group (Vedanta Resources, 54.72% of VEDL as on June 30, 2026) carried over pro rata; promoters excluded from VEDL ESOS/ESPP 2026
verdict.hidden_value: Separation reveals leverage: Vedanta Power's net debt/EBITDA 4.7x, highest of the five, though debt is mostly structural long-term PFC/REC with 7-10 year maturities; residual Vedanta sits at 0.30x with AA+/stable
verdict.selling_pressure_why: 1:1 shares pushed to every Vedanta holder; thermal power unrelated to parent's metals/mining mandate; most levered of the five entities
verdict.listing_timeline: On April 29, 2026: effective and record date set for May 1st, with shares of the resulting companies 'expected to list and commence trading by mid-June'; the July 30, 2026 presentation states '4 new entities listed on NSE & BSE on 15th June'
verdict.read_next: Vedanta Power Limited's own post-listing results and production release, plus Athena Unit 1 restart update and its PFC/REC debt maturity schedule
verdict.quote: The de-merger has been architected with precision on capital structure, aligning debt with earning strength and growth stage of each resulting company.

verdict.what_is_spun: GE Power India's boiler pressure parts manufacturing undertaking (Durgapur), demerged into and vesting in JSW Energy
demerged_business_names: GE Power India Limited (“GEPIL” or “Demerged Company”)
GE Power India's Boiler Manufacturing division
GE boiler manufacturing plant in Durgapur
verdict.reason: For JSW Energy: entry into boiler pressure parts manufacturing, vertical integration via a dedicated facility, less third-party dependency, operational synergies across thermal projects; for GEPIL: focus on retained business, unlock value.
verdict.insiders: JSW promoter group 66.53% pre, 66.36% post; voting results state promoter group “not interested in the agenda/resolution”; promoters separately infused Rs 3,000 crore (JTPM Metal Traders shares locked in to 09-Sep-2027).
verdict.hidden_value: Ready-to-use boiler plant (1.1 GW nameplate, expandable to ~1.6 GW) de-risks BTG supply for a 10.7 GW secured thermal pipeline, for only ~48.4 lakh new shares; offset by heavy leverage — net debt/EBITDA 4.95x.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Only 48,36,509 new JSW shares (~0.26%); documents say “only a nominal dilution”; GEPIL holders get tiny odd-lot stakes.
verdict.listing_timeline: NCLT sanctioned the Scheme 1 October 2026; certified copy received 13 October 2026; letter dated 14 October 2026: “The Company will intimate the Effective Date and the Record Date to the stock exchanges in due course”; per the 18 June 2026 explanatory statement, “After the effectiveness of the Scheme and subject to receipt of regulatory approvals, the equity shares issued as consideration pursuant to the Scheme, shall be listed on the stock exchanges.”
verdict.read_next: The promised Effective Date and Record Date intimation; then Annexure IV joint share entitlement ratio report dated 18 September 2025.
verdict.quote: Upon issuance of equity shares pursuant to the Scheme, there will only be a nominal dilution in the existing shareholding of the shareholders in the Company.

verdict.what_is_spun: Apollo's omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business, demerged into a separately listed company
demerged_business_names: omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business
verdict.reason: Value unlocking via separation and independent listing: sharper strategic focus, operational flexibility, enhanced capital allocation, clearer investor visibility, plus consolidation of pharmacy distribution and a wider capital base
verdict.insiders: Promoter group held 4,02,87,130 shares (voted 100% for). Shobana Kamineni to be Executive Chairperson of Resultant Company; Rasmeli-funded upside share agreement (max 9% of upside at 4x MOIC) to her and identified employees; new ESOP to be established
verdict.hidden_value: A pharmacy/digital platform at ~INR 25,000 crore run-rate revenue with 6.5-7% targeted EBITDA margin, digital losses near breakeven, Keimed distribution consolidated; promoter and investor incentives concentrated in the spin, not the hospital parent
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Shares distributed to all 1.75 lakh AHEL holders in a different industry (pharmacy distribution/digital health) than the hospital parent they own
verdict.listing_timeline: On May 21, 2026 management said the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting was called for June 24 and they were "hopeful the demerger process is completed by Q4 FY27 as planned earlier," with "end of December or early Q4 FY27" when Apollo Healthtech should get demerged and listed; NSE's December 23, 2025 observation letter requires trading to commence within sixty days of receipt of the NCLT order
verdict.read_next: The Scheme's Demerger Share Entitlement Ratio and the Part E abridged-prospectus disclosures for Apollo Healthtech
verdict.quote: During the year, we also announced a strategic restructuring of the omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business, an important step towards sharpening focus on unlocking long-term value across our integrated health care platform.

verdict.what_is_spun: HUL's Ice Cream business undertaking, demerged into Kwality Wall's (India) Limited on a going-concern basis
verdict.reason: "Creation of a leading listed ice cream company in India with focused management having greater flexibility to deploy strategies suited to the Ice Cream businesses' distinctive operating model and market dynamics, to realise its full potential"
verdict.insiders: Promoter stake in KWIL not stated; HUL's own shareholding in KWIL was reduced and cancelled and KWIL ceased to be a subsidiary. KWIL has a dedicated management team (Chitrank Goel, Deputy MD; Prashant Premrajka, CFO) drawn from HUL.
verdict.hidden_value: Cost apportionment puts KWIL at only 1.91% of HUL's value versus 98.09%, set on net assets as at 30 November 2025 — a small, separately listed ice-cream pure-play, 2,34,95,91,262 shares of Re 1, with Kwality Wall's, Cornetto and Magnum.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Very small relative size (1.91% of pre-demerger cost basis) distributed 1:1 to every HUL holder; a separate ice-cream company versus a large FMCG parent.
verdict.listing_timeline: FAQ dated 29th November 2025: "the statutory timeline for the listing and commencement of trading of shares of KWIL is within a period of 60 days from the receipt of the certified copy of the order of the NCLT sanctioning the Scheme (in or around Q4 of FY26)"; filing dated 13th February 2026 confirms listing and trading approval received 12th February 2026 for 2,34,95,91,262 equity shares with "Date of Commencement of Trading: ... 16th February, 2026"
verdict.read_next: KWIL's first standalone results and balance sheet — the net assets behind the 1.91% cost apportionment.
verdict.quote: The Scheme has come into effect on 1st December , 2025, being the Effective Date (as defined under the Scheme ).

verdict.what_is_spun: The power transmission business undertaking: high-speed and niche low-speed gearboxes, gear internals, defence products, aftermarket and retro-fitment services
verdict.reason: Management stated the amalgamation of SSEL and the demerger of the Power Transmission business were "to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies" and to achieve an independent listing of TPTL.
verdict.insiders: Promoter family runs TPTL: Dhruv M. Sawhney Non-Executive Chairman, Tarun Sawhney Vice Chairman & Managing Director (five years, subject to shareholder approval), Nikhil Sawhney director; 3,13,00,000 shares locked in to Oct 2027/Oct 2029.
verdict.hidden_value: A high-margin engineering/defence business hidden inside a sugar-ethanol conglomerate: only 4.45% of TEIL turnover yet ~35-36% PBIT margins, order book just under Rs.500 crore (up 25%), Rs.340 crore capex, new defence facility, exports targeted above 50%; cost-of-acquisition split gives TPTL only 13.40%.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Small (13.40% of cost allocation), 1 share per 3 held; sugar/ethanol holders receive an unrelated engineering-defence company; 73,454,338 of 104,754,338 shares free.
verdict.listing_timeline: On 9 October 2026 TPTL informed TEIL that BSE and NSE approved listing and trading "with effect from October 12, 2026"; 10,47,54,338 shares of Re.2 each, ISIN INE2WKE01011. Earlier, on the 4 June 2026 call management said "by the end of August, we will have a listing of Triveni Power Transmission s Limited."
verdict.read_next: TPTL's first standalone quarterly results and balance sheet post-demerger: PBIT margin (~36%) and the sub-Rs.500 crore order book.
verdict.quote: Consequent upon the Scheme becoming effective, the power transmission business undertaking of the Company stood transferred to and vested into TPTL with effect from the Demerger Appointed Date i.e. April 1, 2026.

verdict.what_is_spun: not stated; filings describe amalgamation of ACC and Orient Cement into Ambuja, not a separation
verdict.reason: Same line of business; amalgamation lets Ambuja assume complete ownership, combining operations for focused growth, operational efficiencies, synergies, economies of scale and a simplified structure — the 'One Cement Platform'
verdict.insiders: Promoter/Promoter Group holds 1,672,081,052 shares, 67.33% of paid-up capital, voted 100% in favour; post-ACC-scheme promoter falls to 61.63%, public rises to 38.32%. Gautam Adani Chairman; Karan Adani non-executive director
verdict.hidden_value: No separation. Filings show the combined entity: debt-free, net worth Rs 72,238 Cr, AAA/A1+ rated, 113.5 MTPA, merger 'expected to be EPS accretive'; but Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 13.8% from 19.2%
verdict.selling_pressure_why: No demerger; merger issues 328 Ambuja shares per 100 ACC shares, lifting public shareholding 32.30%→38.32%; index effects not stated
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated — no entity lists; ACC and Orient shares are cancelled. October 29, 2026: 'Subject to requisite regulatory, statutory and NCLT approvals, completion is expected in FY'27.'
verdict.read_next: NCLT final sanction orders for the ACC and Orient schemes, and the December 22, 2025 joint valuation report behind 328:100
verdict.quote: The amalgamations are expected to simplify the corporate structure, unlock operating synergies and support long-term stakeholder value.

verdict.what_is_spun: Automotive Undertaking of Asia Investments: drivetrain/EV transmissions, BIW-NVH, synchroniser rings, forgings, brake fluids, coolants, DEF, adhesives
demerged_business_names: Anchemco India Private Limited (formerly Andasia Private Limited)
Anand CY Myutec Automotive Private Limited
verdict.reason: Reposition Gabriel from a mono-product suspension company into a diversified, technology-driven mobility solutions provider; rationalise corporate structure, reduce shareholding tiers, eliminate intra-group transactions, create EPS accretion
verdict.insiders: Promoter AIPL held 42.67%; AIPL's shareholders got 3,35,86,081 Gabriel shares (1158 per 1000); later preferential issue at Rs 1,305.89 raised AIPL to ~46.98%. Gabriel is ANAND Group's growth vehicle
verdict.hidden_value: Restatement shows the undertaking's earnings power: FY26 consolidated EPS Rs 24.22 after Scheme vs Rs 17.55 before; adds Dana, Henkel, ACYM equity income (Rs 1,576mn FY26) and Anchemco revenue Rs 3,512.88mn
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Shares went to AIPL's own (promoter-family) shareholders of an unlisted holding company; documents mention no index exclusion or industry mismatch
verdict.listing_timeline: On June 9, 2026 the company said the 3,35,86,081 shares allotted "are proposed to be listed and traded on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited"; Scheme effective May 22, 2026, appointed date April 1, 2026
verdict.read_next: Restated FY26 note 1 and the Rs 22,310mn HL Mando Anand related-party acquisition valuation report
verdict.quote: The Scheme is designed to strategically reposition the Third Applicant Company as a diversified mobility solutions provider by rationalizing the corporate structure and, in the process, enhance stakeholder value.

verdict.what_is_spun: The Power Evacuation Business (substation/evacuation infrastructure undertaking) of Inox Green, transferred into Inox Renewable Solutions Limited
demerged_business_names: Resco Global Wind Services Private Limited
verdict.reason: Segregation of distinct verticals with separate risks, rewards and investors; consolidation of power evacuation into IRSL "will result in unlocking value"; establish IGESL as a pure-play O&M player; two focused listed entities.
verdict.insiders: Inox Wind Limited, Holding Company and Promoter, "directly holds 51.13% of the equity share capital" of Inox Green; IRSL shares allotted pro rata to all eligible shareholders. No new-entity option or incentive plan stated.
verdict.hidden_value: Parent shed ~Rs 1,000 crore gross block and Rs 50-55 crore annual depreciation, lifting ROE/ROCE; O&M runs ~50% EBITDA margins with a Rs 700 crore tax shield. IRSL carries listed NCDs, Rs 235.78 crore secured plus Rs 556.10 crore unsecured debt, large tax losses and a Rs 96.80 crore tax demand.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Only 122 IRSL shares per 1,000 held (4,89,82,030 shares total); different industry — EPC/power evacuation versus pure-play O&M.
verdict.listing_timeline: On 24th August 2026: "IRSL is taking necessary steps for crediting the aforesaid equity shares to the respective demat accounts... and for obtaining the listing and trading approvals for the said equity shares from the Stock Exchanges." On 13th February 2026 call: "Post receiving of the NCLT approval, it is 1 to 1-1/2 month process for the listing of the company... within 3-odd months, 2-3 months, it should get on the process." On 29th May 2026 call: "IRSL will be automatically listed on the stock exchange post receipt of all the approvals."
verdict.read_next: IRSL's first standalone results: debt, the Rs 96,80,78,940 AY2023-24 tax demand and accumulated losses it carries.
verdict.quote: 122 equity shares of IRSL (face value Rs. 10/- each) shall be issued for every 1,000 equity shares (face value Rs. 10/- each) held in Inox Green Energy Services Limited.

verdict.what_is_spun: The NBFC Business (retail mortgage lending: home loans and LAP) of Sammaan Finserve, transferred to listed parent Sammaan Capital
verdict.reason: RBI directed that no other group entity hold an NBFC-ICC/HFC licence; to comply, SFL's NBFC Business is consolidated into SCL, leaving SFL to enter insurance broking/insurtech.
verdict.insiders: No shares allotted as consideration (SFL is wholly owned). Directors' only material interest: Naveen Uppal holds 678 and Rajiv Gandhi 2,50,000 fully paid-up SCL shares.
verdict.hidden_value: Not a value-releasing spin: assets move up into the listed parent, widening SCL's capital and asset base. The stated residual is SFL's unlisted 'independent fintech structure' planning insurance broking/insurtech, retained by SCL.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: No equity consideration issued and no new listed entity; only a 1:1 NCD exchange from SFL to SCL.
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated
verdict.read_next: Valuation Report dated 31.12.2025 by Transaction Square Advisory (Annexure A-14) for the Demerged Undertaking's assets and liabilities.
verdict.quote: The Demerged Company is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Resulting Company.

verdict.what_is_spun: TCIL's resorts and resort management business (Nature Trails brand) demerged into Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited
verdict.reason: Unlock value by separating resorts into SHRL, which has hospitality expertise; attract differentiated investor cohorts; sharper strategic focus; streamline TCIL capital structure improving EPS; subsequently list SHRL
verdict.insiders: Promoter Fairbridge Capital (Mauritius)/Fairfax holds 63.83% of TCIL; SHRL post-scheme promoters 65.55% (incl. 7% held by TCIL), ESOP Trust 2.16%, public 32.30%; 65,70,000 ESOP 2024 options accelerated
verdict.hidden_value: Resort undertaking demerged is tiny — INR 70 crore turnover, ~0.4% of TCIL standalone revenue — but recipient SHRL is a 78-resort, ~3,800-room, debt-free hospitality platform with INR 5,487mn FY26 revenue, 31% EBITDA margin, INR 3,400mn cash, 25 straight profitable quarters
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Documents state no change in TCIL shareholding pattern and similar promoter/public patterns post-demerger; no index or size discussion stated
verdict.listing_timeline: On March 20, 2026 filings: "Shares of SHRL will be listed on BSE and NSE" and listing "is proposed" subject to approvals; NSE letter dated September 1, 2026 requires SHRL to complete listing and commence trading "within sixty days of receipt of the order of the NCLT"; on the May 13, 2026 call Debasis Nandy said it will take "12 to 15 months" and "We expect this process to get completed by Q1 of FY '28"
verdict.read_next: Scheme explanatory statement: SHRL post-demerger balance sheet, valuation report and share entitlement basis
verdict.quote: Accordingly, the Board of TCIL is of the view that for better focus and maximum result, it is better to divest the Resorts and Resort Management Business into SHRL and subsequently list SHRL.

verdict.what_is_spun: Green Mobility Business Undertaking — cleaner-fuel/EV passenger transport fleet business, run via wholly owned subsidiary Refex Green Mobility Limited
demerged_business_names: Refex Green Mobility Limited (RGML, Transferor Company)
Refex EV Fleet Services Private Limited
verdict.reason: Risk, competition, financial profiles and return ratios of Ash & Coal handling are distinct from Green Mobility, which attracts a different set of investors, lenders and partners; separate listing to unlock value
verdict.insiders: Promoter and promoter group 56.57% of RIL mirrors into RML at 1:1; directors/KMP have no interest except directorship and shareholding; promoters' 1,11,70,000 warrants lapsed, Rs.130.69 crore forfeited
verdict.hidden_value: Spin is small and loss-making: green mobility segment EBIT -Rs.3,823.51 lakh FY26, -Rs.1,360.79 lakh Q1FY27, ~Rs.100 crore revenue in three years, RGML carries Rs.64.92 cr secured and Rs.88.41 cr unsecured creditors; parent left as high-margin Ash & Coal
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Tiny loss-making unit, ~3-4% of segment revenue, unrelated mobility industry versus ash/coal and wind; newly listed, no index membership
verdict.listing_timeline: Not dated. Aug 5, 2026 proceedings: RML shares "upon issuance pursuant to the Scheme, were proposed to be listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited"; NSE letter of March 16, 2026 requires trading to commence "within sixty days of receipt of the order of the Hon'ble High Court/NCLT"; on Oct 28, 2026 the demerger was still "awaiting final approval from the Hon'ble NCLT", next hearing 28 October 2026; on May 27, 2026 management said "another 60 to 75 days, this should get completed"
verdict.read_next: NCLT final sanction order and RoC filing date (Effective Date), plus Annexure 16B abridged prospectus and Annexure 19 net assets of RML
verdict.quote: The nature of risk and competition, financial profiles and return ratios involved in the Ash & Coal handling business of RIL are distinct from Green Mobility Business presently undertaken through its wholly owned subsidiary RGML.

verdict.what_is_spun: REL's financial services business — lending, broking, investment activities and ancillary support services — transferred to Religare Finvest Limited
demerged_business_names: Religare Housing Development Finance Corporation Limited (RHDFCL)
verdict.reason: Growth needs differentiated strategy; business is distinct and attracts different investors, lenders and partners; focused management, targeted regulatory compliance and risk frameworks; separate listing to unlock value for REL shareholders
verdict.insiders: Burman promoter group 30.56% as on June 04, 2026 (~34% post warrant conversion); subscribed ₹750 crore of ₹1,500 crore warrants; RFL shareholding will mirror REL's 1:1
verdict.hidden_value: RFL is debt-free with ₹898.8 crore net worth, 261.9% CRAR and ~₹591 crore cash, yet the demerged undertaking was only 6.2% of FY25 consolidated turnover; REL retains Care Health, where management says the value is
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Small (6.2% of FY25 turnover), issued 1:1 to every REL holder, and documents say it suits a different set of investors
verdict.listing_timeline: On February 14, 2026: "The company endeavours to complete the process and list RFL in Q1 of FY28"; Feb 16, 2026 call: process to take 15 to 18 months, culminating in Q1 FY28; NSE letter of July 07, 2026 requires listing and trading within sixty days of the NCLT order; as of August 7, 2026 RBI had not acceded to the no-objection request
verdict.read_next: The next intimation on RBI no-objection after its August 6, 2026 refusal — the scheme's gating approval
verdict.quote: The Company has received a letter dated August 6, 2026, from the RBI, conveying that the application has been examined and that the request has not been acceded to.

verdict.what_is_spun: Astral's Chemicals/Adhesive Business — adhesives, sealants, construction chemicals — merged into paints-and-coatings subsidiary Astral Chemie
verdict.reason: Dedicated leadership and sector expertise, independent capital allocation, consolidation with paints and coatings under one chemicals platform, unlocking shareholder value and eliminating conglomerate discount
verdict.insiders: Promoters and Promoter Group hold 54.22% of Resulting Company post-Scheme (mirroring parent), public 45.78%; MD Sandeep Engineer champions it. No incentive terms stated.
verdict.hidden_value: Reveals a chemicals/specialty platform (₹12,663mn turnover, 21% of Astral's ₹59,076mn standalone) combined with the paints and coatings subsidiary, which management says markets currently value at a conglomerate discount.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Resulting entity is small (21% of turnover), a different industry (chemicals/paints vs plumbing), and newly listed to all holders 1:1.
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated — on June 25, 2026 the documents say only "Upon the effectiveness of the Scheme and subject to receipt of regulatory approvals, the New Shares will be listed on the Stock Exchanges" (NSE and BSE), pending NCLT Ahmedabad, SEBI, exchange, shareholder and creditor approvals
verdict.read_next: The Scheme's definition of Chemicals Business and the demerged undertaking's profit, net worth and debt allocation — not disclosed here.
verdict.quote: The Scheme eliminates any conglomerate discount and allows the capital markets to distinctively value each independent vertical.

verdict.what_is_spun: Nothing is separated; the Scheme is an amalgamation of Go Digit Infoworks Services Private Limited into Go Digit General Insurance Limited
demerged_business_names: Go Digit Infoworks Services Private Limited (First Applicant Company / Transferor Company)
Go Digit General Insurance Limited (Second Applicant Company / Transferee Company)
verdict.reason: not stated
verdict.insiders: not stated; documents only list Annexure H1/H2 'pre and post scheme shareholding pattern (including Promoter and Promoter Group)' without figures
verdict.hidden_value: not stated; documents reference a Share Exchange Ratio valuation report by RBSA Valuation Advisors LLP dated 19th December 2025 and E&Y fairness opinion, but no values are given in the text
verdict.selling_pressure_why: not stated; no shareholding sizes, index treatment or new listing disclosed in the documents
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated
verdict.read_next: Annexure C valuation report (Share Exchange Ratio) and Annexure H1/H2 pre and post scheme shareholding pattern
verdict.quote: The Scheme, if approved by the equity shareholders, will be subject to the subsequent approval of the Hon’ble Tribunal and such other approvals, permissions and sanctions of regulatory or other authorities, as may be necessary.

verdict.what_is_spun: Not stated; documents name only an undertaking demerged from Kitex Childrenswear Limited into Kitex Garments Limited
verdict.reason: not stated

verdict.what_is_spun: Space, Meteorology and Hydrology business of Astra Microwave, demerged into Astra Space Technologies Private Limited
verdict.reason: Strategic re-alignment to create two sector-focused listed entities; distinct industry characteristics, differentiated growth strategy, focused management attention, and unlocking value of the Demerged Undertaking for shareholders
verdict.insiders: Promoters hold 100% of ASTPL pre-scheme, 6.45% post-scheme (mirror of AMPL). MD S. Gurunatha Reddy resigned from AMPL w.e.f. 30 September 2026 to oversee the demerger and join ASTPL as a Director; CFO Rahul Rungta moved to ASTPL as CFO; MD/WTD bonus criteria include 10% weightage for "Other intiatives of corporate restructuring like merger/demerger"
verdict.hidden_value: Separation reveals a scaled-up, profitable, high-growth space/weather business: INR 157 crores FY26 turnover (13.58% of total), ~16% of FY26 revenue, cumulative INR 750 crore ISRO orders plus INR 250 crore to FY28, meteorology INR 330 crore executed with INR 285 crore order book to FY28; margins described as better than defence
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Small relative to parent (13.58% of turnover, stated 10.6% of EBITDA), mirror-shareholding spin of a distinct sector with no index membership
verdict.listing_timeline: Press release 27 February 2026: "The Company aims to complete the demerger and list ASTPL by Q1 of FY28, subject to the timely receipt of all approvals." NSE letter 29 October 2026 requires steps for listing completed and trading commenced within sixty days of receipt of the NCLT order
verdict.read_next: The Scheme of Arrangement and valuation/share entitlement report, plus ASTPL's abridged-prospectus financials in the shareholder notice
verdict.quote: The Space, Meteorology and Hydrology business operates in a sector with distinct industry characteristics, competitive dynamics, regulatory environment, and risk profile, necessitating a differentiated growth strategy aligned with its specific market opportunities.

verdict.rationale: Management presented this as a two-part move announced on 20 March 2026: TCIL demerges its own Resorts and Resort Management undertaking — the six resorts it owns/operates directly under the Nature Trails brand (adventure holidays, educational trips, corporate getaways), with turnover of only INR 70 crore for the year ended 31 December 2025, about 0.4% of TCIL's standalone turnover — into Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited (SHRL), its wholly owned hospitality subsidiary, which is then listed on BSE and NSE. The boards' first reason is capability fit: the resort business 'would reap more benefit from being owned and operated by SHRL in light of their vast expertise in the hospitality industry' (SHRL had 72+ resorts across 62 locations at announcement, 78 resorts/~3,800 rooms/65 destinations by FY26). The second is that SHRL has 'matured' and is 'well poised to chart its own growth path' as a separate listed entity — FY26 revenue INR 5,487mn, EBITDA INR 1,701mn (31% margin), PBT INR 1,142mn (21%), 25 consecutive profitable quarters, ~INR 3,400mn cash at a 55% multi-year CAGR, debt-free, targeting 95 resorts and 4,500 rooms in 2027. The third is investor-facing: unlock value, 'attract differentiated investor cohorts for each business segment', and let two listed entities pursue growth aligned to their own industry dynamics with improved operational efficiency and profitability, while TCIL concentrates on core Travel and Financial Services (FY26 group income INR 83,982mn, EBT INR 3,268mn, down 14% on the Pahalgam/Operation Sindoor and US-Israel-Iran disruptions). Riding along are three capital-structure fixes: consolidation of four Re.1 shares into one Rs.4 share to improve key financial ratios and better reflect intrinsic value; a reduction of face value from Rs.4 to Rs.3 with no payout to 'right size the balance sheet' and improve EPS; and absorption of three dormant subsidiaries (TC Visa Services, Jardin Travel Solutions, Borderless Travel Services) that incur 'unnecessary compliance and administrative costs'. Consideration is non-cash: 81 SHRL shares of Rs.10 for every 100 TCIL shares of Re.1; TCIL keeps its existing SHRL shares (~7%); SHRL's post-scheme pattern mirrors TCIL's (promoters 65.55%, public 32.30%, ESOP trust 2.16%). The documented originators are internal — the Audit Committee and the Independent Directors Committee recommended it to the Board; no investor, lender, franchise or JV partner is cited anywhere as having asked for it, and the capital-deployment questions analysts did press (Mukul Varma, Anil Shah, Meet Shah on the ~INR 780-800 crore net cash and dividends) were answered with 'no conversations' as late as February 2026.
verdict.evolution: Nothing in the Q4 FY25 call (14 May 2025) or Q1 FY26 call (1 August 2025) hints at a separation, though both lay the groundwork: TCIL had just absorbed the Nature Trails resorts business by slump sale in March 2025 for INR 522.5mn, and Vikram Lalvani declared Sterling's 'transformation is complete' and in a growth phase, debt-free with rising cash. The Q2 FY26 (14 November 2025) and Q3 FY26 (6 February 2026) calls still carry no mention — on 6 February 2026 Mahesh Iyer explicitly said there were no conversations on returning cash or acquisitions, six weeks before the Board acted. The Board gave in-principle approval on 20 March 2026 (Scheme, press release, and separate demerger/merger/consolidation/capital-reduction filings), and the first and only call discussion came on 13 May 2026, where Iyer called it a 'strategic divestment… significant strategic move', Lalvani confirmed 'the demerger process from Thomas Cook has also been initiated', and Debasis Nandy reaffirmed the original 12-15 month timeline with completion expected in Q1 FY28. Execution then ran ahead of the calls: BSE no-adverse-observation (31 August 2026), NSE no-objection (1 September 2026), and an NCLT Mumbai procedural order of 4 November 2026 admitting the application and directing meetings of TCIL's equity shareholders and unsecured creditors.

points.point: The Board acted on 20 March 2026 on recommendations from the Audit Committee and the Independent Directors Committee, approving demerger of the Resorts and Resort Management business into SHRL plus a capital restructuring of TCIL.
points.quote: Based on a recommendation by the audit committee and independent committee, the Board of Thomas Cook (India) Limited (TCIL) today gave an in-principle approval to a proposal for the demerger of the company's Resorts and Resort Management business into Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited (SHRL) and a subsequent capital restructuring of TCIL.

points.point: Stated objective one: unlock value for TCIL shareholders and let each business segment be owned by the investor base that suits it, with a future SHRL listing on BSE and NSE.
points.quote: Unlock value for the shareholders of TCIL by demerging the Resorts and Resort Management business into SHRL and to attract differentiated investor cohorts for each business segment

points.point: Capability argument: the six Nature Trails resorts TCIL runs directly belong with Sterling, whose hospitality expertise and scale (72+ resorts, 62 locations) make it the better operator.
points.quote: TCIL and SHRL's Management believes that the Resort Business of TCIL would reap more benefit from being owned and operated by SHRL in light of their vast expertise in the hospitality industry.

points.point: Maturity argument: Sterling is ready to be its own listed company in a fast-growing sector rather than a subsidiary line item.
points.quote: Further, SHRL's Management is of the view that SHRL has matured over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity in the fast-growing hospitality industry.

points.point: Focus argument: segregate verticals so two listed entities can each chase growth on their own industry dynamics, improving operating efficiency and profitability.
points.quote: The main objective of the proposed restructuring, by way of a composite scheme, is to re-organize and segregate the different business verticals and focus on core businesses, in compliance with relevant regulations.

points.point: Scale of what leaves TCIL is tiny — the demerged undertaking is roughly 0.4% of standalone turnover, so this is a listing/value-unlock move, not a disposal of earnings.
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the year ended 31st December 2025 was INR 70 Crores representing ~0.4% of the total standalone turnover of the Company for the year ended 31st December 2025.

points.point: Consideration is all-paper: 81 SHRL shares of Rs.10 for every 100 TCIL shares of Re.1, no cash, with TCIL retaining its existing SHRL stake (~7%) and shareholding patterns mirrored.
points.quote: for every 100 (One Hundred only) equity shares of Thomas Cook (India) Limited of face value of INR 1/- each credited as fully paid up, the issue and allotment by Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited of 81 (Eighty One only) equity shares of Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited of face value of INR 10/-each credited as fully paid up

points.point: The share-capital reduction (Rs.4 to Rs.3 face value, no payment to shareholders) is justified purely as balance-sheet right-sizing and EPS improvement; the 4:1 consolidation is justified as improving key ratios and reflecting intrinsic value.
points.quote: The Management of TCIL believes that the proposed reduction of share capital is required to right size the balance sheet and capital structure of TCIL such that TCIL has a more efficient capital structure and the shareholders also benefit in terms of improved earnings per share.

points.point: Three dormant subsidiaries (TCVSL, JTSL, BTSL — FY25 turnover INR 1.2cr, nil, nil) are folded back into TCIL purely to kill compliance and administrative overhead; their shares stand cancelled with no issuance.
points.quote: TCVSL, JTSL and BTSL are dormant and non-operative companies, incurring unnecessary compliance and administrative costs.

points.point: Iyer's first call commentary on it: value unlock for shareholders, a streamlined TCIL capital structure, and resources refocused on Travel and Financial Services, with the face-value consolidation and dormant-subsidiary merger improving EPS.
points.quote: For Thomas Cook (India) Limited, this restructuring allows us to streamline our capital structure and concentrate our resources on our core Travel and Financial Services business.

points.point: Nandy, answering Ananya Khanna on timing, reaffirmed the 12-15 month Board timeline, NSE/BSE applications filed and queries being answered, with completion expected in Q1 FY28.
points.quote: We expect this process to get completed by Q1 of FY '28, which was the original timeline that we had intimated.

points.point: Lalvani tied Sterling's own readiness to the split: transformation behind it, record FY26 (revenue INR 5,487mn, 31% EBITDA margin, 21% PBT margin, 25 profitable quarters, ~INR 3,400mn cash, debt-free) and a brand re-architecture underway alongside the demerger.
points.quote: In parallel, as you are aware, the demerger process from Thomas Cook has also been initiated.

points.point: Six weeks before the announcement, management told investors asking about the ~INR 1,000 crore gross / INR 780 crore net cash that nothing was in train on shareholder payouts or M&A — no separation was flagged.
points.quote: But currently, there are no conversations around either any kind of disbursement of cash to shareholders or for that matter, any acquisition.

points.point: Precursor signal: Sterling's own management declared the turnaround finished and a growth phase begun, the premise later used to argue it can stand alone as a listed entity.
points.quote: So with this, we can clearly state that our transformation is complete, and now we are in a phase of growth.

points.point: A year earlier the resorts assets moved the other way — TCIL bought the Nature Trails resorts business (3 resorts near Bombay, 80-90 rooms, INR 10-15 crore revenue) from its step-down subsidiary by slump sale, the very undertaking now being demerged into Sterling.
points.quote: We completed this, the slump sale in March.

points.point: Regulatory progress since: BSE no-adverse-observation (31 Aug 2026), NSE no-objection (1 Sep 2026), and an NCLT Mumbai order of 4 November 2026 admitting the application and directing TCIL shareholder and unsecured-creditor meetings.
points.quote: The said order is procedural in nature, providing necessary directions and completing statutory formalities in connection with the proposed Scheme.

verdict.what_management_expects: TCIL: streamlined capital structure, resources concentrated on core Travel and Financial Services, improved EPS from the 4:1 consolidation, face-value reduction and dormant-subsidiary merger. Sterling: a separately listed hospitality pure-play charting its own growth path, holding 31-35% EBITDA margins, debt-free, scaling toward 95 resorts and 4,500 rooms. Both: differentiated investor cohorts, sharper focus, better operational efficiency and profitability.
verdict.gaps: No basis given for the 81:100 ratio or valuation, why face value drops to Rs.3, Sterling's standalone capital needs, tax effects, dis-synergies, or who initiated it.

verdict.segment_name: Leisure Hospitality & Resorts business (Sterling Holiday Resorts; labelled "Vacation ownership and resorts business" in some FY2024 revenue tables)
verdict.measure_notes: Operating profit = consolidated 'Segment result' (EBIT), i.e. segment profit before unallocated corporate expenditure, interest/finance costs, exceptional items and tax; quarterly presentations label the same line EBIT. Revenue is segment revenue from external customers (group-level segment disclosure; no inter-segment amount shown for this segment). Segment PAT is not disclosed. Note the standalone 'Leisure hospitality & resorts business' segment (₹92.2 mn FY2026) is only Thomas Cook Ltd's own small resort operation (Nature Trails, acquired 19 Mar 2025) — not the full demerged business; consolidated figures used.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is AHEL's omnichannel pharmacy and digital health vertical — Apollo HealthCo, comprising the ~7,500-store Apollo Pharmacy retail/front-end network and the Apollo 24/7 digital platform (46mn users, INR 528 cr quarterly platform GMV) — which is being demerged into Apollo Healthtech Ltd, with Apollo Healthco Ltd and the promoter-linked distributor Keimed Private Limited (which supplies ~60,000 pharmacy stores) amalgamated into the same vehicle, which is then renamed Apollo Healthco Limited and listed; hospital-based pharmacies stay inside Healthcare Services, since as A. Krishnan put it in Aug 2025, 'what we are spinning out is only the retail pharmacies and the online.' The Scheme's own rationale states the problem plainly: the Identified Business Undertaking is 'distinct from other businesses undertaken by the Demerged Company' and 'necessitates a differentiated strategy aligned to its industry specific risks, market dynamics, and growth trajectory', so separation lets hospitals and retail/digital each focus on 'their respective businesses, efficient management, and control', consolidates HealthCo's and Keimed's distribution 'in an independent company focusing exclusively on digital health and pharmacy distribution', and lets the new entity 'build a wider capital and financial base, by attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and stakeholders' — plus supply-chain integration, wider assortment, 'improved transparency in the supply chain preventing the entry of counterfeit or substandard medicines', administrative efficiency, board/managerial rationalisation and economies of scale. The financial case management repeated for six straight quarters is scale plus margin convergence: pro-forma combined revenue of INR 4,430 cr in Q1 FY26 (~INR 17,000 cr run-rate, INR 19,000 cr for FY26) becoming a INR 25,000 cr run-rate at 7% EBITDA by Q4 FY27; Sanjiv Gupta's arithmetic was that a 3.2% blended FY25 margin is already 6.4% once Apollo 24/7's losses and the accelerated ESOP charge are stripped out, with offline pharmacy going 7.4%→8-9% on private label (15.5% of pharmacy sales) and Keimed 3.1%→3.5%. The loss drag has in fact collapsed — digital cash losses fell from INR 111 cr (Q4 FY24) and INR 101 cr (Q2 FY25) to INR 29 cr in Q3 FY26 and INR 16 cr in Q4 FY26, with breakeven ex-ESOP guided to Q1 FY27 and including ESOP (~INR 50 cr FY27) by Q3 FY27 — and Apollo HealthCo crossed INR 10,000 cr of annual revenue in FY26, making it listable on its own. Keimed's merger was justified on concrete synergies: shared technology, data, people and product categories, cheaper dark stores (22 today) to push beyond the top six metros to the next ten cities, and private-label penetration across Keimed's franchise base. The push is not purely internal: Rasmeli Limited, the investor holding Class A/B compulsorily convertible preference shares in Apollo Healthco, receives a nominee director in the Resultant Company and signed a June 30, 2025 Upside Agreement sharing up to 9% of its own upside (only above 4x MOIC) with Ms. Shobana Kamineni — proposed Executive Chairperson — and identified employees; after shareholder and proxy-adviser pushback the Company issued clarifications on June 15 and June 19, 2026 adding 10% fall-away thresholds on nomination rights, tiered caps on promoter nominees, an individual 5% waiver, six independent directors and a Lead Independent Director. A second, separate separation was announced in May 2026: AHLL's Apollo Cradle and fertility verticals (INR 450 cr FY26 revenue, INR 45 cr IGAAP EBITDA) were combined with Cloudnine at INR 1,550 cr — 35x EBITDA — for cash plus a 9.9% stake, with the INR 750 cr of cash redeployed into primary care and diagnostics, which management called the funnel into Apollo.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced before this window as the 'strategic intent' for Apollo HealthCo (Aug 14, 2024 call) and was tracked through Feb 11, 2025 and the May 31, 2025 (Jun 2025) call purely as the Keimed merger 'progressing well', with a ~15-month timeline and Sanjiv Gupta's 3.2%→7% FY27 margin bridge; the composite Scheme itself was board-approved and filed on June 30, 2025. On the Aug 13, 2025 call management first spelled out the full shape — Apollo HealthCo as it stands gets demerged and separately listed by Q4 FY27, all steps within 18-21 months, only retail plus online moving out, Keimed folded in for technology/data/people/product synergies. Nov 7, 2025 and Feb 11, 2026 were process updates (statutory steps on track; CCI and SEBI approvals obtained, NSE no-objection Dec 23, 2025, NCLT filed and hearings begun, Keimed's subsidiaries consolidated to 100%), and the May 21, 2026 call set the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting for June 24, 2026 with completion still Q4 FY27. In the final stretch the plan changed on governance rather than structure: clarifications dated June 15 and June 19, 2026 added nomination-right fall-away thresholds in response to shareholder feedback, and on June 24, 2026 the Scheme passed with 90.44% of all votes and 85.71% of public votes in favour, but 14.31% of institutional votes against.

verdict.rationale: The supplied texts do not describe a separation, demerger or spin-off at all: the scheme filing is an amalgamation (absorption) of a subsidiary — the Transferor Company — into Ambuja Cements Ltd., the Transferee Company, and no business is being carved out. The stated starting point is ownership: the Transferee is already the promoter of the Transferor, holding 58.08% of its paid-up equity share capital (as on June 30, 2025) and 100% of its 8% non-convertible cumulative redeemable preference shares, and both are part of the Adani Group. Because 'both the companies are under the same line of business,' management argues the merger lets Ambuja 'absorb the business of Transferor Company completely for carrying on more effectively and beneficially.' The operating case given is integration economics: better resource utilization, reduced overheads, cost savings, economies of scale, elimination of duplicated efforts and streamlined compliance, plus 'reduction and rationalisation of multiple entities in the group.' The value case is stated only generically — enhanced business potential of the Transferor, value added to both companies and increased shareholders' value — with no margin, synergy-rupee or capacity figures in the rationale section. A second, distinct purpose is governance/shareholding: on effectiveness, certain Promoters/Promoter Group/related persons of the Transferor are to be reclassified from 'Promoter and Promoter Group' to 'Public' in the Transferee under SEBI LODR Regulation 31A, on the stated basis that they will not hold more than ten percent of total voting rights, exercise no direct or indirect control, hold no special rights or shareholder agreements, have no board seat or nominee director, are not KMP, and are neither wilful defaulters nor fugitive economic offenders. Process support is documented rather than argued: two valuation reports dated December 17, 2024 (BDO Valuation Advisory LLP for the Transferor; GT Valuation Advisors Private Limited for the Transferee) with fairness opinions from Vivro Financial Services (Transferor) and IDBI Capital Markets & Securities (Transferee), unanimous approval by both boards on December 17, 2024 (6 directors at the Transferor, 8 at the Transferee, including Gautam Adani as Chairman), NSE as Designated Stock Exchange, no-objection applications to the exchanges on January 3, 2025, and complaint reports to BSE (March 6, 2025) and NSE (March 25, 2025, updated June 16, 2025). Nothing in the texts attributes the transaction to a request from investors, lenders or partners.
verdict.evolution: The only tagged call material is February 2026 (transcript header: January 30, 2026), and it contains no mention of any separation, demerger or amalgamation — the Q&A with Rajesh Ravi of HDFC Securities covers clinker commissioning and prior-period tax refunds only, so no call-by-call evolution of the idea can be traced from these texts. The documented timeline comes entirely from the filing: audit committee, independent-directors committee, M&A committee and both boards acted on December 17, 2024 on valuation reports of the same date; exchange no-objection applications followed on January 3, 2025; complaint reports went to BSE on March 6, 2025 and NSE on March 25, 2025, with an updated NSE complaint report on June 16, 2025; share-capital data is stated as on August 31, 2025 and the 58.08% holding as on June 30, 2025. The only change visible across the sequence is procedural (exchange queries raised by NSE/BSE and addressed, and the updated complaint report), not a change in rationale or structure. On the one call, management's forward narrative is organic capacity expansion — four new 4 mt kilns plus a fifth line in Assam — rather than any portfolio separation.

points.point: The transaction is an amalgamation of a 58.08%-owned subsidiary into Ambuja (the Transferee is also the promoter of the Transferor and holds 100% of its 8% non-convertible cumulative redeemable preference shares), justified by the two companies being in the same line of business.
points.quote: As both the companies are under the same line of business, this amalgamation will enable the Transferee Company to absorb the business of Transferor Company completely for carrying on more effectively and beneficially.

points.point: The operating rationale is integration economics — consolidating operations for cheaper, simpler management.
points.quote: This includes better resource utilization, reduced overheads, cost savings, economies of scale, elimination of duplicated efforts, and streamlined compliance requirements through amalgamation.

points.point: A structural aim is cutting the number of group legal entities.
points.quote: The amalgamation will lead t o reduction and rationalisation of multiple entities in the group.

points.point: The value claim is stated only in general terms, without quantification.
points.quote: The amalgamation will enhanc e business potential of the Transferor Company, add value to both the companies, and ultimately increase the shareholders’ value.

points.point: A separate purpose is reclassifying certain Transferor promoters to 'Public' in Ambuja under SEBI LODR Regulation 31A, conditioned on a sub-10% voting stake, no control, no special rights, no board seat and no KMP role.
points.quote: Accordingly, reclassification of the Promoters/Persons belonging to the Promoter Group/Persons related to the Promoters Seeking Reclassification of the Transferor Company from ‘Promoter and Promoter Group’ category to ‘Public’ category in the Transferee Company has been contemplated upon the coming into effect of this Scheme, in accordance with the requirements of Regulation 31A of the Securities and Exchange

points.point: Independent valuation and fairness support was obtained on December 17, 2024, and both boards approved unanimously that day; the Transferee's board meeting was chaired by Gautam Adani with eight directors attending by video conference.
points.quote: None of the directors of the Transferee Company who attended the meeting voted against the Scheme.

points.point: Management's growth narrative on this call is organic clinker capex: four kilns of about 4 mt each — the three being commissioned over the next three to four months plus Mundra — totalling roughly 16 mt of clinker, which at a ~1.5x conversion implies about 24 mt of grinding capacity.
points.quote: So 4 million tons x 4 million tons, 16 million tons x ballpark 1.5 million tons.

points.point: A fifth 4 mt clinker line in Assam has been agreed with the state government (greenfield), alongside brownfield Mundra and Maratha and Penna due up in February, taking the programme to about 20 mt of clinker.
points.quote: by the way, Assam also, we have signed up -- we have entered into agreement with the government in terms of setting up another 1 line of 4 million tons in Assam, which is the fifth one, by the way.

points.point: Asked about below-EBITDA value unlocking at ACC and Ambuja, the CFO framed prior-period tax refunds as a working-capital and balance-sheet item, together with resolution of a substantial share of legal cases — not as part of any corporate restructuring.
points.quote: Tax refunds of the prior period, I think we have done a major efforts on that and unlocked the working capital.

verdict.what_management_expects: No separation benefits are claimed anywhere. For the amalgamation the filing expects Ambuja to absorb the subsidiary's business, run it more effectively, and gain better resource utilization, lower overheads, cost savings, scale economies, no duplicated effort and simpler compliance; fewer group entities; enhanced business potential, added value to both companies and higher shareholder value; plus promoter-to-public reclassification. No margin, capital or valuation numbers given.
verdict.gaps: No separation is discussed, named or quantified. The Transferor is never named here; no synergy, margin, capital-structure, tax or share-exchange-ratio figures; no investor, lender or partner request.

verdict.rationale: Astral Limited says it has grown into two distinct verticals — (a) Plumbing: pipes, fittings, water tanks, faucets and sanitaryware, and (b) Chemicals: adhesives, polyvinyl acetate (PVA), cyanoacrylates, solvent cements, silicone sealants, epoxy resins, construction chemicals, putties and allied products, further scaled into specialty chemicals through recent strategic acquisitions. The Board (approval dated June 25, 2026) adopted a Composite Scheme that (i) demerges the Chemicals/Chemical Undertaking of Astral Limited (the Demerged Company) on a going-concern basis into Astral Chemie Limited, formerly Astral Coatings Private Limited, a 100% subsidiary that already manufactures and supplies paints and coatings for residential, commercial and industrial end-users, and (ii) amalgamates Al-Aziz Plastics Private Limited, another 100% subsidiary making electrofusion fittings, compression fittings, saddles, electrical fittings and allied accessories for gas, water, electricity and solar distribution/transmission, into Astral Limited because it is complementary to the Plumbing Business. The size cited: the Demerged Undertaking's turnover for the year ended March 31, 2026 was ₹12,663 million, 21% of the Demerged Company's total turnover, against Astral Limited's standalone FY26 turnover of ₹59,076 million and net worth of ₹41,058 million; Al-Aziz was small at ₹373 million turnover and ₹215 million net worth. The stated problems it solves: each business has different products, customer segments, operating models, capital requirements, risk profiles and growth opportunities and operates under different macroeconomic environments, regulatory frameworks and market risks, so one corporate roof blurred focus — the demerger puts chemicals plus paints under a single dedicated platform run by a focused leadership team with deep sector-specific expertise, and isolates the operational, cyclical and compliance risks of each business. It is also framed as a capital-structure fix: each entity can independently determine capex, working capital, funding and investment strategy based on its own growth prospects, capital intensity, cash-flow profile and risk-return characteristics, and as separately listed entities both can independently access debt and equity capital and attract strategic and financial investors with different investment objectives. For Al-Aziz, the added reasons are integration of its manufacturing facilities, products and customer relationships with Plumbing, plus reduced legal and regulatory compliance burden and administrative costs. Mechanics are value-neutral to holders: no cash consideration, 1 equity share of Astral Chemie (₹1 face value) for every 1 Astral share (₹1 face value), a mirrored shareholding pattern (promoters 54.22%, public 45.78% post-Scheme versus 100% promoter-held pre-Scheme), Astral's existing shares in Astral Chemie cancelled, no change in Astral's own shareholding, and listing sought on NSE and BSE.
verdict.evolution: The reasoning cannot be traced call by call from the material supplied: the only earnings-call passage provided is [May 2025], and it is entirely about end-market sizing — PVC at about 4.5 million tons in fiscal 25, CPVC at roughly 2.5 lakh tons or about 5% of PVC, and fire-sprinkler pipes as the next leg of CPVC demand — with no mention of a demerger, of the chemicals vertical, or of Astral Coatings/Astral Chemie. The separation therefore appears in these texts only at the Board approval of the Composite Scheme on June 25, 2026, sized off FY26 (year ended March 31, 2026) financials, by which point Astral Coatings Private Limited had already been renamed Astral Chemie Limited and the chemicals portfolio had been expanded 'through recent strategic acquisitions' into specialty chemicals — the one hint of a build-up preceding the announcement. One drafting shift is visible inside the filing itself: the rationale annexure and disclosure tables describe the demerger of the 'Chemical Undertaking'/'Chemicals Business Undertaking', while the press-release text describes 'the demerger of its Adhesive Business', a narrower label for the same undertaking.

points.point: Management sized CPVC at about 2.5 lakh tonnes versus a roughly 4.5 million tonne PVC industry in fiscal 25 — about 5% — calling it a niche product today, confined mainly to hot-and-cold internal plumbing. Nothing in this passage touches the separation.

verdict.rationale: Management frames the separation as a strategic re-alignment of a company that had grown into two very different businesses: Radar Electronics, Electronic Warfare and Telemetry on one side, and Space, Meteorology and Hydrology on the other, the latter being carved into Astra Space Technologies Private Limited (ASTPL), a wholly owned subsidiary that will be listed separately while AMPL continues as a pure-play Defence and Aerospace company retaining its JVs (Astra Rafael Comsys) and other wholly owned subsidiaries. The stated objective is sharper strategic and operational focus, with dedicated management teams free to pursue sector-specific growth, plus enhanced governance and accountability, a simpler corporate structure, clearer investment propositions and a broader investor base. The Scheme filing is explicit that Space/Met/Hydrology 'operates in a sector with distinct industry characteristics, competitive dynamics, regulatory environment, and risk profile', so it needs a differentiated growth strategy and its own capital allocation, and that a standalone entity is better placed to attract investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders with sector-specific interests. The press release adds the capital angle bluntly: Space and Weather is a scaled-up, profitable, high-growth opportunity in satellite design/assembly and satellite data, but it is capital-intensive and execution-dependent, and the demerger 'creates the structural clarity to attract capital and talent at scale'. The numbers cited are modest but real: the demerged undertaking did roughly INR157 crores of FY26 turnover, 13.58% of AMPL's total (space plus meteorology was ~16% of FY26 revenue); cumulative ISRO orders of over INR750 crores across two decades with INR250 crores still to execute by FY28, and over INR330 crores of met/hydrology contracts with a INR285 crores book to FY28; at December 2025 the standalone order book of INR2,226 crores already contained INR249 crores of space and INR369 crores of metrology/hydrology. Consideration is a 1:1 share entitlement (one INR2 ASTPL share for every INR2 AMPL share), no cash, so ASTPL's shareholding mirrors AMPL's (promoters indicatively 6.45%, public 93.55%), with listing sought on BSE and NSE and completion targeted by Q1 FY28. Leadership was split to match: Managing Director S. Gurunatha Reddy stepped down on 30 September 2026 to oversee the demerger and join ASTPL as a Director, Dr M. V. Reddy became MD of AMPL from 1 October 2026, and CFO Rahul Rungta had already moved to ASTPL in February 2026. The texts name no investor, lender or partner as having demanded the split; it is presented throughout as board-initiated, with the benefit framed as 'unlocking the value of the Demerged Undertaking for the shareholders of the Demerged Company'.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaces obliquely as a valuation argument: on 14 Aug 2025 Atim Kabra says the separately incorporated space subsidiary is 'very, very valuable' given how thinly-revenued space peers are priced, and on 13 Nov 2025 he extrapolates space alone to near AMPL's whole market capitalisation while flagging heavy space investment and Astra SAT-1; on 13 Feb 2026 he turns to financing, saying the balance sheet must be 'creative' so blue-sky projects are not starved, and teases 'a few very interesting options'. Structurally it moves fast after that: CFO Rahul Rungta is shifted to ASTPL on 11-12 Feb 2026, the Board grants in-principle approval on 27 Feb 2026 with a same-day press release (revised the same day), and SGR announces it on the 27 May 2026 call. The Board approved the full Scheme of Arrangement on 10 June 2026 with the 1:1 ratio and the INR157 crores / 13.58% disclosure, SGR's exit as MD was confirmed on 10 Aug 2026 effective 30 Sep 2026, and BSE/NSE observation letters with no adverse observations/no objection arrived on 29 Oct 2026.

verdict.rationale: Management's stated reason is structural: Anant Raj Limited (ARL) today runs two unrelated verticals — a real estate and infrastructure business, and a data centre and cloud services business — and the Data Centre Business is currently split across two entities (ARL itself and its wholly owned subsidiary ARCPL), with assets, employees, investments and operations housed in both. The Composite Scheme therefore does two things in sequence: first amalgamates ARCPL into ARL (no shares issued, since ARCPL is a 100% subsidiary with 25,00,000 shares held by ARL), then demerges the consolidated Data Centre Business out of ARL into Ashok Cloud Private Limited (ACPL), whose business is described as data centre and co-location services, sovereign public cloud, AI-ready cloud infrastructure, DC & DR services, cloud migration and data backup. The problems management says this solves are: (a) a fragmented, intra-group ownership structure, which consolidation simplifies and lets intra-group arrangements be cancelled or rationalised; (b) the data centre business being valued inside a real estate company despite a 'distinct operating profile, growth trajectory, risk-return characteristics and funding requirements', which a separate listing is meant to fix through independent, market-driven recognition and valuation; (c) inability to raise sector-specific capital and pursue data-centre-specific strategic investments and partnerships while buried inside ARL; and (d) divided management attention, which the Scheme replaces with dedicated management focus and decision-making per vertical. The scale disclosure supports the 'hidden inside real estate' argument: for the year to March 31, 2026, the demerged undertaking's turnover is ₹145.90 crore against total turnover of ₹1,627.72 crore, i.e. 8.96% (computed after aggregating ARCPL and ARL post-merger). ARL shareholders are kept whole economically — 1 ACPL share of ₹2 face value for every ARL share of ₹2, giving them 49% directly while ARL retains 51%, so post-scheme ACPL is 79.14% promoter-held (ARL 51% plus ARL promoters 28.14%) and 20.86% public, and ARL's own shareholding pattern is unchanged at 57.42% promoter / 42.58% public across 35,98,76,930 shares. ACPL is to be listed on BSE and NSE via a Rule 19(7) exemption under the SEBI Scheme of Arrangement master circular dated June 20, 2023, with the Board approving on July 21, 2026 and NCLT approval sought under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013.
verdict.evolution: No evolution can be reconstructed from the material supplied: the 'CALL PASSAGES' section of the prompt was empty, so there are no earnings-call passages (and no call dates or labels) in the record. The only dated points available are the financial reference date of March 31, 2026 for the turnover split (₹145.90 crore of ₹1,627.72 crore) and the Board's approval of the Composite Scheme on July 21, 2026, announced the same day by press release as creating 'Two Focused Independent Listed Companies'. Within the filing itself the plan is already in final two-step form — ARCPL merged into ARL, then the Data Centre Business demerged into Ashok Cloud — with no earlier variant described.
