verdict.rationale: The "separation" at CELLO is one leg of a composite scheme of arrangement, not a listed spin-off: the Manufacturing Business of 55%-owned listed subsidiary Wim Plast Limited (WPL — plastic moulded furniture, extrusion sheets, air coolers, dustbins, industrial pallets and engineering moulds, plus an investment book) is demerged into Cello Consumer Products Private Limited (CCPPL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Cello World (CWL), while WPL's Remaining Business is amalgamated into CWL and WPL is dissolved without winding up (NCLT Ahmedabad order 14 May 2026; effective 27 May 2026; appointed date 1 April 2025). Management's stated reason is consolidation, not separation: Gaurav Rathod said on the Nov 2024 call there were "2 rationales" — first, "we do not see any point in running 2 separate listed entities as the business is not very different"; second, WPL has manufacturing facilities in several locations that can be shared with CWL's other plastic product lines, since furniture moulding is "very, very similar to our other plastic manufactured products." He added it "reduces our compliance while having it under Cello World," and that the economics were small because "Cello World owns about 55% of the company in any case. So it's only about 45% that is being acquired." The scheme filing lists three benefits: synergy of operations and economies of scale with the legal and regulatory compliances of both listed entities "unified and streamlined"; "consolidation of ownership interests in one listed company instead of two listed entities"; and a unified approach to customer engagement, distribution and supply-chain management. A related clean-up was the inter-company loan: WPL had lent CWL about INR100 crores at 8%, which CWL repaid out of QIP proceeds (QIP of INR738 crores, July 2024, with INR100.00 crores earmarked for "Repayment... of borrowings availed by the Company from one of the Subsidiaries, WimPlast Limited"), so WPL became a 100% subsidiary before merging. The business backdrop was a structurally slow segment: moulded furniture revenue fell 5.0% in FY26 to INR349.0 crores and 13.5% in Q4 FY26 to INR91.5 crores, polymer is "62% of the cost of molded furniture" so revenue tracks polymer prices with "no mitigation... possible," and management had long guided only "low single-digit number growth" for Wim Plast, with premiumisation and outdoor furniture the only margin lever. Consideration was 86 CWL shares of INR5 per 100 WPL shares of INR10 — 55 for the demerger (29,75,909 shares) plus 31 for the amalgamation (16,77,330 shares), 46,53,239 shares in total, i.e. the 0.86 swap ratio management quoted; valuation by KPMG Valuation Services LLP with a merchant-banker fairness opinion, both dated 12 Nov 2024, and NOCs from NSE (2 July 2025) and BSE (3 July 2025).
verdict.evolution: On the Aug 2024 call (13 Aug 2024) a merger was still only an intention tied to the QIP objects — management said "ideally... we would like both of them to be merged and once it is decided by both the boards" — and on the Nov 2024 call (13 Nov 2024) Gaurav confirmed the boards had just approved it (12 Nov 2024) and gave the two rationales, while rejecting an investor's counter-proposal to instead demerge CWL's three verticals into separate listed companies. The idea then went quiet through the Feb 2025 and May 2025 calls; by the Aug 2025 call (13 Aug 2025) it was "almost through," with SEBI permissions received and the 0.86 swap ratio confirmed by the CFO, and shareholders and unsecured creditors approved it on 6 Dec 2025 (equity shareholders: 201,355,406 votes for, 17 against). On the Feb 2026 call (16 Feb 2026) CFO Atul Parolia put the NCLT final hearing in the last week of February with closure in "2, 3 months" from the 1 April 2025 appointed date, and by the Jun 2026 call (29 May 2026) the merger was done, effective 27 May 2026, with FY25 comparatives and EPS restated.

points.point: Jay Doshi noted one stated purpose of the QIP was to enable consolidation/merger of Wim Plast; management said it was a management preference awaiting both boards' decision, with no timeline.
points.quote: In terms of WimPlast ideally, of course, from a management perspective we would like both of them to be merged and once it is decided by both the boards, I think we'll be able to go ahead on that as well.

points.point: Asked directly for the rationale of demerging Wim Plast and merging it into Cello, Gaurav Rathod gave two reasons: no point in two separate listed entities, and shareable multi-location plastic manufacturing capacity.
points.quote: there are 2 rationales, one is that there s - we do not see any point in running 2 separate listed entities as the business is not very different.

points.point: Second rationale was manufacturing sharing — Wim Plast's plants in different parts of the country could be used for CWL's other plastic product lines; compliance cost reduction and the fact that CWL already owned ~55% were also cited.
points.quote: Also, we would be able to use these facilitics as WimPlast has a lot of locations where if's manufacturing capacity is there. So we can use it for our other plastics product lines as well.

points.point: An investor (Deepesh Sancheti) argued the opposite case — that Cello should instead demerge its three unrelated verticals to unlock value, noting Wim Plast traded at 10-12x PE versus CWL at 60x; management refused, citing manufacturing synergy between furniture and other plastics.
points.quote: No, I think - I don't think we arc looking at that because ofherwise, we would have not merged this back into Cello World.

points.point: Management conceded a vertical-level separation would only make sense if one vertical outgrew the rest — explicitly naming glassware — because all categories are consumer-facing and sold to the same retailer.
points.quote: So, I guess, of course, if we say tomorrow, glassware becomes too big, then kind of it would probably make sense.

points.point: Scale and cost of the transaction were framed as small: CWL already held ~55% of Wim Plast, and the inter-company 8% loan of ~INR100 crores was repaid from QIP proceeds so Wim Plast would carry no CWL loan into the merger.
points.quote: Already because Cello World owns about 55% of the company in any case. So it's only about 45% that is being acquired.

points.point: Asked about delays, management said the hold-up was regulatory (SEBI permissions), not structural, and the CFO confirmed the 0.86 swap ratio already filed with the exchanges.
points.quote: It's not a complicated merger. It is just -- we needed some permissions from SEBI.

points.point: A Wim Plast minority shareholder (Ashok Shah, Eklavya Invesco Family Office) challenged the ratio as unfavourable to the ~40% non-CWL holders given CWL's financials; the CFO's entire answer was that it benefits everyone, with no supporting numbers.
points.quote: So it will be beneficial to all actually.

points.point: Timeline update: NCLT final hearing in the last week of February 2026, with completion expected within two to three months and effect taken from the 1 April 2025 appointed date; Gaurav confirmed Q1 FY27 closure.
points.quote: See, in the month of Feb only final hearing is there -- is around last week of Feb. And thereafter, once we get the approval, then everything is set, then we will be in the process of merging the thing.

points.point: In the same call management explained why it is NOT collapsing its other subsidiaries — unit-level P&L accountability — showing the Wim Plast merger was about removing a second listed entity, not about simplifying the group structure generally.
points.quote: So overall, while things can get easier, it also kind of dilutes the P&L of each and every unit and focus on unit economics kind of goes away.

points.point: Completion confirmed, with the forward-looking benefit stated as cross-segment synergy between consumerware and moulded furniture; the merger was listed among the initiatives expected to contribute in FY27.
points.quote: We have completed the merger of Wimplast Limited with Cello World. With this integration, the synergies between consumerware and moulded furniture can be explored further.

points.point: CFO confirmed the composite scheme became effective 27 May 2026 with appointed date 1 April 2025, and that comparatives and EPS were restated from the beginning of the previous year for shares pending issuance.
points.quote: Lastly, Iwould like to inform that composite scheme of arrangement among Wimplast, Cello Consumer Products Limited and the company has become cffective from 27th May 2026, with an appointed date of 1st April 2025 as defined under the scheme.

points.point: The scheme's two-step mechanics: Wim Plast's Manufacturing Business is demerged into CCPPL (a wholly owned CWL subsidiary) and the Remaining Business is amalgamated into CWL, after which Wim Plast ceases to exist.
points.quote: (a) the Manufacturing Business of WPL has been demerged into CCPPL, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, and (b) the Remaining Business of WPL has been amalgamated with the Company, and WPL stands dissolved without winding up.

points.point: Stated benefit one: operating synergy and economies of scale, plus unification of the regulatory burden of two separate listed companies.
points.quote: Bring about synergy of operations and economies of scale and additionally the legal and regulatory compliances of both the listed entities will be unified and streamlined;

points.point: Stated benefit two: a single listed vehicle for shareholders instead of two.
points.quote: Consolidation of ownership interests in one listed company instead of two listed entities;

verdict.rationale: Management (Vishal Mehta) framed the separation as making the listed entity a pure payments company and pushing non-payment assets out of the payments regulatory perimeter: asked directly for the rationale on the Aug 2024 call, he said "we are a payments company," that "with a lot of regulations, we believe that digital marketing will be decoupled from payments," and that digital marketing has "a much larger ecosystem" it can address once separated. The business being carved out is ODigMa, the digital-marketing arm, sized at about INR30 crores of annual revenue and less than INR1 crore of annual profitability — i.e. small on revenue and immaterial on profit, which is why management could treat the revenue impact as minor. A second asset cited was the .OOO ("dot triple O") top-level domain, which they admitted they had "not been able to build up a lot of monetization" on inside the company, implying it needs a different owner/vehicle. The mechanism was a composite scheme of arrangement: filed and awaiting regulators as of Nov 2023, NCLT-approved by Nov 2024 with shares allotted to shareholders and a listing-and-trading application pending with the exchanges. Management drew a deliberate line around AI: Phronetic/the AI vertical was put into a separate company for talent reasons ("AI is definitely a separate company, such a talent tool") but explicitly NOT demerged, because it is a platform with "a lot of synergies between what Phronetic is building out on video intelligence and payments" that they want to build and keep. The retained-side logic was also brand/ecosystem: CCAvenue is the B2B, business-facing brand and the acquired Rediff is the consumer-facing brand, giving them "an ecosystem to target both" for payments and financial products (express settlement at a $600 million run rate, bill payments, recharges, tax payments). The cost side was acknowledged in Feb 2025 — one-time legal costs for demergers plus Rediff advertising/bandwidth costs hitting PAT, with management stating they are "not optimizing for PAT" but for growth and cash flows. Shareholder pressure is visible as context rather than as a stated cause: investors pointed to EPS below INR1, a share price "stagnant since many quarters," consistent insider selling and absent institutional investors; no lender or commercial partner is cited anywhere as requesting the separation.
verdict.evolution: By the Nov 2023 call the demerger was already filed and simply waiting on regulators, with no rationale given — the only framing was an investor's hope that EPS would rise above INR1. On the Aug 2024 call the content appears: ODigMa is named and sized (INR30 crores revenue, <INR1 crore profit), the rationale is articulated as regulatory decoupling of digital marketing from payments plus the unmonetized .OOO top-level domain, and the question widens to whether the AI vertical will also be demerged — answered as "set up as a separate company for now" but no demerger commitment. By Nov 2024 execution is largely done (NCLT approval, shares allotted, exchange listing application pending) and management firmly rules out a near-term Phronetic AI demerger in favour of building it for payments synergies, while investors shift to complaining about stagnant price and insider selling; Feb 2025 only adds that demerger legal costs are a one-time drag. The filing-era documents show the restructuring continued past the calls: the Platform Business Undertaking was slump-sold to subsidiary Rediff.com India Limited, leaving standalone operations in a single Payment Business segment, alongside a rights-issue object variation, a 10:1 share consolidation and the rename to AvenuesAI Limited.

points.point: The demerger was already filed with regulators and management offered no rationale at this stage — only a status update and a promise to revert once regulators respond.
points.quote: We filed for the demerger. So we expect to hear back from the regulators. But as soon as we hear back, we will update you on the same.

points.point: Shareholder context for the restructuring: an individual investor tied his expectations to EPS, which was then below INR1, and management promised to work toward it.
points.quote: We are waiting that our EPS will be increased because it's now below INR1.

points.point: On the core business management refused margin-percentage targets, saying the focus is absolute cash generation in a competitive (non-monopoly) market where they are among the top three in India.
points.quote: So we think that as far as our business is concerned, let's focus on the absolute cash generation and not just percentages while we keep on working on the operating metrics that will help us improve our margins.

points.point: Asked for ODigMa's size, management quantified the demerged digital-marketing business at roughly INR30 crores of annual revenue with under INR1 crore of annual profitability.
points.quote: ODigMa will be about INR30 crores. And about profitability would be about -- I mean these are annual numbers, and profitability will be about less than INR1 crore.

points.point: The stated rationale, given in answer to a direct question: as a payments company under heavy regulation, digital marketing must be decoupled from payments and can then address a far larger ecosystem.
points.quote: With a lot of regulations, we believe that digital marketing will be decoupled from payments. And there's a much larger ecosystem that digital marketing can attend into.

points.point: The second limb of the rationale was the .OOO top-level domain, which management conceded they had not been able to monetize meaningfully within the company.
points.quote: Second is that we have a domain called dot triple O.

points.point: The AI vertical was deliberately treated differently: housed in a separate company mainly as a talent vehicle and an investment bet, with pilots completed and a partial second-phase rollout, but with no demerger commitment.
points.quote: And we think that while we may not have an answer for you in terms of demerger, but it's definitely set up as a separate company for now.

points.point: Retained-side logic: CCAvenue stays the B2B brand while the acquired Rediff supplies a consumer-facing brand, letting financial products be sold to both businesses and consumers; express settlement was cited at a $600 million run rate.
points.quote: CCAvenue is business-facing brand, B2B, and Rediff is a consumer-facing brand.

points.point: Execution update: the composite scheme of arrangement had been approved by NCLT, shares allotted to shareholders, and a listing-and-trading application was pending with the exchanges.
points.quote: So in other words, we believe that NCLT has approved the composite scheme of arrangement. Shares have been allocated to the respective shareholders and the company has filed an application with the exchanges for the approval of listing and trading.

points.point: Management explicitly declined to extend the demerger logic to Phronetic AI, saying it is a platform serving all businesses with direct synergies to payments that they intend to build and keep.
points.quote: And there's a lot of synergies between what Phronetic is building out on video intelligence and payments.

points.point: Investor framing after the first demerger: despite new businesses and rising revenue, the share price was stagnant with insider selling and no institutional participation.
points.quote: But share price performance is stagnant since many quarters, with consistent selling coming from insiders.

points.point: The separation carried one-time costs — demerger legal fees plus new advertising and bandwidth charges from the Rediff acquisition — which management said would hit PAT, a metric they are not optimizing for.
points.quote: So there are certain legal costs for demergers.

points.point: The filing documents a further separation beyond the calls: the Platform Business Undertaking was transferred on a going-concern basis by slump sale to subsidiary Rediff.com India Limited and is reported as discontinued operations.
points.quote: During the previous year, the Company had transferred its Platform Business Undertaking on a going concern basis through a slump sale to Rediff.com India Limited ("Rediff"), subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: Post-separation the standalone entity is a single-segment payments company — CCAvenue payment gateway, CPGS payment infrastructure for banks, and credit and lending.
points.quote: Accordingly, the Company now operates in a single business segment l.e. Payment Business which includes Payment Gateway business with CC Avenue business brand and payment infrastructure including CPGS towards banks, and Credit & Lending related business

points.point: Accompanying capital-structure actions approved by the Board: a 10-for-1 share consolidation (Re. 1 shares into Rs. 10 shares) alongside a variation in the objects of the June 19, 2025 rights issue.
points.quote: The Board has considered and approved the consolidation of the existing 10 (Ten) Equity Shares of Re. 1/- each into 1 (One) Equity Share of Rs. 10/- each, fully paid-up, subject to the approval of the shareholders of the Company and such other statutory and regulatory authorities as may be required

verdict.what_management_expects: Payments stays the regulated core — CCAvenue, CPGS for banks, credit and lending, now a single standalone segment with Rediff adding a consumer brand beside B2B. Digital marketing (ODigMa, ~INR30cr revenue) is freed from payments regulation to chase a much larger ecosystem, with the unmonetized .OOO domain alongside it. Listed shares went directly to shareholders. Focus is cash generation, not PAT or margin percentages.
verdict.gaps: No scheme rationale text (excerpt covers only rights-issue variation, consolidation, AGM); no share-entitlement ratio, valuation, capital or debt allocation, ODigMa standalone outlook, or stated lender/partner demand.

verdict.rationale: These texts do not contain a demerger or spin-off rationale for Coal India — there is no scheme of arrangement and no rationale section in the filings supplied. What the filings actually document is partial monetisation of wholly-owned coal subsidiaries through minority IPOs structured as Offers for Sale by CIL, not a separation of a business line. The trigger stated is governmental, not strategic: the Ministry of Coal, via Office Memorandum I/37811/2025 dated 16.12.2025, 'advised CIL to take concrete steps to ensure further listing of subsidiaries namely MCL and SECL in the upcoming financial year,' after which the CIL Board gave in-principle approval by circular resolution on 23.12.2025 for both Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL) and South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL), to be routed to MoC for onward submission to DIPAM. The executed transaction is Bharat Coking Coal Limited (BCCL): 465,700,000 equity shares of face value ₹10 offered for sale by CIL at ₹23 per share, listed on BSE and NSE effective 19.01.2026, cutting CIL's holding from 100% to 90% (4,657,000,000 to 4,191,300,000 shares), so BCCL ceased to be a wholly-owned subsidiary but remains a subsidiary. The next step is MCL's DRHP dated 1 September 2026, filed with SEBI, BSE and NSE, for an OFS of up to 661,836,300 equity shares of face value ₹2 held by CIL, subject to approvals and market conditions. The only earnings-call passage provided (Feb 2024) runs the other way: asked directly whether renewables/CIL energy would be put into a demerged entity, management said existing subsidiaries and JVs already cover those verticals and that no new entity was under discussion. The sole capital-structure specifics management gave in that call were that coal mine capex would be met from internal accruals, with little debt in FY25 but rising debt in the following year for the renewal and gasification projects. On this evidence the separation is a state-directed stake sale/listing programme for coal-producing subsidiaries (BCCL done, MCL filed, SECL approved in principle), with no management-stated operating or valuation argument on record here.
verdict.evolution: Feb 2024 call: an analyst (Venkatesh Subramanian) raised a demerger of the energy/renewables verticals and management rejected it — subsidiaries and JVs already exist, 'It is not in our discussion right now.' The impetus then came from outside the company: MoC's OM of 16.12.2025 directed further listing of MCL and SECL, and CIL's Board passed in-principle approvals for both on 23.12.2025 for onward submission to DIPAM. Execution followed quickly on a different subsidiary — BCCL disclosures on 03.01.2026 and 14.01.2026, pricing at ₹23 and listing on 19.01.2026 taking CIL to 90%. The programme then advanced to MCL with a DRHP dated 01.09.2026, disclosed 02.09.2026, for an OFS of up to 661,836,300 shares; SECL remains at in-principle stage in these texts.

points.point: An analyst explicitly asked whether coal, CIL energy and the alternative-energy investments would be split into a separate demerged entity; management declined, saying the verticals already sit in existing subsidiaries and JVs and no new entity was being considered.
points.quote: We had already -- some verticals are there for the renewable energy and other projects, for that we had already subsidiaries companies are there. We had already formed the joint ventures and the new companies, so those we'll pursue that. We are not going to create any new subsidy. It is not in our discussion right now.

points.point: On funding, management confirmed coal mine capex comes from internal accruals with minimal FY25 debt, but flagged rising debt in the following year for the renewal and gasification projects.
points.quote: Yes, you are right because we had just started the renewal, so not much debt will come in the '25. But in the coming year, debt will increase in the renewal and gasification projects.

points.point: The listing push is a Ministry of Coal directive, not a company-initiated scheme: MoC's Office Memorandum I/37811/2025 of 16.12.2025 told CIL to progress listings of MCL and SECL in the upcoming financial year.
points.quote: Ministry of Coal, vide its Office Memorandum I/37811/2025 dated 16.12.2025 had advised CIL to take concrete steps to ensure further listing of subsidiaries namely MCL and SECL in the upcoming financial year.

points.point: CIL's Board granted in-principle listing approval for MCL on 23.12.2025 by circular resolution, for communication to MoC and onward submission to DIPAM, subject to regulatory approvals.
points.quote: Accordingly, CIL Board through circular resolution has accorded in –principle approval for listing of Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL) and the same shall be communicated to MoC for onward submission to DIPAM.

points.point: An identical in-principle approval was passed the same day for South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL), also wholly owned, also subject to regulatory approvals — so two subsidiaries were cleared in principle simultaneously.
points.quote: Accordingly, CIL Board through circular resolution has accorded in –principle approval for listing of South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL) and the same shall be communicated to MoC for onward submission to DIPAM.

points.point: BCCL's IPO was pure Offer for Sale by CIL — 465,700,000 shares of ₹10 face value at ₹23 per share — i.e. cash to the parent, no primary issuance disclosed here.
points.quote: Bharat Coking Coal Limited, pursuant to its IPO, has sold 465,700,000 Equity Shares at an issue price of ₹ 23 per share which were offered for sale by the Company .

points.point: BCCL listed on BSE and NSE effective 19.01.2026 and CIL's stake fell from 100% to 90% (4,657,000,000 to 4,191,300,000 shares), following earlier disclosures of 3 and 14 January 2026.
points.quote: As a result of the above, the Company 's shareholding in Bharat Coking Coal Limited stands reduced f rom 100% to 90% (i.e., from 4,657,000,000 Equity Shares to 4,191,300,000 Equity Shares) of the issued and paid -up Equity Share capital of Bharat Coking Coal Limited.

points.point: Control is explicitly retained — BCCL stops being wholly owned but stays a subsidiary, confirming this is a minority sell-down rather than a separation or loss of consolidation.
points.quote: Consequent to the above, Bharat Coking Coal ceases to be a wholly -owned subsidiary of the Company. However, it continues to remain a subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: MCL's DRHP dated 1 September 2026 was filed with SEBI, BSE and NSE for an OFS of up to 661,836,300 shares of ₹2 face value held by CIL, conditional on approvals and market conditions.
points.quote: The DRHP filing pertains to the proposed Initial Public Offering (“IPO”) of MCL, comprising an Offer for Sale of up to 661,836,300 equity shares having a face value of INR 2 each, held by Coal India Limited.

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing is stated. No filing or call passage here claims any benefit — no margin, capital-allocation, capex-funding, focus, re-rating or value-unlocking argument for CIL or for BCCL/MCL/SECL. The only expectations expressed are procedural: listings subject to regulatory approvals, DIPAM routing, and prevailing market conditions. The one capital comment (Feb 2024) concerns internal accruals and project debt, unrelated to any separation.
verdict.gaps: No rationale section, no use of proceeds, no valuation/margin/capital logic, no SECL timeline or size, no investor/lender/partner demand cited, no call discussion of these listings.

verdict.segment_name: Bharat Coking Coal Limited (BCCL) / Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL) / South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL) — subsidiaries of Coal India Limited; not reported as separate segments
verdict.measure_notes: No segment profit or revenue line exists on these pages. Coal India states in all three annual reports (standalone and consolidated) that 'the group's main business is Coal mining and related services... there are no separate reportable segments' (AR2024 p.247, AR2025 p.249 & p.292, AR2026 p.226 & p.270). The only profit figures carried are group/parent-level EPS numerators — consolidated PAT attributable to equity holders and CIL standalone PAT — not the separating entities' own financials. No revenue, EBIT, EBITDA or segment result for BCCL, MCL or SECL appears anywhere in the supplied pages.

Annual Report 2025 — page 292 (no segment reporting; only CIL consolidated PAT 35,358.16 and, page 249, CIL standalone PAT 17,016.56)

verdict.not_found: All of them. Pages carry no revenue, operating profit or PAT for BCCL, MCL or SECL; CIL reports no separate segments. Presentation May 2025 pages show only coal resources, rail projects, gasification JVs and CSR — no quarterly financials.

verdict.rationale: The separation is a Scheme of Arrangement demerging the "Clinical Services" undertaking of NH Integrated Care Private Limited (NHIC, a wholly owned subsidiary) — 9 clinics in Bengaluru and 1 in Hosur — into the listed parent Narayana Hrudayalaya Limited (NHL) on a going-concern basis, while the Narayana Aarogyam care-plan vertical stays behind in NHIC and the IRDAI-regulated insurer Narayana Health Insurance Limited (NHIL) remains a separate reporting entity. Management's stated reason is cost and overhead duplication: Sandhya J said the clinics' residual losses were "mainly because of the corporate overheads that are being incurred to sustain the integrated care infrastructure," with the combined clinics-plus-insurance drag flat at roughly INR 66 crore in FY26 despite the first cohort of clinics breaking even in the modelled 18 months. Viren Shetty framed the demerger as letting the clinics share corporate resources with the parent rather than carry a standalone cost base — "a few of the corporate overheads can be worked in a way that we share resources with the parent and we'll be demerging the clinic business into the core" — and in Feb 2026 as being "better able to manage the synergies and costs between two entities," so the margin dilution "should minimize over the coming quarters." The second rationale is measurement and reporting: clinics are an acknowledged feeder for the hospitals (domestic inpatient referrals replacing lost Bangladesh/international volumes, and a funnel into One Health/insurance plans), and as doctors, manpower and expenses get shared across hospitals and clinics in the same cities, "it will be harder for us to say what is attributable to clinic alone and what is not," so from FY27 the clinic business is rolled into the hospital P&L as "its best reflection of the contribution to the performance of those hospitals." A corollary benefit management cited is cleaner disclosure of the insurance arm: once integrated care merges into NHL, NHIL's profitability is reported separately rather than netted against clinic burn in a single "integrated care" line. Mechanically it is cost-free to shareholders: because NHIC is a 100% subsidiary, no shares are issued, there is no change in share capital or shareholding pattern, no SEBI/BSE/NSE no-objection was required (Regulation 37(6), intimation only), employees transfer on terms no less favourable, and NHIC's sole secured creditor's (HSBC) charge over the demerged undertaking moves to NHL. The only cost called out was one-time transaction expense — "legal stamp duty and other costs" sitting in FY26 India overheads, said to normalise next year. No investor, lender or partner was identified as having demanded the separation; the pressure visible in the calls is analysts repeatedly asking why clinic/insurance losses were not falling and when breakeven would come.
verdict.evolution: Through the Aug 2025 (Q1 FY26) and Nov 2025 (Q2 FY26) calls there is no mention of any demerger — management discussed only the INR 450 crore earmarked for clinics and insurance (INR 100 crore capital into insurance, INR 150 crore into clinics by Q1) and cash burn trending down. The Board approved the Scheme on December 12, 2025 and filed it with NCLT Bengaluru on December 17, 2025, and it was first explained to investors on the Feb 17, 2026 call as "merging it into NHL" to manage synergies and costs, with Sandhya confirming integrated care would merge into NHL while insurance would be reported separately. By the May 26, 2026 call the language hardened to "demerging the clinic business into the core," with FY27 guidance that clinics would be reported inside the hospital business and merger-related stamp duty/legal costs flagged as one-timers. Procedurally it ran from the Feb 13, 2026 first-motion order to near-unanimous approvals on April 2, 2026 (equity 99.9999% in favour; secured and unsecured creditors 100%) and NCLT sanction delivered October 30, 2026 (order uploaded November 4, 2026) with an Appointed Date of April 1, 2025.

points.point: Viren Shetty ties the demerger directly to stripping out duplicated corporate overhead by sharing resources with the listed parent, in answer to why clinic/insurance losses stayed flat.
points.quote: What we are doing is a little bit of consolidation and a few of the corporate overheads can be worked in a way that we share resources with the parent and we'll be demerging the clinic business into the core that should help with a lot of that.

points.point: Sandhya J identifies the residual loss as corporate overhead for the integrated-care structure, not clinic-level losses, since the clinics set up two years earlier had already broken even.
points.quote: the losses that you' re seeing are mainly because of the corporate overheads that are being incurred to sustain the integrated care infrastructure.

points.point: The analyst framing that prompted the demerger answer: clinics-plus-insurance losses stuck at about INR 66 crore in FY26 despite expected maturity-driven decline.
points.quote: If you look at the clinics and insurance losses, it has remained flat around INR 66 crore s loss in FY 26.

points.point: Measurement rationale: shared doctors, manpower and expenses across hospitals and clinics in the same city make standalone clinic attribution impossible, so clinics are reported inside hospitals from FY27.
points.quote: But going forward, it will be harder for us to say what is attributable to clinic alone and what is not simply because a huge amount of the manpower and expenses and doctor talent will be shared between the two.

points.point: Explicit reporting change effective FY27, justified as the truest reflection of what clinics contribute to hospital performance.
points.quote: So, from this year onwards, FY27, the clinic business will be rolled in with the overall hospital business because that is its best reflection of the contribution to the performance of those hospitals.

points.point: Sandhya flags unquantified one-time merger costs (legal, stamp duty) inside FY26 India other expenses, which is why operating leverage did not show at 18% of revenue.
points.quote: In addition, there are some one -time costs in there because we are going through a certain merger process.

points.point: Strategic justification for keeping and expanding clinics: they are the sole driver of domestic referrals that replaced de-emphasised international revenue and the entry point for One Health insurance customers.
points.quote: Ever since we took a call on improving our domestic focus and deemphasizing on growing international revenues, the clinic business has been the sole driver of the increased referrals to our hospitals from the cities in which we operate.

points.point: First investor-facing explanation of the transaction, framed as managing synergies and costs across two entities and reducing margin dilution over coming quarters.
points.quote: We are balancing out the scope of expansion of our clinic program across the country and merging it into NHL.

points.point: Viren links the merger to minimising the dilutive impact of the clinic build-out on reported margins, while confirming continued investment in clinics across core geographies.
points.quote: So, we're better able to manage the synergies and costs between two entities. So, the diluted impact should minimize over the coming quarters.

points.point: Sandhya separates the two legs: integrated care (clinics) merges into NHL; the insurance company stays a separate reported business.
points.quote: Integrated care will merge into NHL. The insurance business we will continue to report out separately.

points.point: A disclosure benefit management expects: post-merger, insurance profitability gets reported on its own instead of being blended into the integrated-care loss line.
points.quote: Once the merger happens, we will report out the profitability of the insurance business separately.

points.point: The transaction perimeter: Clinical Services undertaking of NHIC — 9 Bengaluru clinics plus 1 Hosur clinic — transferred to NHL as a going concern, with Appointed Date April 1, 2025.
points.quote: The Scheme provides for the demerger of the Clinical Services (as defined in the Scheme) undertaking of the Demerged Company, comprising 9 clinics located in Bengaluru and 1 clinic in Hosur, into the Company on a going-concern basis.

points.point: What is left behind: the Narayana Aarogyam care-plan vertical continues inside NHIC, which retains its "Remaining Undertaking" and its own assets and liabilities.
points.quote: to demerge the clinical services as defined in the scheme of NHIC ('the Demerged Undertaking') into the Resulting Company, while continuing the Narayana Aarogyam Vertical within NHIC, on a going concern basis

points.point: No dilution or consideration because NHIC is a 100% subsidiary; share capital and shareholding pattern of the listed company are unchanged.
points.quote: As the Demerged Company is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, no shares shall be issued by the Company as consideration pursuant to the Scheme and, accordingly, there will be no change in the share capital or shareholding pattern of the Company.

points.point: Light regulatory path: as a wholly owned subsidiary demerger, only intimation to the exchanges was required rather than SEBI/NSE/BSE no-objection certificates.
points.quote: in terms of Regulation 37(6) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 read with the applicable SEBI Circulars, no No-Objection Certificate from the Securities and Exchange Board of India, National Stock Exchange of India Limited or BSE Limited is required for the Scheme, and only an intimation to the said Stock Exchanges is necessary

points.point: Employee protection: clinic staff move to NHL without break in service and with provident fund, gratuity and superannuation balances transferred.
points.quote: all employees of Petitioner Company No.1 engaged in the Demerged Undertaking shall become employees of Petitioner Company No. 2 with effect from the Effective Date, on terms and conditions no less favourable than those on which they were engaged by Petitioner Company No. 1, and without any interruption in service.

points.point: Lender treatment: HSBC, NHIC's sole secured creditor, voted for the Scheme and its charge over the demerged clinics shifts to NHL.
points.quote: It is further submitted that the charge in favor of the said Secured Creditor pertains to the Demerged Undertaking and hence shall be moved to Petitioner Company No. 2.

verdict.rationale: Management framed the separation as the core of "Vedanta 2.0": breaking one monolithic diversified natural-resources company into five independent, sector-specific pure-play listed companies — Vedanta Limited (residual: Zinc India/HZL, Zinc International, Copper, Ferrochrome/FACOR, Nickel), Vedanta Aluminium Metal Ltd, Vedanta Power/Talwandi Sabo Power (merchant power), Vedanta Oil & Gas/Malco Energy (Cairn), and Vedanta Iron & Steel — so that each could "chart out their own growth trajectory and attract respective thematic investors" rather than being valued as a conglomerate (Apr 2026, Apr 2025: "pure-play entities that will enhance strategic focus and operational flexibility"). The stated problem was that a single balance sheet and single capital-allocation process blurred very different businesses: Zinc India at 56% EBITDA margin and $959/t COP, aluminium at 38% margin, versus a Copper trading business running ~1% margin, and a power business that wants to add 10–12 GW. The fix was a capital structure "architected with precision… aligning debt with earning strength and growth stage of each resulting company": of $5.5bn net debt (group leverage 0.95x), $3.5bn goes to Aluminium (1.3x), Power sits at 4.7x on long-dated PFC/REC paper, Vedanta Limited keeps ~$1bn (0.4x), while Oil & Gas is nil-debt and Iron & Steel carries no more than $0.2bn. Specific frictions the split removes: the Copper brand fee drops from 3% to 0.75% on ~$3.1–3.2bn of revenue (~$65m, +2.25% to EBITDA), taking Copper margin from ~1% toward at least 5% in FY27; the dividend policy moves from "prescriptive" to "descriptive", from rule-based (minimum 30% of profit) to principle-based, and the mandate to upstream Hindustan Zinc dividends within six months falls away; Ajay Goel also called it "an opportunity… from taxation viewpoint" via recast balance sheets, accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation. Third parties shaped the terms: lenders demanded debt allocation be "broadly aligned with the bankers as a precondition for granting NOC"; the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas objected at NCLT over ~$512–520m of disputed dues and was satisfied only by a Vedanta corporate guarantee covering the full alleged claims, with any arbitration outcome ring-fenced to Oil & Gas; creditor SEPCO was settled in full for ₹660 crore "as part of demerger proceedings… paving the way for a proposed demerger process", and a ₹1,248 crore cash-backed bank guarantee was lodged with NCLAT over the TSPL power demerger. Management also pointed to equity-side demand — "many anchor investors domestically and globally are very keen to come in the cap table" of the de-merged entities as a fresh deleveraging avenue for VRL's remaining $4.7bn. Three months after listing, the Board extended the same logic to a second, vertical separation: ~2,264 acres and ~53,185 sq ft of surplus real estate (22 assets, only ₹1.26 crore of FY26 turnover, 0.001% of standalone revenue) into Vedanta Property Platforms Ltd at 1 share for every 20, because the portfolio was "historically subject to limited focused utilisation, resulting in sub-optimal visibility… and value realization."
verdict.evolution: The demerger was already a live execution item by the Feb 2025 call (Jan 31, 2025), where Ajay Goel flagged the Feb 18 shareholder/creditor meetings as "the important stage of execution"; on the Apr 2025 call (Apr 30, 2025) Deshnee Naidoo recast it as creating "pure-play entities" under Vedanta 2.0 with completion guided for September 2025. It then slipped repeatedly on legal and stakeholder hurdles — Aug 2025 (Jul 31, 2025) disclosed the NCLT second-motion part-hearing of July 2 with the next date Aug 20, an NCLAT interim stay on the TSPL power order, and the MoPNG objection; Nov 2025 (Oct 31, 2025) resolved SEPCO for ₹660 crore and MoPNG via a Vedanta corporate guarantee, guiding to a final Nov 12 hearing and five listings by FY26-end. Jan 2026 (Jan 29, 2026) reported NCLT approval on Dec 16, 2025 (power on Jan 9, 2026) and shifted the detail toward mechanics — bank NOCs conditioned on debt allocation, recast balance sheets, tax structuring — targeting Apr 1 effectiveness; Apr 2026 (Apr 29, 2026) set the record date at May 1 with mid-June listing, 4 extra shares per share, and added two new rationales not previously spelled out: the Copper brand-fee cut to 0.75% and five independent dividend policies. By the Jul 30, 2026 filings the plan had extended beyond the original five, with a sixth vertical split of surplus real estate into Vedanta Property Platforms Ltd at 1:20.

points.point: The demerger was already at the shareholder/creditor-vote stage, pitched purely as investor value unlock, with no operational rationale given on this call.
points.quote: On the demerger front, we are in the important stage of execution , the shareholders and the creditors meeting scheduled on Feb 18th. This transformative step is poised to unlock significant value for our investors.

points.point: First explicit statement of the design goal — pure-play entities for strategic focus and operational flexibility — inside the Vedanta 2.0 ambition of a $100bn critical minerals, energy and technology powerhouse; completion then guided for September 2025.
points.quote: We are making good progress with our demerger plan, aiming to create pure-play entities that will enhance strategic focus and operational flexibility.

points.point: A shareholder (Ashish Kejriwal, Nuvama) pressed that mining leases — Sijimali bauxite and the coal blocks held under Vedanta Limited — must first be transferred to Vedanta Aluminium before the split can complete; management confirmed a parallel approvals plan.
points.quote: Ashish, you are right. This is part of the overall approvals that we have in our sight.

points.point: Execution stalled in two forums at once: the NCLT second-motion petition was part-heard on July 2 with the next date Aug 20, and NCLAT granted an interim stay on the TSPL power demerger order, backed by a ₹1,248 crore fully cash-backed bank guarantee over the SEPCO creditor matter.
points.quote: Separately, the NCL AT has granted an interim stay on TSPL, our power demerger order by NCLT, with the next hearing scheduled on 4th August.

points.point: The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas objected at NCLT, questioning whether the demerged, standalone Cairn oil & gas P&L could absorb disputed dues if arbitration went against Vedanta — i.e. a regulator worrying that separation strips a weaker entity of parent support.
points.quote: In the last NCLT hearing, they did express concern about the payments of any of the disputed dues that may become payable by Cairn in case the ongoing arbitration ruling, as we have all learned now, comes in their favor.

points.point: A long-standing SEPCO creditor dispute was settled in full for ₹660 crore (part of ₹1,547 crore of net exceptional items that quarter) explicitly to clear the path for the scheme.
points.quote: As part of demerger proceedings, a full and final settlement of Rs. 660 Cr has been done with SEPCO , thereby resolving a long -standing dispute, paving the way for a proposed demerger process.

points.point: MoPNG's objection — over roughly $512–520m of alleged claims — was resolved not by cash but by a Vedanta corporate guarantee covering the full extent of the claims, so the demerged oil & gas entity would not carry the obligation.
points.quote: Their concern has been taken care of by us providing a corporate guarantee from Vedanta.

points.point: Five simultaneous listings by FY26-end were framed as the vehicle for sharper strategic focus, with Goel adding that it unlocks "focused value across our five verticals".
points.quote: This will set the stage for the listing of all five demerge d entities by the end of FY '26, enabling greater strategic focus and enhanced value creation for all stakeholders.

points.point: After NCLT approval on Dec 16, 2025 (power order Jan 9, 2026), the rationale was stated as three things at once — sharper strategy, stronger standalone balance sheets, faster growth — with Q3 results already reported under Ind AS 105 demerger accounting.
points.quote: This marks a defining moment in our journey, one that empowers our businesses to sharpen the strategies, strengthen the balance sheets and accelerate growth with the aim of unlocking shareholder value.

points.point: Lenders drove the capital-structure design: debt allocation across the five entities had to be agreed with banks before they would issue no-objection certificates, with $6.7bn of Vedanta India consol net debt split by asset ratio and each entity's own cash-generation and debt-servicing capability.
points.quote: When we went to the banker seeking NOC, in that case, debt allocation was broadly aligned with the bankers as a precondition for granting NOC for demerger approval.

points.point: Goel named taxation and deleveraging as further gains — recast balance sheets, accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation per entity — alongside the intent to make oil & gas and iron & steel debt-free, funded partly by the ₹3,000 crore HZL OFS.
points.quote: One thing I can confirm to the entire audience and to the stakeholders at large, that demerger in fact, becomes an opportunity across the areas.

points.point: Final articulation: five sector-specific pure-play companies whose purpose is independent growth paths and dedicated thematic investor bases; record date May 1, 2026, one Vedanta share yielding four additional shares, listing targeted by Q1 FY27 (mid-June).
points.quote: This will entail creation of five independent sector -specific pure -play companies, allowing each company to chart out their own growth trajectory and attract respective thematic investors.

points.point: Debt was matched to each business's earnings power and growth stage rather than split pro-rata: Oil & Gas nil debt, Iron & Steel under $0.2bn, Aluminium $3.5bn at 1.3x, Power 4.7x on 7–10 year PFC/REC paper, Vedanta Limited ~$1bn at 0.4x, against group leverage of 0.95x.
points.quote: The de -merger has been architected with precision on capital structure, aligning debt with earning strength and growth stage of each resulting company.

points.point: A concrete economic benefit of unbundling: the brand fee was re-benchmarked per entity, cutting Copper's rate from 3% to 0.75% on ~$3.1–3.2bn of revenue (~$65m), lifting Copper margin from roughly 1% to at least 5% in FY27, while the other entities stay at 3% (fixed to FY29).
points.quote: So the brand fee for copper from the current 3% will go down to 0.75% and that alone from India's viewpoint means higher EBITDA by 2.25%.

points.point: Each of the five boards gets its own dividend policy; Vedanta's shifts from rule-based (minimum 30% of profit) to principle-based, and the obligation to pass through Hindustan Zinc dividends within six months is removed.
points.quote: Currently, Vedanta's policy on dividend is more prescriptive; it will become more descriptive.

points.point: Separation creates a new deleveraging route for VRL's remaining $4.7bn: differentiated capital structures that anchor investors can enter at the entity level, on top of the ~$400m brand fee and 4–5% dividend.
points.quote: Now as we de -merge all the five companies, additionally we'll have the optionality of a differentiated capital structure and in that case, many anchor investors domestically and globally are very keen to come in the cap table , and that will be additional avenue for de -leveraging.

points.point: M&A governance was redrawn around the split: each CEO is mandated to grow organically on their own 2x/3x plans, with cross-sector or out-of-portfolio acquisitions sitting at a new holdco with its own M&A team and the Chairman.
points.quote: Holdco will be set up to make sure there is some visibility of capital allocation across all 5 businesses, but also with its own M&A team to start looking at some of these opportunities.

points.point: The May 16, 2026 cost-apportionment filing fixes the five resulting entities and their relative weights: Vedanta Limited 52.34%, Vedanta Aluminium Metal 7.15%, Talwandi Sabo Power 12.23%, Malco Energy (oil & gas) 21.49%, Vedanta Iron and Steel 6.79% — one share of each per Vedanta share, effective/appointed date May 1, 2026.
points.quote: In accordance with provisions of the Scheme, Resulting Companies issued and allotted 1 (One) fully paid -up equity share of each Resulting Companies for every 1 (One) fully paid -up equity share held in the Company

points.point: On July 30, 2026 the Board approved a sixth, vertical separation — surplus real estate (22 assets, ~2,264 acres and ~53,185 sq ft, just ₹1.26 crore of FY26 turnover, 0.001% of standalone revenue) into Vedanta Property Platforms Ltd at 1 share per 20 — because the assets sat embedded in the operating business and were under-utilised.
points.quote: The real estate business is currently embedded within the operating business and the real estate portfolio has been historically subject to limited focused utilisation, resulting in sub -optimal visibility of the real estate business segment and value realization.

points.point: The real estate scheme's stated aim mirrors the five-way logic — a pure-play platform with its own management, capital structure and investor base, potentially consolidating real estate from other group companies (Meenakshi Energy, Incab) and claiming a value-creation opportunity of over ₹30,000 crore on ~130mn sq ft.
points.quote: To unlock the inherent value of the Real Estate Business, enable focused development, exploit the growth potential of the Real Estate Business and attract a distinct set of investors and strategic partners aligned with real estate and infrastructure development, it is proposed to consolidate the Real Estate Business of the Demerged Company under an independent, dedicated entity.

points.point: The Q1 FY27 filings present the completed demerger as having validated the thesis: combined market cap of the resulting companies up over ₹71,000 crore in one quarter, and ₹225.50 at announcement (Sep 29, 2023) versus ₹932.05 combined on listing day (June 15, 2026).
points.quote: Vedanta’s  demerger is unlock ing significant shareholder value, with combined market cap of resulting companies growing  by over ₹71,000 crore  in the 1st quarter .

verdict.what_management_expects: Five pure-plays each chasing its own growth and thematic investors; debt matched to earnings — Oil & Gas nil, Iron & Steel <$0.2bn, Aluminium 1.3x, Power 4.7x, Vedanta Ltd 0.4x; Copper brand fee 3%→0.75% lifting margin ~1%→5%+; independent dividend policies with HZL upstream mandate dropped; tax efficiency from recast balance sheets; anchor investors entering entity cap tables to deleverage VRL; real estate platform targeting ₹30,000 crore+.
verdict.gaps: No per-entity EBITDA/valuation targets, no quantified stranded corporate or listing costs, no reason the other four brand fees stay at 3%, no real-estate monetisation timeline or revenue model.

verdict.rationale: Triveni's board approved a Composite Scheme of Arrangement on 10 December 2024 with two legs: amalgamating its ~61.77%-owned listed subsidiary Sir Shadi Lal Enterprises (SSEL, the Shamli sugar/distillery unit) into TEIL, and demerging the Power Transmission Business (PTB — high-speed/turbo gearboxes at Mysuru plus the incubating defence business) into Triveni Power Transmission Limited (TPTL), a wholly-owned subsidiary, for separate listing. Management framed it consistently as 'value unlocking' and, by Feb 2026, 'to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies' — the logic being that PTB is a technology business with robust, predictable economics (FY25 turnover +27%, PBIT ₹126.8 crore, +18.4%, margins >34%; order booking ₹475 crore) sitting inside a conglomerate whose sugar and ethanol businesses are, in Tarun Sawhney's words, 'regulated from every corner' on both input and output pricing, producing mercurial quarterly outcomes that investors (notably Bharat Shah, Feb 2025) said made the group hard to value. Separation also lets PTB fund its own growth: the board approved capex in three tranches totalling ₹340 crore (gears capacity from ~₹400 crore to ₹700 crore by September 2026, plus a defence facility of just north of ₹100 crore); ₹231 crore was incurred by 31 March 2026, of which ₹78 crore was defence, and management said TPTL 'is armed with sufficient cash flows and a balance sheet' to complete it. Critically, TEIL deliberately retained ~30% of TPTL rather than a clean 100% distribution — Sawhney said the defence business, co-located in Mysuru and sharing the same facility and offices, needs group balance-sheet backing to secure pre-qualifications and the ability to bid, and he cited the earlier Triveni Turbine separation as a positive precedent, pushing back on investor Resham Jain's holdco-discount objection. The SSEL leg removes a separately listed, loss-making subsidiary (plantation-white sugar selling at a discount, white-fly-hit recoveries, two breakdowns, a Shamli distillery that had not operated since acquisition) and folds its crush, varietal and distillery de-bottlenecking upside into TEIL's commodities platform. Mechanically: SSEL holders got 100 TEIL shares (₹1 FV) per 137 SSEL shares; TEIL holders get 1 TPTL share (₹2 FV) per 3 TEIL shares; scheme appointed date 1 April 2025, demerger appointed date 1 April 2026. Post-approval ICRA reaffirmed TEIL's long-term rating at AA+ Stable, lifting it from 'under watch', and management committed to separate boards, published results and earnings calls for TEIL and TPTL from Q1 FY27.
verdict.evolution: The scheme was announced on 10 December 2024 and first discussed on the Feb 2025 call, where Sawhney tied it to 'value unlocking', guided to NCLT approval by end-CY2025, and defended the retained ~30% stake in TPTL against investor pushback; the same call approved the incremental ₹60 crore gears capex. Through Jun 2025 and Aug 2025 the file sat with SEBI ('we're following up continuously with SEBI', possibly 'another 30-odd days'), and investors began asking for granular PTB disclosure ahead of a separate listing, which management accepted; by Nov 2025 the stock exchanges had cleared it (observation letters 7 and 11 August 2025) and NCLT stakeholder meetings were set for end-November/early December, with TPTL also acquiring the Swiss subsidiary Triveni Power Transmission GmbH. Shareholders and creditors approved on 7 December 2025, and on the Feb 2026 call Sawhney said 'the next time we speak in all probability, this will be two separate companies' and described systems work to let TPTL 'hit the ground sprinting'. NCLT sanctioned it (orders 7 and 18 May 2026), effective 19 May 2026; on the Jun 2026 call Sawhney called it a 'historic call', guided to a TPTL listing by end-August 2026, and TPTL shares were in fact allotted on 28 July 2026 and listed on 12 October 2026.

points.point: First investor call after the 10 December 2024 board approval; Sawhney explicitly tied the two-part scheme (SSEL amalgamation into TEIL; PTB demerger into wholly-owned TPTL) to value unlocking as a board priority.
points.quote: I also wanted to provide an update on the Scheme, as you're all aware, this is in conjunction with value unlocking that the Board of Directors has felt very important.

points.point: Asked by Resham Jain (DSP) why TEIL would keep ~30% of TPTL instead of a clean split that avoids a holdco discount, Sawhney gave two reasons: the positive Triveni Turbine precedent, and the need for group balance-sheet strength to win defence pre-qualifications.
points.quote: The second and very, very important is because we are incubating a Defence business, which we have large aspirations for. In establishing pre-qualifications (PQs) and the ability to be able to quote, there are balance sheet considerations that even from a Group perspective that are very, very important to allow us to be in contention.

points.point: He added that the defence business is co-located with PTB in Mysuru and must not be handicapped by the separation, which he said was being done 'because it's the right time'.
points.quote: we should not handicap a business just because we're separating the business, the Power Transmission business because it's the right time, we are separating it with the Defence business, which is co-located in the same city and utilising the same facility and offices that exist today.

points.point: Investor Bharat Shah (ASK) framed the core valuation problem the demerger addresses: PTB has robust, predictable economics while the rest of the group produces 'mercurial' outcomes; Sawhney conceded sugar and ethanol are regulated on both input and output pricing.
points.quote: Turning then to large businesses, as far as Sugar and Ethanol are concerned, you are absolutely right. They are regulated industries, they are regulated from every corner. The pricing of your raw material and the pricing of your end product.

points.point: The same board meeting approved an incremental ~₹60 crore of gears capex (gears only, not defence), taking PTB gears capacity from ~₹400 crore to ₹700 crore by September 2026 — the growth the separately listed entity is meant to fund.
points.quote: The Board meeting of the Directors concluded yesterday had an important announcement of an incremental capex of ₹60 crore for the enhancement of capacity in the Power Transmission business . This will take the gears capacity to ₹700 crore by September 2026.

points.point: Initial regulatory timeline guidance: NCLT approval expected by end of calendar 2025.
points.quote: As far as the Scheme of Arrangement is concerned, we anticipate approval from NCLT by the end of this calendar year.

points.point: PTB's FY25 standalone performance — the asset being separated — was record: turnover +27%, PBIT ₹126.8 crore (+18.4%), margins above 34%, order booking over ₹475 crore, with growth not costing profitability.
points.quote: And the PB IT grew by 18.4% to ₹126.8 crore with PBIT margins in excess of 34%, which is a very much in line with our long -term average.

points.point: Scheme status: pending with SEBI, with NCLT and court-convened meetings to follow; Sawhney reiterated separation of the PTB business by Q4 FY26 / middle of Q1 CY2026.
points.quote: With respect t o the scheme of arrangement that is underway, I'd like to just briefly comment that this lies with SEBI at this particular point in time. We are awaiting the approval for SEBI.

points.point: Resham Jain asked for far more granular PTB disclosure precisely because it would be separately listed — an investor-driven push for transparency that management accepted.
points.quote: I would request maybe if you can start giving more colour on the Power Transmission business from like what kind of customers you are targeting ? What kind of mix you have between various industries going forward? That would be very helpful , given that this is going to get separately listed in the next one year.

points.point: Still awaiting regulatory clearance; Sawhney flagged possible slippage of about 30 days but held to Q4 FY26, and said the board would run workshops on what post-demerger TEIL does with its cash flows.
points.quote: The amalgamation with Sir Shadi Lal and the demerger of the Power Transmission business. We are still awaiting regulatory approvals. We're following up continuously with SEBI.

points.point: On post-demerger TEIL, Sawhney said the board intends to evaluate options for deploying the commodities businesses' cash flows to rebuild the FY23-type margin structure, but had nothing concrete to share.
points.quote: Now with respect to Triveni, after the demerger, looking at other things, we have some time for that demerger to happen, yet the thought process is on and the Board is going to conduct workshops, et c., and evaluate a series of different options.

points.point: Stock exchange approvals received (observation letters dated 7 and 11 August 2025); NCLT stakeholder meetings scheduled for end-November and early December 2025, keeping Q4 FY26 on track. TPTL also bought 100% of the Swiss entity Triveni Power Transmission GmbH, building out the standalone export engine.
points.quote: The proposed scheme has been approved by the stock exchanges, and the process is obtaining approval of NCLT . The meetings of stakeholders under the NCL T process has been scheduled for the end of November and early December for the 2 companies.

points.point: Disclosed PTB order-book split showing the defence weighting that justified keeping group balance-sheet support: of a ~₹395 crore book, ₹185 crore was long-tenure and 'the vast majority of that is defence'.
points.quote: In terms of the break up of short -tenure and long -tenure, as of September 2026, our short -tenure is ₹210 crore and long is ₹185 crore .

points.point: The clearest statement of purpose: unlock value and drive operational efficiencies. Shareholders and creditors approved in December 2025; an NCLT hearing was set for February 2026.
points.quote: Lastly, with respect to the proposed scheme of amalgamation of SSEL and the demerger of the Power Transmission business to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies, the scheme has been approved by shareholders of creditors, this was in December of 2025.

points.point: Standalone-readiness work was underway so TPTL could operate as an independent listed company with TEIL-level efficiency from day one.
points.quote: Looking at the Power Transmission business, gaining a lot of skill sets in terms of ability to operate as a separate company. A lot of systems work is being done as we speak to let them hit the ground sprinting, frankly speaking, and have the same kind of efficiencies that we've had at Triveni Engineering.

points.point: Sawhney signalled the split was imminent and thanked investors for years of feedback on the combined entity's call.
points.quote: I think the next time we speak in all probability, this will be two separate companies.

points.point: On the SSEL leg, Sawhney conceded Shamli would still be loss-making in SS 2025-26 (white fly in ratoon, urea dosing by farmers, two breakdowns) and that turnaround comes the following year — context for folding it into TEIL.
points.quote: Shamli being a new unit and the relationships speak new, our sway over the farming population needs to improve and increase

points.point: Scheme effective 19 May 2026 after NCLT approval; Sawhney called it a 'historic' call, with the scheme appointed date 1 April 2025 and the demerger appointed date 1 April 2026.
points.quote: I'm delighted to inform you that the composite scheme of arrangement is effective from the 19th of May, 2026 after the approval of the NCLT.

points.point: A concrete financial benefit of the approval: ICRA reaffirmed TEIL's long-term rating at AA+ Stable and removed the 'under watch' status the pending scheme had caused.
points.quote: I am very proud to announce that post the scheme having been approved, ICRA has reaffirmed our long -term credit rating as AA+ Stable, lifting it from its previous under watch status.

points.point: Total approved PTB capex is ₹340 crore in three tranches (₹700 crore of gears output, excluding defence); ₹231 crore incurred by 31 March 2026 of which ₹78 crore was defence; TPTL will carry the remaining ~₹109 crore on its own balance sheet.
points.quote: Of course, as power transmission migrates into Triveni Power Transmission Limited, the company is armed with sufficient cash flows and a balance sheet to be able to incur all of this CapEx and OpEx and more.

points.point: Independent listing described as the business's strategic push, with the Swiss subsidiary and new AVL qualifications (pumps, compressors, gas, defence test rigs) as the growth engine; FY26 order book just under ₹500 crore, 25% higher.

verdict.rationale: The stated primary object is to consolidate all NBFC business of the two applicant companies into a single entity. The trigger is regulatory: Sammaan Capital Ltd (SCL), the listed company, was formerly registered with the National Housing Bank as a non-deposit-taking HFC (certificate dated December 28, 2005, registration number 02.0063.05), a licence later surrendered; following a shareholder resolution of September 25, 2023 and an application to RBI for conversion from HFC to NBFC-ICC, SCL received a certificate of registration dated June 28, 2024, number N-14.03624, under Section 45IA of the RBI Act, 1934, and RBI directed while issuing it that no other group entity shall hold an NBFC-ICC/HFC CoR within a prescribed timeline. Because Sammaan Finserve Ltd (SFL) — a wholly owned subsidiary that is itself an NBFC-ICC and is the Demerged Company here, with SCL as the Resulting Company holding its entire equity — also holds such a licence, the demerger transfers SFL's NBFC business to SCL on a going-concern basis to comply. Management argues the merged lending book gets a wider and stronger capital and asset base, pooled resources, knowledge and client relationships, a more diversified product suite on a unified platform, simpler corporate structure, economies of scale, lower administrative and compliance cost and a stronger risk-management architecture. The split also frees SFL, which says it is contemplating entry into the strategically distinct insurance broking and insurtech business and wants a dedicated management and operational structure for it, citing sustained insurance-industry growth, rising dependence on the broking channel, digital disruption, favourable regulatory reform and rising investor interest. Mechanically it is structured as a tax-neutral demerger under Section 2(19AA) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, with no shares issued as consideration since SCL already owns SFL fully, and NCD holders of SFL receiving one NCD of SCL for every one held on identical coupon, tenure, ISIN, redemption price, quantum and security.

Nothing in the supplied text describes how management first raised the idea publicly or how it changed.
