verdict.rationale: The supplied texts do not state a rationale for separating any business, and no business separation is described in them at all. The "CALL PASSAGES" section provided is empty — there are zero earnings-call excerpts to draw on — so nothing can be attributed to management about a demerger, the businesses involved, any numbers cited, problems solved, or requests from investors, lenders or partners. The one document with content is a truncated NCLT Chandigarh Bench order in CP(CAA) No. 32/Chd/Hry/2025, and it concerns a Scheme of Amalgamation (a merger of a Transferor Company into a Transferee Company between entities under common control, accounted for under the Pooling of Interest Method per Appendix C of Ind AS 103), not a spin-off or separation. That order explicitly declines to restate the rationale, noting it "have already been discussed in details in the First Motion Order dated 17.07.2025" — a document not included here. The passage that is included is procedural and liability-focused: board approval on 21.03.2025, first-motion dispensation of shareholder/creditor meetings on 17.07.2025, newspaper notices on 05.08.2025 in Business Standard and Jansatta, and the Official Liquidator's and RD/RoC's reports. The only figures in the text are disputed/contingent liabilities, not business economics: civil cases and consumer dispute claims of Rs. 2,523 lakhs as on March 31, 2025, and a Rs. 139 lakhs Ghaziabad Development Authority infrastructure surcharge demand, plus unquantified Provident Fund exposure from the Supreme Court allowance-inclusion ruling effective April 1, 2019 and open income-tax disputes. Answering the question as asked would require inventing content, so I am reporting the absence instead; the named entities, the segment being separated, and management's stated reasons cannot be established from these texts alone.

verdict.rationale: The supplied texts do not contain a stated rationale for separating a business at Polycab India Ltd. The only separation-adjacent reference is an analyst question on the January 19, 2024 call, where Ashish Jain of Macquarie asked Chirayu Upadhyaya 'why even we are now thinking of restructuring the business' in the FMEG (fast-moving electrical goods) segment, pairing it with a question on the sharp ramp-up in advertising cost that quarter and suggesting the next two to three quarters could be 'a lost opportunity.' Management did not confirm, describe or justify any separation, demerger or carve-out in reply; Upadhyaya only addressed the advertising point, saying A&P spend is not for FMEG alone but is also spent 'widely for the wires business,' and that branding cannot be stopped for a year and restarted at will. The only other operational detail given was on asset fungibility: the optical fibre cable (OFC) facility and the export-cable facility are dedicated and not fungible, while domestic cables have 'better fungibility' — a constraint discussed in a capacity-addition context, not as a reason to separate anything. The documents labelled as the scheme filing are not a separation rationale at all: one pair is a Regulation 30 disclosure dated October 07, 2026 that the NCLT Ahmedabad Bench admitted a Section 9 IBC petition by Asier Metals Private Limited against Polycab over an alleged operational debt of ₹2.79 crore (C.P. (IB) No. 273/9/AHM/2026), which the company says it will appeal at NCLAT as a commercial dispute, noting zero debt, net cash above Rs.4,000 crores and net-worth of Rs.11,682 crores as at 31st March 2026. The other two are disclosures on a Scheme of Amalgamation — a consolidation in the opposite direction, merging wholly-owned subsidiary Uniglobus Electricals and Electronics Private Limited into Polycab, approved by NCLT on February 27, 2026 and effective March 27, 2026. No business being separated is named, no scheme rationale clause, no entity structure, no swap ratio, no financials of a separated unit, and no mention of investors, lenders or partners requesting it appear anywhere in these texts.
verdict.evolution: Only one call passage was supplied (January 19, 2024), not three years, so no call-by-call evolution can be traced. In that single call the idea of FMEG 'restructuring' surfaced solely as an analyst premise from Macquarie's Ashish Jain and was left unaddressed by management, which pivoted to advertising spend. The later filings (February 28 and March 27, 2026) move the opposite way, completing the amalgamation of Uniglobus into Polycab, and the October 07, 2026 filing concerns an IBC admission, so nothing in the record shows a separation plan forming or changing.

verdict.rationale: The premise of the question cannot be supported by the supplied texts: no earnings-call passages were provided (the "CALL PASSAGES" section is empty), and the only document supplied — the NCLT order in CP (CAA)-33(ND)/2026, dated 24.09.2026 — describes a Composite Scheme of Amalgamation, i.e. Dabur India Ltd. (the Transferee Company) absorbing a transferor company referred to as "Sesa", not Dabur separating or demerging a business. The rationale as stated by the Petitioners is combinative, not separative: Dabur is "a market leader in the hair oil category" while Sesa is "a leading brand with strong recall and 3rd position in the ayurvedic hair oil category", and the deal brings a premium ayurveda-credentialed brand into "a key whitespace in its current hair oil portfolio", strengthening Dabur's hair care presence and taking Sesa's ayurvedic hair care range to a wider consumer base domestically and internationally. Growth of the combined entity in hair oil is to be driven by Dabur's advanced supply chain capabilities, extensive distribution network, deep category knowledge, market research abilities, technical engineering and access to key international markets, with synergies from pooling financial, managerial, technical, distribution and marketing resources. Financially, the Petitioners cite "greater efficiency with better control in cash and debt management of the combined entity and unfettered access to cash flow generated by the combined businesses", enabling more efficient utilisation of capital in one entity, plus "optimisation of costs, coordination and streamlining of day-to-day operations". Mechanics in the text: Appointed Date 01.04.2026; share exchange of 10 equity shares of Dabur of ₹1 each for every 433 0.001% cumulative redeemable preference shares of the Transferor of ₹10 each, per the Finvox Analytics valuation report dated 24.05.2025; equity shareholders approved with 1,342 holders (97.742% of those voting) and 99.999% by value in favour against 31 holders holding 11,112 shares, and all 57 unsecured creditors (₹9,01,17,79,799) voted in favour. No management explanation of a business separation exists in these texts, so none is reconstructed here.

verdict.rationale: On these texts alone, there is no stated rationale for separating a business — the documents describe the opposite transaction plus one unrelated operational 'carve-out'. The Jan 2026 filing is a cover letter for a joint call on 'announcement of merger through a Scheme of Arrangement involving Sapphire Foods India Limited ("Transferor Company"), Devyani International Limited ("Transferee Company")' — an amalgamation of Sapphire into Devyani, not a demerger, and the transcript body itself is truncated before any management reasoning is given. The only 'carve out' language anywhere is operational, from the May 2025 call, where CFO Manish Dawar explained how KFC can still earn roughly 20% restaurant operating margin at about Rs.105k ADS: new KFC openings had cannibalised existing stores, so Devyani is resizing formats, carving physical space inside KFC stores for 'newer brands, which are very small kiosk type of formats', and saying 'These brands will be independent' — independence of brand/format within a store, with no mention of a legal entity, scheme, or shareholder event. Supporting margin levers he cited were format change, labour and overhead synergies if ADS stays soft, and continuous landlord rent negotiation. The so-called scheme rationale text supplied is not a rationale at all: it is the NSE observation letter and BSE letter of June 12, 2026 conveying SEBI's comments and 'No objection' under Regulation 37, which merely *require* the companies to disclose 'The rationale and objectives underlying the proposed scheme' to shareholders — the rationale is demanded, never stated. The only shareholder-structure specifics given are a separate SFIL Secondary Sale of up to 5,94,55,837 equity shares, up to 18.5% of Sapphire's share capital as of December 31, 2025, from Sapphire Foods Mauritius Limited to Arctic International Limited, promoter/promoter-group entities of Sapphire and Devyani 'intending to be reclassified in the Public Category in Devyani', and a condition that the scheme be expressly subject to Competition Commission of India approval before NCLT filing.
verdict.evolution: May 2025: carve-out appears only as a store-level idea — space inside cannibalised KFC stores for small kiosk-format 'independent' brands, as one lever to defend ~20% ROM at ~Rs.105k ADS. January 6, 2026 (transcript filed January 13, 2026): the corporate action announced is a merger, Sapphire Foods as transferor into Devyani as transferee, with the SFIL Secondary Sale of up to 18.5% of Sapphire measured as of December 31, 2025 sitting alongside it. June 12, 2026: NSE and BSE issue Regulation 37 observation/no-objection letters adding CCI approval as a pre-NCLT condition and ordering disclosure of the rationale, cost-benefit analysis, valuation methods and promoter reclassification. Across the three documents the direction of travel is consolidation plus promoter reclassification, not separation.

verdict.rationale: On the evidence supplied, the separation is a holding-company clean-up of the GFL Group rather than an operating-business carve-out: a composite scheme of arrangement among Inox Leasing and Finance Limited (ILFL, the listed/NBFC holding vehicle), Inox Holdings and Investments Limited (IHIL) and Gujarat Fluorochemicals Limited (GFL/GFCL). Management's stated reason, given by Group CFO Akhil Jindal on the Dec 2024 call, is to 'make it a clean structure' so that ownership of GFCL passes directly into the hands of the ultimate shareholders, the promoters, and so that GFCL's holding company ends up 'just holding the GFCL assets rather than the combined' pool of unrelated assets it holds today. The mechanics in the filing match that: ILFL's demerged undertaking — explicitly including its mutual fund distribution activities and the brokerage income generated thereon (clarified by ILFL and IHIL board resolutions dated March 25, 2026) — goes to IHIL, ILFL's remaining assets and liabilities are transferred into GFL, and ILFL is to surrender its NBFC certificate, i.e. the financial-services and investment activities are stripped away from the fluorochemicals asset. A separate perimeter point was clarified on the same call: the existing Fluoropolymers business GFCL reports does not form part of GFCL EV (the EV/battery-materials entity), so fluoropolymers stays with GFCL. The investor-side motive was voiced by Ketan Gandhi of Gandhi Securities, who framed it as unlocking value 'after 20 years' for minority shareholders of the holding company and praised management for doing a demerger that 'takes care of their loyal shareholders'; management did not dispute that framing. Notably, no financial quantification was offered in any of the supplied text — management cited no revenue, EBITDA, capital, holding-company discount or value-unlock numbers. The scheme document supplied is in fact a BSE/NSE observation letter, in which 'the rationale and objectives underlying the proposed scheme' appears only as item (b) on a list of disclosures the exchanges require GFL to make, alongside a cost-benefit analysis, valuation/fairness-opinion details, promoter reclassification for GFL, and any lender-imposed conditions — so the company's own written rationale is requested there, not stated.
verdict.evolution: Only one call passage is supplied, Dec 2024, where the idea is already a live, announced plan: an analyst (Rohit Nagraj) asks a perimeter question confirming Fluoropolymers sits outside GFCL EV, a shareholder (Ketan Gandhi) thanks management for the holding-company restructuring and asks about the Wind business leg, and Akhil Jindal restates the goal as a clean structure with promoters owning GFCL directly. The filing trail then shows the process grinding through regulators: NSE's reference letter to SEBI dated February 18, 2025, ILFL/IHIL clarificatory board resolutions on March 25, 2026 pulling mutual-fund distribution and brokerage income explicitly into the demerged undertaking, SEBI's comments on July 08, 2026 and NSE's observation letter (ref NSE/LIST/45331) on July 09, 2026 with six months' validity to file at NCLT. So the only visible change over time is a narrowing/clarification of what exactly leaves ILFL, not a change of rationale.

verdict.rationale: The supplied texts do not describe a separation at all — they describe the opposite: an amalgamation (merger) of a wholly owned subsidiary into Godrej Properties Limited, and no demerger, spin-off, carve-out or business separation appears anywhere in them. In the NCLT Mumbai filing (CP(CAA)/25/MB/2026 c/w CA(CAA)/268/MB/2025), the Transferee Company is Godrej Properties Limited, listed on BSE and NSE, and the Transferor Company is Embellish Houses Private Limited (CIN U116810OMH2025PTC460029), incorporated on 31 October 2025 upon conversion of Embellish Houses LLP; both are stated to be 'engaged in the business of real estate development and other related activities.' The stated rationale is purely consolidation and housekeeping: consolidation of the real estate business because of 'several commonalities and synergistic linkages' yielding operational efficiency; a streamlined group structure with fewer legal entities and less multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances; pooling of technical resources, personnel, capabilities, skills and expertise for optimum use of infrastructure and cost reduction; administrative and operational convenience with elimination of duplicated communication and coordination; rationalising costs by eliminating multiple record-keeping and administrative functions; and reduced time and effort to consolidate financials at group level. Because the Transferor is a wholly owned subsidiary, no shares are issued as consideration and its shares are cancelled, so there is no swap ratio, no value unlocking for shareholders and no new listed entity — mechanically incompatible with a separation thesis. The filing gives an Appointed Date of 1 November 2025 (the text also garbles this once as '07sf November 2025'), an Effective Date tied to filing the certified NCLT order with the ROC Mumbai, and records the Regional Director (WR) report dated 29.04.2026 with routine observations only (creditor and employee protection, Section 232(3)(i) fees, Ind AS 103/AS 14 accounting entries, income tax and GST compliance, stock exchange filing for disclosure since the subsidiary is wholly owned, and two ROC complaints against GPL — SRN J00036911, closed, and Anil Kumar Poddar's SRN 100057751 — both stated not to pertain to the Scheme). The only earnings-call passage provided, from May 2025, contains no separation discussion whatsoever: it is a capital-deployment and guidance answer in which management cites an absolute net debt cap, FY26 collections guidance of Rs. 21,000 crores ('40% higher than our last year's guidance and 20% higher than actuals'), expected healthy operating cash flows whose post-business-development positivity depends on how much business development is done, and Pirojsha Godrej's comment that 'a lot of value unlocking can happen for the business by sustaining the kind of rapid growth we have seen' alongside high imputed returns on equity and capital — i.e., value unlocking through organic growth, not through separating a business.
verdict.evolution: Only one call excerpt was supplied (May 2025), and in it the separation idea never surfaces: the discussion is confined to the net debt cap, Rs. 21,000 crores of FY26 collections guidance, business-development pace and 'value unlocking' via sustained growth, with analyst questions from Pritesh Sheth and Parvez Qazi on cash flows and FY25 sales mix. There is therefore no call-by-call arc to trace, and no earlier or later call in which the proposal is first floated, debated or refined. The only corporate-action document is the amalgamation Scheme, whose timeline runs from the Transferor's incorporation on 31 October 2025 and Appointed Date of 1 November 2025 through the Regional Director's report of 29.04.2026 and the pending NCLT Mumbai petition. On these texts alone, the plan did not evolve from a separation into anything — the separation premise is unsupported and the actual transaction is a consolidation.

verdict.rationale: Management frames the separation not as a financial restructuring but as an identity and speed problem: over the last two years Intellect curated two parallel architectural disruptions — eMACH.ai, its composable open-finance platform, and Purple Fabric, its Business Impact AI / Enterprise Intelligence Operating System — and concluded that the 'intrinsic DNA' of the two is 'completely different', so running them inside one structure was constraining both. The trigger cited is market timing: the enterprise AI market is at an inflection point, 'moving rapidly from AI experimentation to scaled, enterprise-wide deployment', which management says makes this the optimal moment to give Purple Fabric an independent identity. The stated problems the carve-out solves are shared/contested resources, lack of freedom and lack of agility; the carve-out gives the new Line of Business 'dedicated resources, freedom, and agility' to accelerate growth and 'curate its own destiny' in the Business Impact AI market. A second, explicitly cultural rationale is organizational design: Purple Fabric is to be an organization in 'flow' — young talent, boundaryless thinking, fluidity — abandoning traditional hierarchy for a networked 'Leadership Circle' model with micro-team, high-speed DNA, which management implies cannot be built inside Intellect's existing structure. Governance is set up accordingly: Deepak Dastrala becomes CEO and Business Head of Purple Fabric, reporting directly to Chairman and Managing Director Arun Jain, joining the Intellect Management Council as Senior Management Personnel, with Arun Jain continuing to mentor him and his leadership circle. The traction numbers offered as justification that Purple Fabric can stand alone are 45+ clients live, a 95%+ accuracy SLA for high-stakes financial workflows where minor errors have 'catastrophic consequences', an 18-layer architecture integrating hundreds of enterprise technologies, and 550 domain-aware agents for multi-agent orchestration. Arun Jain positions the two businesses as complementary rather than overlapping — eMACH.ai as 'foundational architecture', Purple Fabric as the 'critical cognitive intelligence' layer — and justifies the split by the scale of the prize, 'a massive long-term opportunity for value creation'. Note: no earnings call passages were supplied with this request, so the entire reconstruction rests on this single filing/announcement text.
verdict.evolution: No earnings call passages were included in the material provided, so no call-by-call evolution can be traced and no call dates are available. The structure announced is an independent Line of Business with its own CEO, not a described legal demerger, share-swap or listing, so whether the plan changed over time cannot be established from these texts.

verdict.rationale: On the texts supplied, there is no separation to explain: the "CALL PASSAGES" section is empty (no earnings-call extracts were provided), and the document labelled "scheme rationale" is not a scheme of arrangement at all but a Regulation 30 intimation dated March 10, 2026 about the completion of a voluntary liquidation. The subject is Suburban Diagnostics (India) Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary incorporated on June 6, 2002, registered at Andheri (West), Mumbai, which operated pathology and diagnostics centres in Maharashtra. The transaction described runs in the opposite direction to a separation: Suburban's entire business undertaking was distributed by the liquidator to the parent, so that "the entire business operations of Suburban stands consolidated with the Company with effect from close of business hours on March 18, 2025" — i.e. a corporate-structure simplification that folds a subsidiary's diagnostics business into Dr. Lal PathLabs Limited and then dissolves the empty shell. The only quantification given is scale, not rationale: as on March 31, 2024 Suburban's turnover was INR 164.03 crore (7.37% of consolidated) and net worth INR 126.62 crore (7.05%). The process was solvent and debt-free by declaration — the directors declared under Section 59(3)(a) that the company "has no debt or will be able to pay its debts in full from the proceeds of its assets" — so no lender, investor or partner is identified anywhere as having asked for it. The filing explicitly disclaims the forms a separation would take: no sale agreement ("Not Applicable"), no buyer, no related-party transaction, and "Voluntary liquidation is not a sale of undertaking" / "not a slump sale". Accordingly no management rationale for separating a business — no business names on either side, no margin, capital, valuation or focus argument, no investor demand — can be reconstructed from these texts, and I will not supply one from memory.

verdict.rationale: The supplied filing text does not describe a separation at all — it is the rationale for an amalgamation (merger) of IAC International Automotive India Private Limited (the "Transferor Company"), a wholly owned subsidiary, into Lumax Auto Technologies Limited (the "Transferee Company"), whose described activities span lighting solutions, moulded parts and frame chassis plus trading of accessories for the automotive industry. Management's stated reasons are: to achieve greater integration, greater financial strength and flexibility and to maximize overall shareholder value; to achieve cost savings from more focused operational efforts, rationalization, standardization and simplification of business processes, productivity improvements and rationalization of administrative expenses; and to obtain operational synergies, greater productivity and economical operations for future growth of the Transferee Company. The filing also cites pooling of managerial, technical and financial resources to increase competitiveness, economies of scale with reduction in overheads (administrative, managerial and other expenditure), organizational efficiency and optimal utilization of funds and resources, and a significant reduction in the multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances currently borne by two entities. Mechanically it is a cashless, no-new-shares transaction: all equity shares of the Transferor held by the Transferee (directly or through nominees, including single shares held by Mr. Anmol Jain, Mr. Deepak Jain, Mr. Sanjay Mehta, Mr. Vikas Marwah, Mr. Raajesh Kumar Gupta and Mr. Naval Khanna) stand cancelled, and the Transferor's 10,08,459 equity shares and 1,30,207 preference shares go to nil. LATL's shareholding pattern is unchanged pre- and post-arrangement: promoters 3,81,54,430 shares / 55.98%, public 3,00,03,275 / 44.02%, total 6,81,57,705 / 100.00%. The same filing carries two unrelated Regulation 30 disclosures: an investment of up to Rs. 5 crores in Optionally Convertible Redeemable Debentures of wholly owned subsidiary Lumax Resources Private Limited (Rs. 10 face value, 0.01% p.a. coupon, 10-year tenure, 1:1 mandatory conversion at expiry, annual interest, related-party but at arm's length), and a proposed Rs. 0.93 crores (approx.) investment in Power Pulse Trading Solutions Limited, an Independent Power Producer in renewable energy (net worth Rs. 9,188.43 lakhs, PAT Rs. 1,190.18 lakhs, turnover Rs. 1,198.88 lakhs), done purely to qualify LATL as a captive user under the Electricity Act, 2003 and Electricity Rules, 2005 for solar power, with no major impact on the listed entity and completion indicated in about 3 months, for cash and no related-party interest. No business is identified as being separated, demerged or spun off anywhere in the provided text.

verdict.rationale: The texts provided do not describe a separation at all — the only rationale document supplied is a Scheme of Amalgamation (NCLT New Delhi, C.A. (CAA) No. 62/ND/2025, order dated 07.04.2026), in which four wholly-owned subsidiaries (Transferor Companies No. 1 to 4, unnamed in the truncated filing) are merged INTO the parent (the Transferee Company, identified only by its 1,93,534 equity shareholders as on 31.03.2025, consistent with the listed parent). The boards of all five companies approved it unanimously by resolutions dated 05.02.2025, with an appointed date of 1st April 2025 or such other date as the NCLT may direct. The stated reasons are purely structural consolidation, not divestiture: because all transferors are wholly owned subsidiaries, the group wants to simplify and streamline the corporate structure by reducing the number of legal entities, eliminating corporate redundancies such as duplicated administrative work, duplicate corporate-governance work streams, and multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances with their associated costs. It further cites pooling of the transferors' resources with the parent's, greater efficiency in managing the cash balances presently available with the companies plus access to the cash flows generated by the combined business, and greater management focus and control over the combined operations. No business lines, revenue, margin, headcount or valuation figures are cited anywhere in the supplied text; the only numbers are stakeholder counts used to dispense with meetings — Transferor 1: 2 equity shareholders and 2 CCD holders; Transferors 2, 3 and 4: 7 equity shareholders each, with 1 debenture holder, 1 preference shareholder and 1 debenture holder respectively; all four with nil secured and nil unsecured creditors; the parent with 3 secured and 37 unsecured creditors. No investor, lender or partner is identified as having asked for the transaction; the filing says no shares will be issued and no arrangement or compromise is proposed with the parent's shareholders or creditors, so their rights are unaffected. Critically, the 'CALL PASSAGES' section of the prompt is empty — zero earnings-call text was supplied — so management's own spoken rationale, the business being separated, and any cited numbers cannot be reconstructed from these texts.
verdict.evolution: No evolution can be traced: the prompt's 'CALL PASSAGES' section contains no passages, so there are no call dates, no first mention, and no change in the plan to report. The only datable steps inside the supplied filing are the board resolutions of 05.02.2025, the 1st April 2025 appointed date, the 31.03.2025 shareholder/creditor cut-off, and the NCLT order dated 07.04.2026. Whether the idea surfaced on a call, and how it changed, is not answerable from these texts.

verdict.rationale: The supplied texts do not actually contain a stated rationale for a separation — they document two separation-adjacent moves without management's reasoning. The only concrete separation described is the hive-off of NTPC's coal mining business into its wholly-owned subsidiary NTPC Mining Limited (NML): a business transfer agreement was signed at an estimated value of ₹10,503 crore, the Chatti Bariatu and Badam mines had already been transferred as of the October 30, 2025 call, and management said it expects to complete transfer of all remaining mines to NML within the current fiscal. The second thread is NTPC Green Energy, raised only as an investor question in the July 2024 call, where Atul Mehra of Motilal Oswal Asset Management asked whether NTPC would do a 'full-fledged demerger' of NTPC Green or keep it substantially held by NTPC with only a minority offloaded in the IPO — the passage ends before any management answer is given. Critically, the document labelled 'scheme rationale' is not a demerger scheme at all: it is a Regulation 30 intimation dated 28th November 2025 that the NCLT, Delhi approved the resolution plan of the NTPC–MAHAGENCO consortium for Sinnar Thermal Power Limited, a 5x270 MW (1,350 MW) coal-based plant at Sinnar, Nashik, Maharashtra, under CIRP per the IBC — an acquisition, not a separation. So on these texts the structure is: coal mining carved into NML by business transfer at ₹10,503 crore, renewables housed in NTPC Green with an IPO, and no articulated problem being solved, no lender or partner demand, and no margin, capital-allocation or valuation argument on record. Any claim about why NTPC is separating the business would have to come from outside these passages.
verdict.evolution: July 2024: the idea appears only from the buy side — an analyst (Motilal Oswal AM) presses on whether NTPC Green will be a full demerger or just a minority IPO stake sale; the passage carries no management reply. By the call dated October 30, 2025 (tagged Nov 2025), the coal mining hive-off is already executed rather than debated: the business transfer agreement to NTPC Mining Limited is signed at ₹10,503 crore, Chatti Bariatu and Badam are transferred, and the rest are guided to move within the fiscal. The 28th November 2025 filing adds nothing to the separation story, as it concerns the Sinnar Thermal acquisition via CIRP. There is no call in between that explains the shift from investor question to executed carve-out.

verdict.rationale: The supplied texts do not describe a separation: the only filing text provided is the rationale for a Scheme of Amalgamation (a merger), in which Transferor Company 1 and Transferor Company 2 are absorbed into the Transferee Company, and no earnings-call passages were included at all (the CALL PASSAGES section is empty), so nothing here can be attributed to management on a call. The stated reasoning is wholly consolidation logic: the two transferors are 'engaged in the similar line of business' as the transferee, so merging is said to improve operational capabilities and market competitiveness, enrich the combined product offerings and expand the customer base locally and globally. The filing cites optimum use of infrastructure, cost reduction and efficiencies, productivity gains, logistics advantages, lower administrative and operational costs, and a reduction in the number of legal entities; it also cites pooling of assets, intellectual property, technical know-how, trade secrets and brands, and combining distribution and marketing resources. A specific aim is creating an integrated value chain to raise the degree of vertical integration in the products segment, plus greater efficiency in cash and debt management with 'unfettered access to cash flow generated by the combined business' for better capital deployment and debt management. Governance motives are explicit: simplified management structure and strategic focus, elimination of duplication and multiplicity of compliance requirements, and better control over the business and financial conduct of the Transferee Company. The only hard numbers in the excerpt are the reclassified authorised capital (33,00,10,000 equity shares of Rs.10 each = Rs. 3,30,01,00,000 plus 50,00,000 preference shares of Rs.10 each = Rs. 5,00,00,000, total Rs. 3,35,01,00,000) and unsecured creditors as on 31st March 2026 — Transferee 955 creditors / Rs. 537,88,23,955; Transferor 1 192 creditors / Rs. 14,75,57,745; Transferor 2 56 creditors / Rs. 77,45,460. Structurally, Transferor Company 2 is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Transferee, while Transferor Company 1's promoters are already part of the Transferee's promoter group, so new shares issued under the Scheme only adjust their shareholding proportionately with no new promoter designated. No business, segment, product or company is named anywhere in the provided text, PRIVISCL included, and no party is identified as having asked for the transaction.
verdict.evolution: No call passages were provided, so the idea's origin and evolution cannot be traced and no call dates exist in the source. The only datable facts in the filing excerpt are the creditor positions stated as on 31st March 2026 and an authorised-capital reclassification implied to accompany the Scheme. Whether the structure changed over time, and from what, is not shown in these texts.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is Reliance's FMCG/consumer-brands arm. Under a composite scheme of arrangement among Reliance Retail Limited, Reliance Retail Ventures Limited (RRVL), the old Reliance Consumer Products Limited (RCPL) and Tira Beauty Limited (renamed Reliance Consumer Products Limited, 'New RCPL'), the 'Consumer Brands Business Undertaking' was demerged out of RRVL effective 1 December 2025; the old RCPL stood dissolved, RRVL shareholders received 1 New RCPL share of Rs.10 for every 2 RRVL shares of Rs.10, New RCPL's pre-scheme capital held by RRVL was cancelled without consideration, and RCPL became an 83.56% DIRECT subsidiary of RIL instead of sitting under retail — confirmed on the Jan 2026 call ('RCPL became the direct subsidiary of RIL from 1st December 2025'). The only explicit rationale management gave is organisational focus and growth speed: the 16 January 2026 media release said the consumer products vertical, 'ranging from classic Indian brands to new age labels,' is 'progressing on its accelerated growth trajectory with a focused organizational structure.' Everything else they offered was scale and investment facts that imply the logic: FMCG revenue of Rs.5,000 cr in Q3 FY26 (+60% Y-o-Y), Rs.15,000 cr for 9M FY26, Rs.22,000 cr for FY26 and Rs.7,350 cr in Q4 FY26 (both ~2x), Campa at Rs.4,700 cr (4th largest CSD brand), Independence at Rs.2,600 cr, #3 water player, Rs.8,600 cr in Q1 FY27 (2x, beverages Rs.2,900 cr, daily essentials Rs.3,200 cr, #3 NARTD), 5,000+ distributors, 3 million outlets, >80% of sales through external channels, 40 export markets, 12 plants plus integrated food parks and an acquisition run (Udhaiyam, Manna, Goodness Group, Sosyo majority, Brylcreem, Toni & Guy, Badedas, Matey) — i.e. a heavy-capex, acquisitive, breakeven-EBITDA business ('yes, we are breakeven on EBITDA terms') chasing Rs.1 lakh crore by FY2030, run through third-party general trade, which fits poorly inside a ~7.9-8.0% margin omni-channel retailer. The visible consequence management kept quantifying was the drag it removes from retail's reported growth: Q4 FY26 retail growth of 11% was 'almost 14%' adjusted for the demerger, and Q1 FY27 was 7.4% reported versus 11.6% underlying. No investor, lender or partner was named as having asked for it — the scheme was presented as done, and analysts (Harit Kapoor, Vikash Jain, Percy Panthaki) only pressed afterwards for the like-for-like revenue and EBITDA impact, which Dinesh Taluja deferred ('It is a number which is going out. It is a number as well... We will have to wait for the next quarter'). Two parallel separation tracks run alongside it: the Jio Platforms IPO (fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares, DRHP 19 June 2026, SEBI observation letter 28 August 2026, RHP 14 October 2026, priced at Rs.1,119 on 24 October 2026, with Rs.2,500 cr reserved for individual/HUF RIL shareholders and Rs.500 cr for employees), and the ring-fencing of AI/data-centre capex into RIL/'Reliance Intelligence' with JPL kept asset-light ('the AI data centers are not being done in Jio Platforms Limited').
verdict.evolution: On the Oct 2024 call the consumer-brands business was still reported inside Reliance Retail as a line item ('general trade revenues are growing at 250% plus'), with no hint of a separation. By the Jan 2026 call (16 Jan 2026) it was presented as a completed fact — 'the demerger happened on 1st December' — RCPL had become a direct RIL subsidiary, got its own presenter (Ketan Mody) and its own revenue disclosure, and the same-day media release supplied the only stated reason: 'a focused organizational structure' and an 'accelerated growth trajectory.' On the Apr 2026 and Jul 2026 calls the demerger appeared only as a base adjustment to retail growth (11% reported vs ~14% adjusted; 7.4% vs 11.6%), while RCPL's own disclosure escalated to Rs.22,000 cr FY26 revenue, EBITDA breakeven and a Rs.1 lakh crore FY2030 target. In parallel, the Jio Platforms listing moved from 'imminent' and 'awaiting the new notification from the government' (Jan/Apr 2026) to DRHP on 19 June 2026 and pricing at Rs.1,119 on 24 October 2026.

verdict.what_management_expects: For RCPL: a focused structure and accelerated growth — 2x revenue run-rate toward Rs.1 lakh crore by FY2030, margin improving from EBITDA breakeven as food parks, beverage lines and distribution (5,000 distributors, 3m outlets) scale. For retail: cleaner reported growth (11.6% vs 7.4%) and undiluted focus on omni-channel/hyperlocal.
