verdict.what_is_spun: Cyient Semiconductor — the semiconductor business, to be given an independent capital structure and value
verdict.reason: To establish an independent value for Cyient Semiconductor because management believes there is a huge/significant value unlock available, and to raise the money the business needs
verdict.insiders: not stated for the new entity; in the parent buyback, promoters, promoter group and persons in control declared their intention not to participate, so their stake rises
verdict.hidden_value: Management says significant value unlock is available in Cyient Semiconductor that the parent price does not reflect; separately Cyient is buying back 5.76% at INR 1,125 (INR 720 crore), and DLM's established value accrues to Cyient holders indirectly
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Documents describe raising capital to establish independent value, not a share distribution; no size, listing or index detail stated
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated — the Apr 2026 call says only that Cyient Semiconductor will 'raise the money' to establish an independent value; no listing date is given
verdict.read_next: The Cyient Semiconductor capital-raise disclosure: valuation, stake sold, and whether a listing or demerger scheme follows
verdict.quote: Now for Cyient Semiconductor, I think we want to establish an independent value because we believe there is a huge value unlock in Cyient Semiconductor.

verdict.rationale: The separation in question is the carve-out of Cyient's Semiconductor business (turnkey ASIC) out of the parent into a dedicated entity, Cyient Semiconductor — not a demerger of Cyient DLM, which management explicitly declined to separate further. Management's stated logic (July 25, 2024 call, tagged Aug 2024) was that Cyient already had a rare end-to-end semiconductor capability — it can "design these chips, ... fabricate these chips, test these chips, prototype these chips and sell these chips" by leveraging design, FAB, OSAT and testing — and that in a market shifting to analog/sensory-to-digital chips, this deserved a business that could "exclusively and dedicatedly focus on turnkey ASIC" rather than sit inside a services P&L. The explicit template was Cyient DLM: the opportunity was framed "along the lines with the value unlock of Cyient DLM," i.e. a separate structure with its own capital and its own independently established value. The Board approved the spin-off into a different entity (May 2025 call), a dedicated CEO was hired (Suman Narayan for Cyient Semiconductor; Sukamal Banerjee became CEO for the DET business), and by the Jul 2025 call the carve-out was "completed as planned," with the group moving to four reported segments — DET, Semiconductor (a separate subsidiary "with its own leaders, with its own management and with its own structure"), DLM and Others — and DET numbers restated to exclude Semiconductor so the core services business could be judged like-for-like. The problem being solved is structural mismatch: Semiconductor is to be "run as a start-up investment positioned for accelerated growth," which needs capital and risk tolerance that would otherwise dilute the parent's margin and growth optics. The demand side was cited as external pull — "significant interest in the business from our customers, our partners and investors" — with order intake in the first post-carve-out quarter exceeding budget by about 10%. By Apr 2026 the financing was explicitly bifurcated: a buyback at the Cyient level (the Board judging it the right time given capital requirements and where the share price "is and has been") versus a separate fundraise at Cyient Semiconductor to "establish an independent value," sized not large but enough to carry it to breakeven, expected towards the end of a period the transcript cuts off. In Jul 2026, asked by ChrysCapital for a clean DLM demerger, Krishna Bodanapu refused on operating grounds — DLM and Cyient are mutually dependent, engineering deals are won because of the manufacturing capability — confirming that separation is applied only where there is no such interdependence.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced on the Aug 2024 (July 25, 2024) call as an intention to create a separate turnkey-ASIC business, pitched explicitly as a repeat of the Cyient DLM value unlock. The Feb 2025 call did not advance the separation — it was about internal sales/performance re-engineering (a new large-deal function, a performance framework rewarding revenue and margin growth, 13 large deals in Q3). By May 2025 Board approval for the spin-off was in hand and Suman Narayan was named CEO of Cyient Semiconductor alongside Sukamal Banerjee taking over DET; the Jul 2025 call declared the carve-out complete, introduced four-segment reporting with DET restated ex-Semiconductor, and reported order intake ~10% above budget. Apr 2026 moved it to the capital stage — a Cyient-level buyback alongside a separate Cyient Semiconductor fundraise to establish independent value and fund the path to breakeven — while Jul 2026 drew the boundary by ruling out a DLM demerger for now.

points.point: First articulation of the separation: Cyient already has end-to-end turnkey ASIC capability (design, fabricate, test, prototype, sell) and wants a dedicated business for it, explicitly modelled on the Cyient DLM value unlock.
points.quote: We already have this ability within Cyient to provide an end to end service offering for these turnkey chip design and now we believe that there is a significant opportunity along the lines with the value unlock of Cyient DLM to actually create a separate business that can exclusively and dedicatedly focus on turnkey ASIC .

points.point: Differentiation argument for a standalone semiconductor entity: amid India's FAB and OSAT announcements, Cyient claims to be one of few players spanning design, FAB, OSAT and testing, serving chips that convert real-world analog/sensory signals to digital.
points.quote: You may have also seen a number of announcements that have been made in the last couple of months on va rious elements of Cyient Limited July 25, 2024 Page 3 of 18 semiconductor, be it semiconductor FABs or semiconductor OSATs , but we believe that we are one of the few and unique companies that are able to provide an end to end solution by leveraging various capabilities including design FAB, OSAT, testing etc.

points.point: No separation update on this call; the structural change discussed was internal — a new dedicated large-deal function supporting sales leaders, plus a performance framework rewarding revenue and margin growth over status quo.
points.quote: We now have a large steel team working supporting the current sales leaders and sales managers to construct a deal from what we were doing previously , especially as we move towards the selling of technology in a cons ultative model.

points.point: Management framed the gap as 'what we are selling' rather than portfolio structure — the market wanted more technology-driven solutions — and cited 13 large deals signed in Q3 as early evidence of the new discipline.
points.quote: And the 13 large deals that we have signed in Q3 is also probably it is a little bit early to take it as a trend but also is a good reflection of the focus that we were able to bring into that discipline and to carve out larger deals than what we were doing before.

points.point: Board approval obtained to spin off Semiconductor as a separate entity, with Suman Narayan appointed CEO of Cyient Semiconductor for his track record of scaling semiconductor organizations.
points.quote: As you know, we got the permission or we got the approval from the Board to spin off the semiconductor business as a different entity.

points.point: Parallel leadership separation on the core side: Sukamal Banerjee takes over as CEO with DET presented as a diversified platform not dependent on any single industry, geography or capability.
points.quote: We are not dependent on any single industry, any single geography, any single capability.

points.point: Carve-out declared complete as planned, with Semiconductor to be run as a start-up investment positioned for accelerated growth on the strength of IP, domain expertise, global talent and customer relationships.
points.quote: Coming to the highlights for this quarter , It is my pleasure to announce that the Semiconductor business carve out process is completed as planned.

points.point: Reporting consequence: four segments — DET, Semiconductor as a separate subsidiary with its own leadership and structure, DLM, and Others — with DET restated like-for-like excluding Semiconductor; Semiconductor order intake beat budget by ~10% and drew customer, partner and investor interest.
points.quote: The focus of this call will remain the DET segment, and to that extent, all numbers for the DET segment are like -for-like to the previous period, which means that the numbers have been restated to exclude our Semiconductor business.

points.point: Asked to reconcile a buyback with a simultaneous fundraise, Krishna Bodanapu separated the two: the buyback sits at Cyient (given its capital requirements and the share price level), while the fundraise sits at Cyient Semiconductor to establish an independent value and fund it to breakeven.
points.quote: So the buyback is for Cyient. The fundraise is for Cyient Semiconductor.

points.point: The explicit purpose of raising outside capital in the carved-out entity is price discovery on a value management believes is trapped — a modest raise sized to reach breakeven, timed toward the end of a period the transcript cuts off.
points.quote: Now for Cyient Semiconductor, I think we want to establish an independent value because we believe there is a huge value unlock in Cyient Semiconductor.

points.point: Rajas Joshi of ChrysCapital pushed for a clean DLM demerger as a shareholder value unlock for the main Cyient entity — investor pressure for a second separation.
points.quote: So, as things stand, DLM is a partly owned subsidiary for us and is there a plan for a clean demerger given how things have shaped up over the past few quarters now because that would help with regards to significant value unlock for shareholders in the main Cyient entity ?

points.point: Management declined a DLM demerger on operating-interdependence grounds: engineering deals are won on the back of DLM's manufacturing capability and vice versa, and a separate capital structure was already the intended route to value unlock.
points.quote: Right now, we are still not considering that because there is quite a dependence between DLM and Cyient .

points.point: The supplied filing text contains no scheme-of-arrangement rationale; it is the 3 March 2026 board outcome (Shrinivas Kulkarni, ex-CFO of Cyient DLM who oversaw its 2023 IPO, becomes Cyient CFO from 1 April 2026; Prabhakar Atla moves to COO) plus the 19 June 2026 buyback Letter of Offer — 64,00,000 shares, 5.76% of paid-up capital, INR 1,125 per share, up to INR 720 crore via tender offer, record date 17 June 2026, manager Axis Capital, qualifying for the U.S. Tier I exemption after U.S. holders were determined below 10% as of 22 May 2026.
points.quote: OFFER TO BUY BACK UP TO 64,00,000 (SIXTY FOUR LAKH) FULLY PAID-UP EQUITY SHARES OF FACE VALUE OF INR 5/- (INDIAN RUPEES FIVE ONLY) EACH OF CYIENT LIMITED, REPRESENTING UP TO 5.76% OF THE EXISTING PAID- UP EQUITY SHARE CAPITAL OF THE COMPANY

verdict.what_management_expects: Cyient Semiconductor: a dedicated start-up entity with its own CEO, management and structure, accelerated growth in turnkey ASIC, its own fundraise to reach breakeven, and an independently established value — a 'huge value unlock' mirroring Cyient DLM. Cyient/DET: a clean like-for-like services P&L free of semiconductor investment drag, diversified across industries and geographies, with capital returned via the INR 720 crore buyback.
verdict.gaps: No scheme rationale, swap ratio, shareholder entitlement, listing plan, semiconductor revenue/losses, fundraise size or valuation, breakeven date, or tax and related-party treatment.

verdict.what_is_spun: not stated — the documents describe acquisitions (Swiss Parenterals 30% stake, Velbiom probiotics business), not a demerger
verdict.reason: not stated — no separation is disclosed; the stated objective is "fully consolidating its position, enhancing operational synergy, and strengthening its long-term strategic presence" by acquiring 100% of Swiss
verdict.insiders: No new entity disclosed. Mr. Naishadh Shah, Director of Swiss, allotted 23,06,372 Eris shares (1.69% fully diluted), locked in; no promoter/promoter group interest in the transaction
verdict.hidden_value: not stated. Documents disclose Swiss group turnover of Rs 220.80cr (FY23), Rs 282.97cr (FY24), Rs 351.11cr (FY25), presence in ~80+ countries, valued at Rs 423.30cr for 30%
verdict.selling_pressure_why: No demerger or share distribution in documents; only a locked-in preferential allotment of 1.69% to one acquiree
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated for any demerged entity; the 16 January 2026 filing says only "The aforesaid Subscription Shares shall be listed on the NSE and BSE, upon receipt of the relevant listing approvals"
verdict.read_next: Valuation report of Rashmi Shah dated 24 November 2025 supporting the Rs 423.30 crore Swiss consideration
verdict.quote: Pursuant to the said acquisition, Swiss will become a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.

verdict.rationale: These texts do not describe a separation, demerger or spin-off at all — they describe the opposite, a buy-in and full consolidation, so no separation rationale can be reconstructed from them. The only transaction explained is Eris Lifesciences' acquisition of the remaining 30% of Swiss Parenterals Limited (parenterals, incorporated 4 February 1997, presence in ~80+ countries) from Mr. Naishadh Shah, a Director of Swiss, taking Eris from 70% to 100% so that Swiss becomes a wholly owned subsidiary. The stated objects are 'fully consolidating its position, enhancing operational synergy, and strengthening its long-term strategic presence', with expected benefits of complete managerial control, full financial consolidation, improved cost efficiencies, streamlined governance and enhanced shareholder value. Consideration is INR 423.30 crore, discharged not in cash but by a preferential issue of up to 23,06,372 equity shares of face value Re. 1 at INR 1,835.35 each (premium INR 1,834.35), taking Mr. Shah from nil to 1.69% on a fully diluted basis, priced per Chapter V of the SEBI ICDR Regulations and a valuation report of 24 November 2025 by Rashmi Shah, Independent Registered Valuer (IBBI/RV/06/2018/10240). It is disclosed as a related party transaction (a transaction with a related party of a subsidiary under Regulation 2(zc) of SEBI LODR), stated to be at arm's length, with no promoter/promoter group/group company interest, no governmental or regulatory approvals required, and completion expected before 31 March 2026. The scale cited for Swiss is group-level turnover of INR 220.80 crore (FY2022-23), INR 282.97 crore (FY2023-24) and INR 351.11 crore (FY2024-25). No business is being carved out, no resulting entity is named, no demerger scheme or rationale clause is present, and no party (investor, lender or partner) is identified as having asked for anything.
verdict.evolution: No earnings call passages were supplied — the 'CALL PASSAGES' section is empty, so there is no call-by-call history to trace. The documentary trail runs only across two Regulation 30 intimations: the Board meeting of 24 November 2025 (2:45 PM to 5:30 PM) approving the 30% Swiss acquisition, the share-swap consideration and a postal ballot with a 21 November 2025 cut-off date; and the intimation of 16 January 2026 recording that shareholders approved by postal ballot on 24 December 2025 and that the Board's Executive Committee approved the allotment of the 23,06,372 shares that day. The plan therefore did not change over time in these texts — it moved from board approval to shareholder approval to allotment without alteration, and the filing explicitly records 'None' against any cancellation or termination of the issuance proposal.

points.point: The transaction is a consolidation, not a separation: Eris proposes to move from its existing 70% holding to 100% ownership of Swiss Parenterals, the stated purpose being consolidation of position, operational synergy and long-term strategic presence.
points.quote: With the objective of fully consolidating its position, enhancing operational synergy, and strengthening its long-term strategic presence, the Company now proposes to acquire 100% ownership of Swiss.

points.point: The benefits management lists are control, accounting and governance benefits rather than the focus/valuation arguments typical of a demerger rationale.
points.quote: This consolidation is expected to provide complete managerial control, enable full financial consolidation, improve cost efficiencies, streamline governance, and contribute to enhanced shareholder value.

points.point: End state of the deal: 16,74,493 Swiss shares (30% of its capital) are acquired and Swiss ceases to have a minority partner.
points.quote: Pursuant to the said acquisition, Swiss will become a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: Consideration of INR 423.30 crore is paid in Eris paper rather than cash, via a preferential allotment to the selling Swiss director Mr. Naishadh Shah at INR 1,835.35 per Re. 1 face value share, giving him 1.69% of Eris on a fully diluted basis.
points.quote: The acquisition of 30% stake in Swiss by the Company from Mr. Naishadh Shah is proposed to be undertaken for a total purchase consideration of INR 423,30,00,000 (Indian Rupees Four Hundred and Twenty Three Crores and Thirty Lakhs Only), which will be discharged by the Company by way of issuance of up to 23,06,372 (twenty three lakh six thousand three hundred and seventy two) equity shares of the Company on a preferential basis to Mr. Naishadh Shah

points.point: The deal is flagged as a material related party transaction because Mr. Shah is a Director of the subsidiary Swiss, requiring postal ballot approval; it is asserted to be at arm's length with no promoter interest.
points.quote: The transaction is being undertaken at arms' length.

points.point: Swiss's cited scale and reach: parenterals sold in roughly 80-plus countries, with group-level turnover rising from INR 220.80 crore in FY2022-23 to INR 282.97 crore in FY2023-24 and INR 351.11 crore in FY2024-25; no regulatory approval is needed and closing is targeted before 31 March 2026.
points.quote: Country in which the acquired entity has presence : ~80+ countries

points.point: The second filing (16 January 2026) confirms execution: shareholder consent by postal ballot on 24 December 2025 and allotment of the full 23,06,372 shares at a premium of INR 1,834.35 approved by the Executive Committee of the Board.
points.quote: the Executive Committee of the Board of the Directors of the Company at its meeting held today i.e., January 16, 2026 has approved the allotment of 23,06,372 (Twenty-Three Lakh Six Thousand Three Hundred and Seventy-Two) fully paid-up equity shares of face value of Re. 1 (Indian Rupee One) each

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing is said about any separated entity, because none exists here. For Eris post-consolidation they expect complete managerial control, full financial consolidation of Swiss, improved cost efficiencies, streamlined governance, greater operational synergy, a stronger long-term strategic presence and enhanced shareholder value. No margin, capital-structure, leverage or valuation-multiple expectation is quantified, and no guidance is given on dilution impact from the 1.69% share issuance.
verdict.gaps: No earnings call text was provided and no separation/demerger is described: no carved-out business, resulting entity, swap ratio rationale, requesting investors/lenders/partners, Swiss margins, debt treatment, or dilution/EPS effect.

verdict.quote: In order to simplify and rationalize the group's corporate structure, the companies have undertaken the present Scheme with a view to streamlining the group's legal framework by eliminating multiple entities and consolidating the business operations under a single corporate entity.

verdict.rationale: The texts provided do not support a separation narrative: the CALL PASSAGES section was supplied empty (no earnings-call text at all), and the filing excerpt is a Scheme of Amalgamation, i.e. a combination rather than a separation, demerger or spin-off. In it, two wholly-owned subsidiaries of the listed parent are being merged into their holding company and dissolved: Dealskart Online Services Private Limited (incorporated 8 September 2011, CIN U74140DL2011PTC224819, PAN AADCD9571D), which provides operations and maintenance (O&M) services to the parent's omni-channel stores PAN India, and Lenskart Eyetech Private Limited (incorporated 2 July 2015, CIN U74110DL2015PTC282327, PAN AACCL8854C), which operates training centres for retail staff. The Transferee Company is Lenskart Solutions Limited (originally incorporated 19 May 2008 as Valyoo Technologies Private Limited, renamed on conversion to a public company on 16 June 2025, CIN L33100DL2008PLC178355), a listed entity on NSE and BSE, engaged in designing, manufacturing, branding and retailing eyewear, and the holding company of both transferors. The only stated motive visible in the excerpt is tax and legal form: the scheme is drawn to comply with the conditions for an 'amalgamation' under Section 2(6) of the Income Tax Act, 2025 and other applicable provisions. The structural plumbing is set out as Parts A–E, covering introduction and rationale, share capital, amalgamation of the transferors into the transferee, consideration, accounting treatment and dissolution of the transferors, and general terms. Beyond this, the substantive 'Purpose and Rationale' clauses of Part A are cut off by the truncation, so no synergy, margin, capital, focus, valuation, investor, lender or partner rationale is stated anywhere in the supplied material. No businesses are identified as being separated, and no numbers, demands from investors/lenders/partners, or management commentary of any kind appear in these texts.
verdict.evolution: No evolution can be traced: the prompt's CALL PASSAGES block contains no passages, so there are no call labels or call dates in evidence, and nothing can be attributed to management across three years of calls. The only dated markers in the supplied text are corporate-history dates in the filing — incorporation on 19 May 2008 as Valyoo Technologies Private Limited, the subsidiaries' incorporations on 8 September 2011 and 2 July 2015, and conversion to a public limited company renamed Lenskart Solutions Limited on 16 June 2025. Within the filing itself the proposal appears only in its final form, as an amalgamation of the two wholly-owned subsidiaries into the listed parent.

points.point: The filing is a scheme of amalgamation (two subsidiaries merging into the parent), not a separation, demerger or spin-off; its structure is laid out in five parts, A through E.
points.quote: This Scheme of Amalgamation is divided into the following parts:

points.point: The only motive stated in the visible text is tax/legal form — the scheme is structured to qualify as an 'amalgamation' under Section 2(6) of the Income Tax Act, 2025.
points.quote: in compliance with the conditions relating to “amalgamation” as specified under Section 2( 6) of the Income Tax Act, 2025 and other applicable provisions, if any, of the Income Tax Act, 2025 (the “ IT Act ”).

verdict.rationale: On these texts alone, there is no demerger or spin-off of a pharmaceutical business being explained — the only 'separation' documented is a non-core asset exit: at its July 11, 2026 board meeting Mankind approved divesting 100% of Broadway Hospitality Services Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, to AKRK Projects LLP and Partners for ₹49.00 crore (subject to closing adjustment), to be completed within 90 days, with the stated reason being 'the Company's strategy to divest it's non-core assets'. The size disclosures make the logic plain: Broadway contributed FY26 revenue of ₹9.63 crore (0.07% of the company), total income ₹9.90 crore (0.07%) and net worth ₹38.99 crore (0.24%) — a hospitality business immaterial to a pharma company, sold to a non-promoter, non-related party. The same board approved the opposite leg of the reshaping: a new Netherlands wholly owned subsidiary as an SPV to hold R&D assets and do business development in niche therapies, through joint ventures or strategic interests, with investment of up to EUR 5 million in tranches — i.e. cash out of non-core hospitality, capital into focused R&D/in-licensing. A third, earlier step in the same clean-up was the April 13, 2026 approval to wind up Mankind Pharma Lanka (Private) Limited, a non-operating, non-material Sri Lankan WOS, because 'changed regulatory requirements' made the anticipated business objectives no longer viable. The earnings calls supply the cultural/structural argument rather than any scheme rationale: on Jan 2025 management cited the OTC business as precedent, where they corrected practices by 'hiving off', cutting the number of distributors and bringing in outside talent so one leader no longer ran OTC and pharma together, after which growth improved, and said 80–90% of the analogous changes in the Mankind Pharma Delhi division were complete with one quarter to go. The Nov 2024 call frames the productivity problem behind that focus push: the chronic-focused specialty division has productivity below the company average, newer specialty divisions (MD/DM/KOL-facing, launched in the last 3–4 years) run at about ₹3 lakh PCPM against ₹8–10 lakh in the legacy multi-specialty divisions carrying brands like Telmikind and Amlokind (₹400–500 crore each), and acute versus chronic cannot be carved out because divisions were launched as multi-specialty; chronic was ~28% of the mix five years ago. On BSV, management argued the acquired business is 'a totally different ball game' — super-specialty, critical care, gynec, IVF — with only 5–10% overlap, the exception being the TTK portfolio's 3–4 branded-prescription divisions that move to the Delhi side for optimisation; BSV's PCPM averaged 6.5 last year, but excluding TTK (under 3) the rest is upwards of ₹8 lakh.
verdict.evolution: Nov 05, 2024: the groundwork is diagnostic rather than structural — low-productivity chronic/specialty divisions (~₹3 lakh PCPM vs ₹8–10 lakh legacy), an admission that acute and chronic cannot be carved out of multi-specialty divisions, and BSV described as near-zero overlap except the TTK divisions to be re-homed to Delhi. Jan 2025: the method is named, with OTC as the template — 'hiving off', separate leadership for OTC versus pharma, distributor rationalisation and outside hires — and management says 80–90% of the same changes in the Delhi division are done, one quarter remaining. Then a gap in the supplied record until April 13, 2026, when the board winds up the dormant Sri Lanka WOS, and July 11, 2026, when it converts the 'focus' theme into balance-sheet action: sell Broadway for ₹49 crore as non-core, and seed a Netherlands R&D/niche-therapy SPV with up to EUR 5 million. No call passage here ever discusses the Broadway sale, the Netherlands SPV, or any demerger of a listed business.

verdict.what_is_spun: Tata Motors' commercial vehicle business — trucks, buses, vans, pick-ups — demerged into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited, now listed separately
demerged_business_names: Tata Motors Limited (formerly TML Commercial Vehicles Limited)
verdict.reason: not stated; filings only describe the outcome — CFO says demerger effective 1 October 2025 makes Tata Motors "a pure play commercial vehicle company"; no rationale given in these documents
verdict.insiders: Promoter/management stake not stated. Incentives: TML Share-based Long Term Incentive Scheme approved 11 March 2026 — up to 23,07,647 shares (0.062% dilution), PSUs at Rs 2 exercise price, replacing demerged company PSUs 1:1
verdict.hidden_value: A pure-play CV company with standalone FY26 revenue ~Rs 77,000 cr, EBITDA margin 13.2% (7.8% in FY23), EBIT 11%, FCF Rs 9,200 cr (12% of revenue), ROCE 72%, net cash Rs 7,500 cr — now levering up for Iveco (EUR 3,825,000,000 facility)
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Documents give listing dates only; no share-entitlement size, shareholder base or index inclusion/exclusion detail stated
verdict.listing_timeline: Demerger "effective from 1st of October 2025"; name changed "to Tata Motors Limited from TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (effective 29 October 2025)"; "equity shares have been listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited, effective 12th November 2025" (stated in press releases of 1 February 2026, 1 March 2026 and 1 April 2026)
verdict.read_next: The NCLT-sanctioned Composite Scheme of Arrangement — share-entitlement ratio and promoter shareholding in the resulting company
verdict.quote: Demerger being effective from 1 st of October 2025, Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company, and this is a defining shift that changes how we think is most appropriate to present our financials.

verdict.rationale: Management presents the separation as a Composite Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232, sanctioned by the NCLT Mumbai Bench amongst Tata Motors Limited (the demerged company, now Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited), TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (the resulting company) and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (amalgamated into the demerged entity), effective 1 October 2025; the resulting company was renamed Tata Motors Limited on 29 October 2025 and its shares listed on BSE/NSE (ticker TMCV) on 12 November 2025, with outstanding PSUs replaced one-for-one under a new scheme covering up to 23,07,647 shares (0.062% dilution). The stated problem the split solves is a reporting and identity one: 'Historically, we reported a CV segment. It was an internal construct that carved out CV operations from within the erstwhile combined entity. That was a practical necessity then' — from Q4 FY26 the company reports standalone financials including the Tata Cummins joint operation as its primary lens, giving 'a cleaner, more complete, and more directly comparable picture'. The separation cost ₹960 crore of one-time demerger expense booked in Q3 FY26 (part of ₹1,500 crore standalone / ₹1,600 crore consolidated exceptionals, alongside ₹603 crore of new labour code and ₹82 crore of Iveco acquisition cost). The pure-play case is argued with numbers: FY26 revenue ₹77,000 crore (vs ₹66,000 crore FY23), EBITDA margin up from 7.8% (FY23) to 13.2% (FY26) — ~550bps of 'structural improvement' — EBITDA doubled from ₹5,100 crore to ₹10,200 crore, PBT before exceptionals ₹8,700 crore, first-ever double-digit EBIT at 11% (the CV segment first crossed it at 10.6% in Q3 FY26), FCF ₹9,200 crore or 12% of revenue, Auto ROCE 72%, cash conversion cycle of negative 31 days, net cash ₹7,500 crore standalone and ₹13,700 crore consolidated, and a maiden final dividend of ₹4/share (~₹1,500 crore outflow). Cyclicality is the second problem: non-cyclical revenue (parts & service, Fleet Edge digital subscriptions, Smart City e-bus operations) is compounding at 2.7x the cyclical CAGR, 'deliberately building this mix', and Q4 working-capital sinks historically concentrated in Q4 have been spread through the year. Third, the standalone CV entity became the acquisition vehicle: its own balance sheet and a committed EUR 3.825 billion bridge from Morgan Stanley and MUFG funded an all-cash voluntary totalitarian tender offer for Iveco Group N.V. at EUR 14.10 (raised to EUR 14.40), valuing Iveco at ~EUR 3.82 billion, creating ~EUR 21 billion (INR 2,28,000 crore+) of combined revenue and ~590k units with Europe ~46%/India ~32%/South America ~8%/RoW ~14% and 'substantially no overlap' — expected to 'drive better operating leverage by spreading its capital investments over larger volumes, generating operating efficiencies and reducing the cash flow volatility inherent in the commercial vehicles sector', plus enhancing Iveco's FPT powertrain business. Structural simplification continues inside the CV entity: TMF Holdings Limited and TMF Business Services Limited (wholly owned subsidiaries) are being amalgamated into it, and Tata Motor Finance had already been folded into Tata Capital (whose October 2025 IPO priced 20–25% below the merger valuation, forcing a ₹2,000 crore mark-to-market loss in Q2 FY26 and a ₹295 crore write-back in Q3).
verdict.evolution: In the Nov 2025 call (Q2 FY26, 13 November 2025) management reported the split as done rather than argued for it — demerger effective 1 October, CV listing completed as TMCV 'as committed previously', Iveco approvals underway and the bridge loan secured. In the Feb 2026 call (Q3 FY26, 29 January 2026) the cost showed up as a ₹960 crore one-time demerger exceptional while the CV segment hit a double-digit EBIT margin (10.6%) for the first time and Iveco approvals were guided to end-March. In the May 2026 call (Q4 FY26, 13 May 2026) the framing shifted decisively: 'Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company... a defining shift', the old carved-out CV segment was retired in favour of standalone reporting, three-year pure-play metrics were laid out, and Iveco closure slipped to Q2 FY27 pending French and Spanish financial-regulator approvals. Filings then show execution: offer launched 4 September 2026, 89.42% tendered by 27 October 2026, 96.29% after the reopening on 6 November 2026, triggering the Dutch legal squeeze-out, alongside the TMF Holdings/TMF Business Services amalgamation notices.

points.point: First call of the separated entity: management confirmed the demerger took effect 1 October 2025 and that the CV business was listed as Tata Motors Limited under ticker TMCV on both exchanges, describing it as a commitment delivered.
points.quote: We successfully completed the demerger with Effective date of 1st October.

points.point: Comparatives had to be derived because the resulting company only came into existence in June 2024 — a direct consequence of the scheme structure.
points.quote: the prior period financials in this presentation, they reflect the impact of the demerger as it has just been effective since the Company’s incorporation that happened in June 2024.

points.point: The newly separated CV entity immediately tied up its own acquisition financing for Iveco through a bridge loan, with refinancing options (equity or debt) left open.
points.quote: On the Iveco acquisition, the regulatory approvals are underway and the initial funding through bridge loan has been secured.

points.point: The separation carried an explicit one-time cost of ₹960 crore, booked as an exceptional item in Q3 FY26 within ₹1,500 crore of standalone exceptionals (with ₹603 crore labour code and ₹82 crore Iveco acquisition cost).
points.quote: Demerger cost has been around ₹960 crore.

points.point: Management flagged the demerger and labour-code charges as non-recurring, separating transaction cost from underlying performance.
points.quote: And both these are going to be one-time for us. We don't expect this on a recurring basis.

points.point: The CV business crossed a double-digit EBIT margin for the first time as a standalone reporting unit — the profitability milestone used to validate the standalone case.
points.quote: The CV segment also achieved the milestone of a double-digit EBIT margin for the first time, which now stands at 10.6%.

points.point: The clearest statement of what the separation achieved: a pure-play commercial vehicle company, which management calls a defining shift that changes how the business should be presented.
points.quote: Demerger being effective from 1st of October 2025, Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company, and this is a defining shift that changes how we think is most appropriate to present our financials.

points.point: The problem the split solves, as stated: the CV business was previously visible only as an internal carve-out construct inside the combined entity.
points.quote: Historically, we reported a CV segment. It was an internal construct that carved out CV operations from within the erstwhile combined entity. That was a practical necessity then.

points.point: Post-demerger reporting switched to standalone financials including the Tata Cummins joint operation as the primary lens, for transparency and comparability.
points.quote: This gives you a cleaner, more complete, and more directly comparable picture of the business going forward.

points.point: The margin record cited as structural rather than cyclical: 7.8% to 13.2% EBITDA over three years, with EBITDA doubling from ₹5,100 crore to ₹10,200 crore and FY26 EBIT at 11%.
points.quote: EBITDA margins have expanded from 7.8% in FY23 to 13.2% in FY26. That's nearly 550 bps of structural improvement over three years.

points.point: Capital-efficiency case for the standalone entity: ₹9,200 crore FCF (12% of revenue), ₹2,800 crore reinvested, Auto ROCE of 72%, negative 31-day cash conversion cycle, net cash ₹7,500 crore standalone and ₹13,700 crore consolidated.
points.quote: Finally, the Auto ROCE stands at 72% is an industry-leading number, when EBIT doubles, capital discipline holds, returns follow.

points.point: Deliberate de-cyclicalisation of the standalone business via parts & service, Fleet Edge digital and Smart City e-buses, growing far faster than the cyclical truck business.
points.quote: Over the period, non-cyclical CAGR is running at 2.7x the cyclical CAGR. We've been deliberately building this mix, and this is now showing up meaningfully in the numbers.

points.point: Mechanics of the separation as disclosed in every filing: NCLT Mumbai-sanctioned Composite Scheme of Arrangement amongst Tata Motors Limited, TML Commercial Vehicles Limited and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited, with the resulting company renamed and listed.
points.quote: As per the Composite Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by the Hon’ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench—amongst Tata Motors Limited, TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (the Company) and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited—the Company’s name was changed to Tata Motors Limited from TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (effective 29 October 2025), and its equity shares are listed on the BSE Ltd and the NSE Ltd.

points.point: Employee incentives were carried across the split one-for-one: outstanding PSUs of the demerged company entitle holders to a matching PSU from the CV entity, implemented via a new scheme for up to 23,07,647 shares (0.062% dilution).
points.quote: the unexercised performance share units (“PSUs”) (whether vested or unvested) granted to participants under the Demerged Company’s Incentive Scheme(s) and remaining outstanding as on the record date shall entitle such participants to receive one (1) corresponding PSU to be granted by the Resulting Company under a new incentive scheme.

points.point: The separated CV entity's strategic use of its independence — the Iveco combination is justified on scale, no overlap, operating leverage and dampening CV cash-flow volatility; ~EUR 21 billion combined revenue, ~590k units, Europe 46%/India 32%.
points.quote: The new company will be able to drive better operating leverage by spreading its capital investments over larger volumes, generating operating efficiencies and reducing the cash flow volatility inherent in the commercial vehicles sector.

points.point: Iveco was pursued as an all-cash EUR 14.10 (later EUR 14.40) offer valuing Iveco at ~EUR 3.82 billion, funded by a committed EUR 3.825 billion bridge from Morgan Stanley and MUFG, with Exor (27.06% of shares, 43.19% of votes) irrevocably committed.
points.quote: TML CV HS signed a debt commitment letter with Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A., Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc. and MUFG Bank, Ltd. for fully committed bridge financing to be used in connection with the Transaction, which was subsequently implemented through a facility agreement entered into by the Offeror for an aggregate amount of up to EUR 3,825,000,000.00.

points.point: Structural simplification continued after the demerger: the CV entity is absorbing its own wholly owned financing subsidiaries TMF Holdings and TMF Business Services under a further NCLT scheme.

verdict.rationale: The separation is the demerger of the power-evacuation / substation (common infrastructure) business out of Inox Wind's listed O&M subsidiary Inox Green Energy Services Ltd (IGESL, ~56% held by IWL, later diluted to 54.78%) and its merger into Inox Renewable Solutions Ltd (IRSL, formerly Resco Global Wind Services, ~88.84% held by IWL), IWL's EPC arm, after which IRSL is automatically listed and Inox Green's shareholders receive 122 IRSL shares for every 1,000 Inox Green shares. The problem management says it fixes: Inox Green's balance sheet carried roughly Rs 1,000 crore of gross block of substations/evacuation assets (84 substations pan-India) that produced only about Rs 10 crore of revenue but around Rs 50-55 crore of annual depreciation, depressing PBT, ROE and ROCE and burying the asset-light ~50%-EBITDA-margin O&M business. Post-demerger Inox Green has virtually no depreciation and negligible finance cost, so PBT equals EBITDA equals cash profit — FY27 EBITDA guided above Rs 600 crore, 'broadly everything' converting to operating cash profit, helped by a ~Rs 700 crore accumulated-loss tax shield. The infrastructure instead lands in IRSL, where the group's EPC capability, in-housed cranes, transformer manufacturing and multi-gigawatt project/land pipeline already sit, and whose value rose after the Sept-2025 CERC amendment allowing hybridisation of existing wind evacuation with solar above 50 MW — giving access to what Devansh Jain called almost 10 GW of plug-and-play infrastructure. Akhil Jindal framed the intent as shareholder choice: investors can hold the O&M business, the infrastructure business, or the whole value chain through Inox Wind, and he said no further corporate action is therefore needed (explicitly refusing to demerge Green or IRSL out of IWL). Value-unlocking is the other stated driver: IRSL raised Rs 175 crore in Sept 2025 at a valuation of ~Rs 7,400 crore, and IWL has since sold small IRSL stakes to group parties (91.90%→88.84% for Rs 173.5 crore; then →87.98% for ~Rs 50 crore). Investors and analysts (Vishal Singh, Pradyumna Choudhary, Hansal Thakker, Prit Nagersheth, Pradeep Motwani) repeatedly pressed on timing and on whether minority shareholders would see value unlocked; the scheme also required and received approval from equity shareholders, warrant holders and secured and unsecured creditors (1 Nov 2025) — no lender or partner demand was cited as the trigger.
verdict.evolution: IGESL's board approved the scheme on 13 Nov 2024; the earliest discussion in these transcripts is the Feb 2025 call (31 Jan 2025), where Manish Garg confirmed board approval and filing with NSE/BSE after an investor asked when 'the demerger of that EPC subsidiary' would happen. By the Sep 2025 call (1 Sep 2025) exchange no-objections were in, the scheme was filed at NCLT Ahmedabad with approval guided in 2-3 quarters, IRSL had raised Rs 175 crore at ~Rs 7,400 crore, and Akhil Jindal reframed the logic as giving shareholders a choice of which business to own while ruling out any further demerger out of IWL. On the Nov 2025 call (14 Nov 2025) shareholder and creditor approvals were announced and Devansh Jain said the demerger and IRSL listing would 'unlock substantial value'; on the Feb 2026 call (13 Feb 2026) it was in final NCLT hearings with the impact quantified (only ~Rs 10 crore revenue out, ~Rs 50 crore depreciation out, 84 substations to be merged). NCLT sanctioned it on 12 March 2026, effective 4 May 2026, and on the Jun 2026 call (29 May 2026) management confirmed the Rs 1,000 crore gross block and Rs 50-55 crore depreciation were eliminated, with listing 1-2 months away, while declining to give IRSL's financials until it is demerged.

points.point: First disclosure in these calls: the IGESL board had approved demerging the substation business and the scheme was filed with NSE/BSE, to be followed by an NCLT filing; an investor had asked when the 'EPC subsidiary' demerger would happen.
points.quote: So the Board approval for a demerger of the substation business from Inox Green has already been taken in the last Board meeting, the scheme has been filed with NSE and BSE, and we are waiting for their approval.

points.point: Akhil Jindal explained the mechanics — infrastructure and connectivity assets move out of Inox Green into Resco/IRSL, which then lists automatically, with Inox Green shareholders receiving IRSL shares.
points.quote: Under that, there would have been an automatic listing of Resco. And to that extent, the shareholders of INOX Green would be getting the shares of INOX Resco also.

points.point: Asked whether IGESL and IRSL would later be demerged to IWL shareholders, Jindal said the point of separating these businesses was to let shareholders pick which business to own, so no further corporate action is needed.
points.quote: As management, we have provided enough window for a shareholder to be present where he wants to be. And I think that was the intention of separating these businesses.

points.point: The balance-sheet rationale quantified: ~Rs 1,000 crore gross block leaves Inox Green and ~Rs 50-55 crore of annual depreciation is eliminated, lifting PBT and improving ROE/ROCE.
points.quote: Once the scheme is approved by the NCLT, the gross block of around INR1,000 crores will be off our balance sheet and subsequently the depreciation of approximately INR50 crores to INR55 crores annually will be eliminated, thereby increasing the PBT by that amount.

points.point: IRSL was independently valued shortly before the demerger, and the CERC hybridisation amendment (allowing existing wind evacuation infra to be shared with solar above 50 MW) multiplied the value of the infrastructure being moved into it.
points.quote: We have recently raised INR175 crores at Inox Renewable Solutions at a valuation of approximately INR7,400 crores.

points.point: Devansh Jain sized the infrastructure asset that IRSL will house post-hybridisation as near-unique in India.
points.quote: I think it gives us access to almost 10 gigawatts of plug and play infrastructure across wind and solar , which is huge.

points.point: On receiving shareholder and creditor approvals, Sanjeev Agarwal set out the two-sided benefit: IRSL lists as Inox Wind's EPC arm, Inox Green sheds the depreciation on the demerged asset blocks.
points.quote: This will add value for both Inox Wind, with subsequent listing of Inox Renewable solution as an EPC arm of Inox Wind, and Inox Green with elimination of depreciation on demergers of the asset blocks

points.point: Devansh Jain stated the headline objective as value unlocking for both listed entities.
points.quote: I believe that the de-merger and subsequent listing of Inox Renewable Solutions will unlock substantial value for both Inox Wind and Inox Green.

points.point: Management quantified the asymmetry that makes the separation accretive for Inox Green: barely any revenue leaves, but the depreciation does.
points.quote: So post the demerger, as we have clarified on the multiple cores, there would be a very limited amount of revenue in the range of INR 10 odd crore will get out of the balance sheet. And around INR 50 odd crores of depreciation will go out from the balance sheet.

points.point: Mathusudhana described the scale of the infrastructure being consolidated — 84 substations pan-India — and claimed further unquantified synergy value plus a connectivity advantage no competitor has.
points.quote: And like merging 84 substations across India, it will be a huge exercise. And that will unlock synergy value, which we will reveal in the future.

points.point: Post-NCLT confirmation that the benefit has crystallised in Inox Green's accounts, with the residual step being administrative before IRSL's automatic listing (guided at 1-2 months).
points.quote: With this gross block of approximately INR1,000 crores has been eliminated from Inox Green's balance sheet. And subsequently, the annual depreciation of approximately INR50 crores to INR55 crores has been eliminated, thereby increasing the profitability.

points.point: Devansh Jain placed the IRSL demerger in a sequence of value-creating separations, after the Inox Green spin-off, while shrugging off the share-price criticism from minority holders.
points.quote: We've spun off Inox Green, which has created tremendous value. We're on the verge of demerging Inox Renewable Solutions, which we hope will create tremendous value.

points.point: Management refused to give any top-line or EBITDA profile for the business being separated until the demerger is complete.
points.quote: We cannot say at this point in time. I think once that demerged, we'll elucidate more plans. At this point in time, it's part and parcel of Inox Wind.

points.point: Post-demerger Inox Green is positioned as a near-pure cash generator: no depreciation, no finance cost and a ~Rs 700 crore loss tax shield, with FY27 EBITDA guided above Rs 600 crore.
points.quote: Out of INR600 crore fees, broadly everything will be converted into the operating cash flow. As such, there will be no depreciation, no finance cost, and we have a tax shield up to INR700 crore of losses.

points.point: The filings record the legal path: IGESL board approval 13 Nov 2024 for demerger of the Power Evacuation business into IRSL under sections 230-232; approval by equity shareholders, warrant holders and secured and unsecured creditors on 1 Nov 2025; NCLT Ahmedabad sanction on 12 March 2026; effective 4 May 2026.
points.quote: On March, 12, 2026, Hon'ble National Company law Tribunal, Ahmedabad (NCLT) sanctioned the Scheme.

points.point: Consideration mechanics and the dilution of IWL's stake in the resulting company are specified in the filings.
points.quote: Pursuant to the Scheme, 122 equity share in the Resulting company for every 1000 share held in the demerged company to be issued to the shareholders as on the record date.

points.point: The demerger itself reduces Inox Wind's holding in IRSL, though control is retained under Ind AS 110.
points.quote: Furhter, due to effect of the demerger scheme between the lnox Renewable Solutions Limited and lnox Green Energy Services Limited as approved by NCLT vide order dated 13 March 2026, the Company shareholding in IRSL is expected to reduced from 88.41% to 79.75%.

verdict.what_management_expects: Inox Green: ~Rs 1,000 cr gross block and ~Rs 50-55 cr annual depreciation gone, higher PBT, sharply better ROE/ROCE, a pure-play ~50%-margin asset-light O&M business whose FY27 EBITDA (>Rs 600 cr) converts almost fully to cash. IRSL: a separately listed EPC/infrastructure arm of Inox Wind holding evacuation infra, cranes, transformers and hybridisation-ready plug-and-play sites. Both: substantial value unlocking.
verdict.gaps: No IRSL standalone revenue, EBITDA, debt or valuation basis disclosed; no explanation of the 122:1,000 share ratio, tax treatment, IRSL's post-listing capital needs, or any lender requirement.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is SBI Funds Management Limited (SBIFM) — SBI Mutual Fund, the bank's asset-management joint venture with Amundi — which SBI is partially separating by listing it, not by demerging it; management repeatedly framed the purpose as "value unlocking" and, in Chairman C.S. Setty's words, "more importantly, value recognition for the industry" (Nov 2025), with SBI General Insurance named alongside AMC as the other listing candidate. The driver management gave was that SBI's own stock does not reflect the conglomerate's worth: Setty called SBI's valuation "a conundrum, considering our return on equity and growth metrics" (Nov 2025, with ROE 19.7%–20.68% and ROA >1% through FY26), and the same theme runs through the hidden-value argument on strategic holdings — of the group's ~7.3% NSE stake he said "the moment NSE gets listed, the whole shareholding by SBI will be available as reserve to us to mark to market" (May 2026). Explicitly NOT a capital-need story at first: in Nov 2025 Setty said "these two companies do not require capital at this juncture. Neither the parent requires because we just raised Rs. 25,000 crores" (the July 2025 QIP, India's largest, 4.5x oversubscribed on a >Rs. 1.1 trillion book, >60% cross-border), which is why timing was left to "respective boards"; by May 2026 the rationale had hardened into a capital one — the listing "will result in capital augmentation, CET-1" on top of CAR already up 115bps to 15.4%. The structure confirms it is monetisation, not a fix for the business: the IPO is a pure offer for sale (no fresh issue), SBI offering 6.3007% and JV partner Amundi India Holding 3.7006%, total up to 10.0013% / 203,709,239 shares at Rs. 1 face value, so no money reaches SBIFM itself. Management stressed that separation does not break the franchise link — SBIFM stays the country's largest AMC inside the "One SBI" cross-sell engine (a special dividend of ~Rs. 2,200 crore came up to the bank in Q3FY26, cross-sell/CVE income targeted at $1 billion, YONO "deep integration with subsidiary production"), and Setty was explicit that "Mutual fund, we are not fully exiting. So we still have potential to monetize further when market improves" (Feb 2026). The push came from the sell side and retail investors — Sushil Choksey (Indus Equity), Manoj Alimchandani and Kunal Shah (Citigroup) raised monetisation/value-unlocking on four of the five calls, Alimchandani even arguing in Feb 2026 that delaying the IPO five years could fetch three times the market cap — rather than from lenders or regulators; the only regulator-linked nudge cited was the SEBI chairman on NSE's listing. No problem with SBIFM's performance was ever offered as a reason: it was described only as "the largest AMC in the country," contributing Rs. 4,969.09 crore of FY26 total income, just 0.70% of group income.
verdict.evolution: May 2025 had no separation plan at all — only "we will continue to nurture these subsidiaries," while the bank instead took an enabling resolution for Rs. 25,000 crore of its own equity. By Aug 2025 Setty conceded "a couple of candidates for listing, but… there is no sense of urgency," and in Nov 2025 he named them — SBI AMC and SBI General — as the right candidates for "value unlocking" and "value recognition," with boards to set timing; the SBIFM stake-sale approval for 6.3007% followed on 6 Nov 2025 and the DRHP on 19 Mar 2026 (share count restated to 128,334,397 after a bonus issue and ESOP exercises). Feb 2026 added the retained-upside caveat ("we are not fully exiting") and May 2026 re-cast the deal as CET-1 capital augmentation to be completed within FY27. The plan then changed in execution in July 2026: a pre-IPO placement of 28,832,748 shares (1.4156%) to 30 investors at Rs. 574 for Rs. 1,655 crore on 9–10 July cut SBI's offer-for-sale from 6.3007% to 4.8851% (total offer 8.3933%), priced at Rs. 574 with allotment expected 18 July 2026.

points.point: No separation on the table: subsidiaries framed purely as value creators to be retained, while the bank instead took an enabling resolution to raise Rs. 25,000 crore of its own equity.
points.quote: Our subsidiaries are consistently performing well and continue to create significant value for all the stakeholders. We will continue to nurture these subsidiaries and maintain leadership position in the respective businesses.

points.point: First acknowledgement of listing candidates, asked for by Sushil Choksey (Indus Equity Advisors); Setty explicitly de-prioritised it because the Rs. 25,000 crore QIP had just closed.
points.quote: No, as we mentioned that we definitely have a couple of candidates for listing, but the timing is not very… there is no sense of urgency there, I believe.

points.point: The rationale stated in full for the first time, in answer to Choksey on the group's underperforming consolidated value: SBI AMC and SBI General named, with value unlocking and industry recognition of value as the purpose.
points.quote: But among these four major subsidiaries, we definitely would be looking at, as I mentioned several times, SBI AMC and SBI General are right candidates for listing in our stable. It also provides some value unlocking and, more importantly, value recognition for the industry.

points.point: Answering Kunal Shah (Citigroup) on what would trigger the decision, Setty ruled capital need out as a motive for either the subsidiaries or the parent, leaving timing and quantum to the subsidiary boards.
points.quote: I think we need to just look at, see, one is, as I mentioned earlier also, that these two companies do not require capital at this juncture.

points.point: The underlying grievance the separation is meant to address — SBI's own market valuation not tracking its ROE and growth — stated in the Chairman's opening remarks; Ashok Ajmera had quantified it as a Rs. 8.82 lakh crore market cap on Rs. 100 trillion of business versus Rs. 15.14 lakh crore for a Rs. 57 trillion peer.
points.quote: Although the current valuations of SBI are a conundrum, considering our return on equity and growth metrics, we are confident that they will eventually align with our fundamental and operational metrics, the institutionalized nature of our business and our market leadership in the coming years.

points.point: Retained-stake logic: asked by Manoj Alimchandani whether delaying the IPO five years could treble the market cap, Setty defended a partial sale that keeps future upside with SBI.
points.quote: Mutual fund, we are not fully exiting. So we still have potential to monetize further when market improves.

points.point: Why the AMC is worth separating while staying attached: it is already the country's largest AMC, upstreamed a Rs. 2,200 crore special dividend into SBI's Q3FY26 profit, and feeds a cross-sell income stream management targets at $1 billion.
points.quote: If I have to talk about one-off, I think the one item which is a special dividend we have received, around Rs. 2,200 crores from SBI Mutual Fund.

points.point: The rationale shifts to capital: with the AMC listing under way, Setty tied it to CET-1 augmentation supporting credit growth (the bank could already fund ~Rs. 12 trillion of growth, CAR 15.4%, up 115bps YoY).
points.quote: We are also seriously, as you are aware, we have embarked on listing SBI AMC and hopefully in this financial year we will be able to complete, which will result in capital augmentation, CET-1.

points.point: Same hidden-value argument applied to the group's ~7.3% NSE holding, which is not marked to market today — listing is the mechanism that converts unrecognised strategic stakes into reported reserves.
points.quote: But as you mentioned, I think the moment NSE gets listed, the whole shareholding by SBI will be available as reserve to us to mark to market.

points.point: 6 Nov 2025 board approval, restated in the 19 Mar 2026 DRHP filing: a pure offer for sale of up to 10.0013% (203,709,239 shares of Rs. 1 each) — SBI 6.3007% (128,334,397 shares) and JV partner Amundi India Holding 3.7006% (75,374,842 shares). No fresh issue, so no proceeds go to SBIFM.
points.quote: The IPO comprises an offer for sale of up to 128,334,397 Equity Shares (amounting to 6.3007% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFML) by State Bank of India, and of up to 75,374,842 Equity Shares (amounting to 3.7006% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFML) by Amundi India Holding.

points.point: Plan changed in execution: a pre-IPO secondary placement on 9–10 July 2026 moved 1.4156% of pre-offer capital to 30 investors at the eventual Rs. 574 offer price, raising Rs. 1,655 crore for SBI ahead of the book build.
points.quote: State Bank of India had entered into share purchase agreements each dated July 9, 2026 to sell, in aggregate, 2,88,32,748 equity shares of SBIFM of face value Rs. 1 (one) each ("Equity Shares"), being equivalent to 1.4156% of pre-Offer share capital of SBIFM, to a total of 30 (thirty) investors at Rs. 574.00 per Equity Share, for an aggregate consideration of Rs. 1,655.00 crores.

points.point: The 11 July 2026 addendum cut SBI's offer-for-sale by exactly the pre-IPO quantum, to 4.8851% (total offer 8.3933%); the offer was priced at Rs. 574 on 16 July with a Rs. 54 employee discount and allotment expected on or about 18 July 2026.
points.quote: The size of the offer for sale by the State Bank of India in the IPO has been revised from up to 128,334,397 Equity Shares (amounting to 6.3007% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFM) to up to 99,501,649 Equity Shares (amounting to 4.8851% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFM).

points.point: Materiality disclosed for the separated business: SBIFM's FY2026 total income of Rs. 4,969.09 crore is 0.70% of group income and its reserves 0.59% of group reserves — the separation is about price discovery, not size.
points.quote: Total income: Rs. 4,969.09 crores (0.70% of Total Income of SBI Group)

verdict.what_management_expects: For SBIFM: a listed market price that recognises India's largest AMC, with SBI retaining control, banca distribution and future monetisation upside. For SBI: value unlocking and "value recognition," CET-1 capital augmentation supporting 13-15% credit growth, hidden reserves surfaced (as with NSE), and valuation converging on >1% ROA and 15%+ through-cycle ROE. No margin or focus benefit was claimed.
verdict.gaps: No valuation target, expected proceeds, CET-1 basis points, or use of funds; no reason the offer was trimmed; Amundi's motive, SBI General's timeline, and post-listing distribution/royalty terms unexplained.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is Swara Baby Products Limited, Brainbees' diaper/hygiene manufacturing subsidiary, which filed a DRHP on July 02, 2026 for an IPO of up to Rs 10,000 million (Rs 5,000 million fresh issue plus Rs 5,000 million offer for sale), with Brainbees itself selling up to Rs 3,000 million in the OFS (board approval July 01, 2026). Management's stated reason is drift in purpose: Brainbees invested Rs 906.17 million in 2020 for 53.45% (fully diluted) purely as backward integration — "to scale up our home brands within diaper category" with "more control on quality at scale, production timelines and continued innovation in diaper manufacturing" — but Swara then became the largest contract manufacturer by value in Fiscal 2025 in Indian hygiene manufacturing, adding adult diapers and sanitary napkins (similar absorbent raw materials and processes), third-party and multinational customers, and exports via a US subsidiary (Swara Corp, incorporated 08 December 2025). Brainbees' share of Swara's revenue fell from 27.03% in FY24 to 22.64% in FY26, so management says Swara "has charted a very different long term vision as compared to the original alignment with Brainbees," with "different capex and working capital needs" it should "bridge their own capital requirement" rather than draw on Brainbees' cash. On selling into the OFS despite holding cash, management argued "holding cash and holding an investment are two different capital allocation decisions" and that partial monetisation lets it "crystallize value, improve return on investment and maintain flexibility for future strategic opportunities." Control and commercials are explicitly unchanged: Brainbees stays Promoter at 76.59% (raised from 75.92% in a December 2025 swap that moved Solis Hygiene under Swara to put the hygiene vertical "under a single roof"), Swara remains a subsidiary, Brainbees' management has no involvement in running it (Alok Birla and Udit Birla lead; Supam Maheshwari and Gautam Sharma sit as non-executive directors), and "terms of trade" stay at arm's length with "no impact either on supply chain or pricing." Swara contributed Rs 11,639 million revenue in FY26 (Rs 9,004.39 million after eliminating Rs 2,634.61 million of inter-company sales) and Rs 1,445.7 million of adjusted EBITDA into the India multi-channel segment. No lender, partner or investor is named as having demanded it; analysts had only pushed on a separate asset, GlobalBees, where Supam said in August 2025 that "the most probable outcome for Globalbees... will be listing" given its separate board, management and investors (Premji, Lightspeed, Chiratae).
verdict.evolution: The idea first surfaced as an analyst question about a different unit: on the Aug 2025 call (Aug 13, 2025) Sachin Dixit asked whether FirstCry investors could expect liquidity from GlobalBees "getting demerged, having its own IPO," and Supam said listing was the most probable outcome over a few years; on the Feb 2026 call (Feb 13, 2026) Ajay Agarwal asked for GlobalBees listing timelines and got no answer. Meanwhile the hygiene business was quietly being tidied for separation — a December 26, 2025 intra-group restructuring put Solis Hygiene under Swara Baby to bring the whole hygiene vertical under one roof, lifting Brainbees' Swara stake to 76.59%. Neither the Feb 2026 nor the Jun 2026 call (May 26, 2026) mentioned Swara or any separation at all; on Jun 2026 Supam even said buybacks and similar capital actions had not been discussed internally or at board level. The plan then appeared fully formed in filings only — board approval of OFS participation on July 01, 2026, DRHP plus a management Q&A on July 02, 2026 — followed by a related narrowing at GlobalBees, whose non-core brand rationalisation culminated in the October 07, 2026 sale of its entire 51.54% in Mush Textile.

points.point: Asked by JM Financial's Sachin Dixit whether FirstCry shareholders could get liquidity from GlobalBees being demerged or separately IPO'd, Supam framed listing as the likely eventual route and Brainbees' monetisation path over a few years.
points.quote: Having said this, the most probable outcome for Globalbees as an outcome will be listing, which company and its shareholders will decide over a period of time, is when Brainbees also will find a monetization opportunity over a period of a few years.

points.point: The structural argument for separability given for GlobalBees was that it already runs independently of Brainbees, with its own CEO, board and outside shareholders including Premji, Lightspeed and Chiratae.
points.quote: The company has a separate management team, which is run separately and also it has its separate board, and also it has a separate set of investors as well, apart from Brainbees as well, which includes Premji, Lightspeed, and Chiratae, and so on and so forth.

points.point: Garima Mishra pressed on the CCPS infusion into GlobalBees; Gautam said it funded working capital, and that all three investor-directors who had stepped off the GlobalBees board participated in that round — the capital-need theme that later justifies Swara funding itself.
points.quote: This is largely for taking care of their working capital requirement, Garima

points.point: Ajay Agarwal again asked directly for a GlobalBees listing timeline; the reply covered only Flipkart's revenue-recognition impact and GlobalBees' EBITDA growth (c.150% YoY in Q3, c.50% in 9M), with no timeline given.
points.quote: And again on Globalbees, any plans on listing of Globalbees? Can you share the tentative timelines or any sense on the same?

points.point: Five weeks before the Swara DRHP, asked about the low valuation, takeover risk and buybacks, Supam said no such capital action had been discussed internally or by the board — and said nothing about any separation.
points.quote: Yes, we have sufficient cash on the company, but we haven't discussed any of these buybacks and stuff like that so far, in our internal discussions or even board discussions.

points.point: The July 02, 2026 DRHP filing states the original purpose of the 2020 Rs 906.17 million investment for 53.45%: backward integration to scale FirstCry's own diaper home brands with control over quality, timelines and innovation.
points.quote: We wanted to scale up our home brands within diaper category and wanted to do backward integration to get more control on quality at scale, production timelines and continued innovation in diaper manufacturing.

points.point: Core rationale: Swara outgrew the FirstCry ecosystem — multiple third-party and multinational customers, adult diapers and feminine hygiene, exports and a US subsidiary, with Brainbees' share of its revenue down from 27.03% (FY24) to 22.64% (FY26).
points.quote: With Swara Baby's diversification across product lines, more channels, expansion into International geographies, the business has charted a very different long term vision as compared to the original alignment with Brainbees.

points.point: Why not just fund Swara off Brainbees' balance sheet: its capex and working-capital profile differs, so it should raise its own money while Brainbees keeps supply and arm's-length pricing unchanged.
points.quote: With this expansive and global vision in contract manufacturing of disposable hygiene products with different capex and working capital needs, we decided to initiate the process of separately listing this business so that they can follow their independent journey and bridge their own capital requirement.

points.point: Why Brainbees sells up to Rs 3,000 million into the OFS despite ample cash: capital-allocation discipline and value crystallisation, while Swara stays a 76.59% subsidiary and Brainbees' management stays out of its operations.
points.quote: Partial monetization of a successful investment allows us to crystallize value, improve return on investment and maintain flexibility for future strategic opportunities.

points.point: Preparatory step on December 26, 2025: Swara Baby acquired 100% of Solis Hygiene (FY25 turnover Rs 240.73 crore, 3% of consolidated), with Brainbees swapping its 79.34% Solis stake for 56,26,738 Swara shares, lifting its Swara holding from 75.92% to 76.59%.
points.quote: In order to bring the complete Hygiene vertical under a single roof, the restructuring is being done.

points.point: The parallel pruning at GlobalBees: on October 07, 2026 it signed an MOU to sell its entire 51.54% in Mush Textile (brands Mush and BePlush, Rs 11.34 crore or 0.13% of FY26 turnover) for Rs 5,68,93,940 to Nihar Gosalia and Vaishvik Brahmbhatt.
points.quote: Upon completion of the aforesaid transaction, Mush will cease to be a Subsidiary of GlobalBees and, accordingly, will also cease to be a Step-down Subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: The GlobalBees brand-rationalisation logic that frames the Mush exit: loss-making, slow-growing non-core brands were being exited, with core categories at 30% growth and 4.9% adjusted EBITDA versus 2% consolidated.
points.quote: As you're aware, over the last few quarters, we've been speaking about rationalizing certain brands because they were delivering a relatively lower revenue growth as well as incurring losses.

verdict.what_management_expects: Swara funds its own capex/working capital from the Rs 5,000 million fresh issue and pursues an independent global contract-manufacturing path; Brainbees crystallizes value, improves ROI and gains flexibility via up to Rs 3,000 million OFS cash, while keeping 76.59% control, Promoter status, consolidation of Swara's Rs 9,004 million revenue and Rs 1,445.7 million adjusted EBITDA, and unchanged arm's-length supply and pricing.
verdict.gaps: No earnings call ever mentions the Swara IPO, its valuation, or use of OFS proceeds; GlobalBees listing timeline never answered; Mush sale pricing and loss unexplained.

verdict.segment_name: Swara Baby Products Limited / Solis Hygiene Private Limited (hygiene vertical) — not a reported segment; the documents disclose it only as a subsidiary, with its operations subsumed in the 'India multi-channel' segment
verdict.measure_notes: No profit or revenue line of any kind is disclosed for Swara Baby / the hygiene vertical on these pages. The only segment profit measures shown are 'Segment Results before depreciation and amortisation expense' (labelled Adjusted EBITDA in the presentations) and 'Segment Results' (segment EBIT-type figure, before finance cost, ESOP expense and other income), reported for four reportable segments only — India multi-channel, International, Globalbees, Others — with revenue from operations shown gross of inter-company items and a separate 'Inter Company Adjustments' column. Swara Baby and Solis Hygiene appear solely in the list of significant investments in subsidiaries (Swara Baby Products Private Limited 86.01% at 31-Mar-2024, 87.30% at 31-Mar-2025; Swara Baby Products Limited 76.59% at 31-Mar-2026; Solis Hygiene Private Limited 79.34% at 31-Mar-2024 and 31-Mar-2025, 0.00% at 31-Mar-2026) — AR2025 p.210 and AR2026 p.216 — with no financial figures attached.

years.source: Annual Report 2025 — page 210 (subsidiary holding only, no financials)
Annual Report 2026 — page 216 (subsidiary holding only, no financials)
Annual Report 2026 — page 216 (subsidiary holding only, no financials)

verdict.not_found: All of them: no revenue, EBITDA/segment result or PAT for Swara Baby/Solis Hygiene. Pages carry only the four reportable segments and subsidiary shareholding percentages; no standalone or quarterly hygiene-vertical figures.

verdict.segment_name: SBI Funds Management Limited (SBIFML / SBI Mutual Fund) — disclosed as a subsidiary, not a reportable segment
verdict.measure_notes: Only subsidiary-level PAT is disclosed, in the 'SBI and its subsidiaries – leveraging synergies' slides: PAT as per Ind AS, without OCI (ROE recomputed on average networth). No revenue, EBITDA, EBIT or PBT line for SBIFML anywhere on these pages. In the annual-report segment tables SBIFML is not a separate segment — it falls inside consolidated 'Other Banking Operations' (FY2026 revenue ₹34,821.89 cr, result ₹10,027.19 cr; FY2025 ₹31,108.69 cr / ₹8,376.83 cr), which also contains all other non-insurance subsidiaries, so those figures are not SBIFML's own.

verdict.what_is_spun: Nothing is spun off — listed subsidiary Shiva Cement is amalgamated into parent JSW Cement
verdict.reason: Create a single unified cement platform unlocking operational, financial and management synergies; backward integration of clinker, cheaper funding, simplified structure, and greater liquidity for Shiva's public shareholders.
verdict.insiders: JSW Cement holds 66.23% of Shiva's equity and all its OCCRPS; promoter group of JSW Cement goes 72.02% to 71.39% post-merger; no consideration/benefit to promoters stated.
verdict.hidden_value: Shiva's 1.32 mtpa Sundargarh clinker unit plus FY26-commissioned 1.0 MTPA Sambalpur grinding unit come in with negative net worth (INR -30.08 crore) and INR 133.92 crore accumulated losses written off against securities premium.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Only 1.21 crore new shares on 137.55 crore base (~0.9%); same industry, same promoter, larger and more liquid entity.
verdict.listing_timeline: No new listing; Shiva Cement "shall cease to exist upon effectiveness of the Scheme without being wound up" and the transaction "is expected to be completed within 12-14 months" (said September 29, 2026 and repeated October 27, 2026)
verdict.read_next: The Regulation 37 Scheme filing with the valuation report and fairness opinions behind the 5:41 share exchange ratio.
verdict.quote: This consolidation creates a single unified cement platform to unlock operational, financial, and management synergies.
